theorem_title: Descending modular subtraction computes the remainder
formal_statement:
theorem Light.Emod.reduce_ends : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {d : Nat} {μ : Nat → Int} {x : Int} {Mo V fr a : Nat}
  (F : Light.Emod.Pre lim Mo V fr) (haV : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat a V) {μ' : Nat → Int} {t : Int}
  (tab : Light.Emod.Table μ μ' Mo fr (Light.emodRounds a Mo)),
  Light.Ends lim P d Light.emodReduce
    {
      loc :=
        Light.frame
          (@List.cons.{0} Int x
            (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt Mo)
              (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt fr)
                (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt a)
                  (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (Light.emodRounds a Mo))
                    (@List.cons.{0} Int t (@List.nil.{0} Int))))))),
      mem := μ' }
    (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
      (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 24) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 24))) (Light.emodRounds a Mo))
      (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 4) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 4))))
    fun (σ' : Light.State) =>
    @Eq.{1} Light.State σ'
      {
        loc :=
          Light.frame
            (@List.cons.{0} Int x
              (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt Mo)
                (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt fr)
                  (@List.cons.{0} Int
                    (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt
                      (@HMod.hMod.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMod.{0} Nat Nat.instMod) a Mo))
                    (@List.cons.{0} Int (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0)))
                      (@List.cons.{0} Int t (@List.nil.{0} Int))))))),
        mem := μ' } := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Fix resource limits with memory bound $S$ and word-magnitude bound $W$, a program, and a call depth. Let $M,V,f,a\in\mathbb N$, with $M\ge1$, $a\le V$, $S\le W$, $4V+4M+16\le W$, and $f+\log_2^{\mathrm{nat}}(V+1)+2\le S$. Put $K=\operatorname{bits}(a\mathbin{/}M)$, with $\operatorname{bits}(0)=0$. Suppose memory $\nu$ stores $M2^j$ at $f+j$ for $j<K$ and agrees with a reference memory below $f$. For arbitrary integers $x,t$, the reduction loop has the state transition

$$([x,M,f,a,K,t],\nu)\longrightarrow([x,M,f,a\bmod M,0,t],\nu)$$

within $24K+4$ steps. This verifies the read-only subtraction phase of the remainder routine.

theorem_title: Sign correction gives the Euclidean remainder of an integer
formal_statement:
theorem Light.Emod.sign_ends : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {d : Nat} {x : Int} {Mo V fr a : Nat} (F : Light.Emod.Pre lim Mo V fr)
  (hax : @Eq.{1} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt a) (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup x))
  {μ' : Nat → Int} {t : Int},
  Light.Ends lim P d Light.emodSign
    {
      loc :=
        Light.frame
          (@List.cons.{0} Int x
            (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt Mo)
              (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt fr)
                (@List.cons.{0} Int
                  (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt
                    (@HMod.hMod.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMod.{0} Nat Nat.instMod) a Mo))
                  (@List.cons.{0} Int (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0)))
                    (@List.cons.{0} Int t (@List.nil.{0} Int))))))),
      mem := μ' }
    (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 12) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 12))) fun (σ' : Light.State) =>
    And
      (@Eq.{1} Int (σ'.loc (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))))
        (@HMod.hMod.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHMod.{0} Int Int.instMod) x (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt Mo)))
      (@Eq.{1} (Nat → Int) σ'.mem μ') := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Fix resource limits with memory bound $S$ and word-magnitude bound $W$, a program, and a call depth. Let $M,V,f\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $M\ge1$, $S\le W$, $4V+4M+16\le W$, and $f+\log_2^{\mathrm{nat}}(V+1)+2\le S$. Let $x,t\in\mathbb Z$, let $a\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $a=|x|$, and let $\nu$ be any memory. Starting from register vector $[x,M,f,a\bmod M,0,t]$, the sign-correction block finishes within $12$ steps with

$$\operatorname{register}_0=x\bmod M,\qquad\operatorname{memory}=\nu.$$

The remainder is Euclidean and nonnegative. This final phase converts the absolute-value remainder to the signed-input result; the theorem does not require $a\le V$.

theorem_title: Building the doubled-modulus table
formal_statement:
theorem Light.Emod.table_ends : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {d : Nat} {μ : Nat → Int} {x : Int} {Mo V fr a : Nat}
  (F : Light.Emod.Pre lim Mo V fr) (haV : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat a V),
  Light.Ends lim P d Light.emodTable
    {
      loc :=
        Light.frame
          (@List.cons.{0} Int x
            (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt Mo)
              (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt fr)
                (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt a)
                  (@List.cons.{0} Int (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0)))
                    (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt Mo) (@List.nil.{0} Int))))))),
      mem := μ }
    (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
      (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 19) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 19))) (Light.emodRounds a Mo))
      (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 6) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 6))))
    fun (σ' : Light.State) =>
    ∃ (μ' : Nat → Int),
      And
        (@Eq.{1} Light.State σ'
          {
            loc :=
              Light.frame
                (@List.cons.{0} Int x
                  (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt Mo)
                    (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt fr)
                      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt a)
                        (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (Light.emodRounds a Mo))
                          (@List.cons.{0} Int
                            (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt
                              (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) Mo
                                (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
                                  (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat
                                    (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid)))
                                  (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2)))
                                  (Light.emodRounds a Mo))))
                            (@List.nil.{0} Int))))))),
            mem := μ' })
        (Light.Emod.Table μ μ' Mo fr (Light.emodRounds a Mo)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Fix resource limits with memory bound $S$ and word-magnitude bound $W$, a program, and a call depth. Let $M,V,f,a\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $M\ge1$, $a\le V$, $S\le W$, $4V+4M+16\le W$, and $f+\log_2^{\mathrm{nat}}(V+1)+2\le S$. Put $K=\operatorname{bits}(a\mathbin{/}M)$, with zero bit length for zero. For any integer $x$ and initial memory $\mu$, the table-building loop finishes within $19K+6$ steps with register vector

$$[x,M,f,a,K,M2^K].$$

Its final memory $\nu$ satisfies $\nu(f+j)=M2^j$ for every $j<K$ and $\nu(q)=\mu(q)$ for every $q<f$. This constructs the exact doubling table consumed by modular subtraction.

theorem_title: A counting-loop rule with a constant body budget
formal_statement:
theorem Light.Ends.for {σ : State} {i : ℕ} {hi : Expr} {body : Stmt} {T : ℕ} {Q : State → Prop}
    (I : ℕ → State → Prop) (n b : ℕ)
    (start : I 0 { σ with loc := Function.update σ.loc i 0 })
    (round : ∀ (j : ℕ) (σ : State), j < n → σ.loc i = j → I j σ → Ends lim P d body σ b fun σ' =>
      σ'.loc i = j ∧ I (j + 1) { σ' with loc := Function.update σ'.loc i ((j : ℤ) + 1) })
    (done : ∀ σ : State, σ.loc i = n → I n σ → Q σ)
    (bound : ∀ (j : ℕ) (σ : State), j ≤ n → σ.loc i = j → I j σ → hi.Safe lim σ ∧ hi.val σ = n)
    (hn : (n : ℤ) ≤ lim.word := by omega)
    (hT : n * (hi.cost + b + 7) + hi.cost + 5 ≤ T := by first
                                                          |
                                                            ((simp only [Light.Stmt.blockCost, Light.Cond.cost, Light.Expr.cost,
                                                                  List.map_cons, List.map_nil, List.sum_cons, List.sum_nil, ]);
                                                              (first
                                                                | omega
                                                                | ((ring_nf); (omega))))
                                                          | omega
                                                          |
                                                            (simp [] <;>
                                                                first
                                                                | omega
                                                                | ((ring_nf); (omega)))) :
    Ends lim P d (Stmt.for i hi body) σ T Q := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Fix a program, resource limits, and a call depth. Consider a loop whose counter register $i$ starts at zero, whose upper-bound expression $e$ has fixed value $n$, and whose body costs at most $b$ per iteration. Let $I_j$ be state predicates. Assume initialization establishes $I_0$; every body execution at counter $j<n$ preserves that counter and establishes $I_{j+1}$ after incrementing it; and counter $n$ with $I_n$ implies the postcondition $Q$. Also assume $e$ is safe and equals $n$ in every invariant state with $j\le n$, and $n$ fits in a word. If

$$n\bigl(\operatorname{cost}(e)+b+7\bigr)+\operatorname{cost}(e)+5\le T,$$

the counting loop terminates within $T$ steps with $Q$. This rule includes initialization, increments, and all guard evaluations.

theorem_title: Safe blocks yield bounded executions
formal_statement:
theorem Light.Ends.of_blockSafe : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {d : Nat} {s : Light.Stmt} {σ : Light.State} {T : Nat}
  {Q : Light.State → Prop},
  Light.Stmt.BlockSafe lim s σ → @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat s.blockCost T → Q (s.after σ) → Light.Ends lim P d s σ T Q := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Fix resource limits, a program, and a call depth. Let $s$ be a statement, $\sigma$ an initial state, $T\in\mathbb N$ a budget, and $Q$ a predicate on final states. Suppose the block-safety predicate holds for $s$ at $\sigma$, its static block cost is at most $T$, and its computed final state $\operatorname{after}(s,\sigma)$ satisfies $Q$. Then there are a final state $\sigma'$ and an execution cost $t$ such that

$$\operatorname{Exec}(s,\sigma,\sigma',t)\;\land\;t\le T\;\land\;Q(\sigma').$$

This connects the compositional safety and evaluation rules for finite blocks to the operational execution relation.

theorem_title: A verified rule for sequential memory passes
formal_statement:
theorem Light.Ends.pass {c x y n T : ℕ} {e : Expr} {loc : ℕ → ℤ} {Q : State → Prop} (f : ℕ → ℤ)
    (round : ∀ j < n, e.Safe lim ⟨Function.update loc c j, wrote μ dst f j⟩ ∧
      e.val ⟨Function.update loc c j, wrote μ dst f j⟩ = f j)
    (done : Q ⟨Function.update loc c n, wrote μ dst f n⟩)
    (hw : (lim.space : ℤ) ≤ lim.word) (hdst : dst + n ≤ lim.space) (hlen : loc x = n)
    (haddr : loc y = dst) (hx : x ≠ c := by decide) (hy : y ≠ c := by decide)
    (hT : n * (e.cost + 12) + 6 ≤ T := by first
                                            |
                                              ((simp only [Light.Stmt.blockCost, Light.Cond.cost, Light.Expr.cost,
                                                    List.map_cons, List.map_nil, List.sum_cons, List.sum_nil, ]);
                                                (first
                                                  | omega
                                                  | ((ring_nf); (omega))))
                                            | omega
                                            |
                                              (simp [] <;>
                                                  first
                                                  | omega
                                                  | ((ring_nf); (omega)))) :
    Ends lim P d (pass c (v x) (v y) e) ⟨loc, μ⟩ T Q := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Consider a Light state with locals $\lambda$, memory $\mu$, and destination $b$. Let $\mu_j$ overwrite exactly the first $j$ destination cells with $f(0),\ldots,f(j-1)$, where $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$, and set $\lambda_j=\lambda[c\mapsto j]$. Assume the expression $e$ is safe and evaluates to $f(j)$ in $(\lambda_j,\mu_j)$ for every $j<n$.

Suppose locals $x,y$, both distinct from $c$, hold $n,b$; the destination satisfies $b+n\le\mathrm{space}\le\mathrm{word}$; and the desired postcondition $Q$ holds at $(\lambda_n,\mu_n)$. Whenever
$$
n\bigl(\operatorname{cost}(e)+12\bigr)+6\le T,
$$
the pass writing $e$ to cell $b+j$ at round $j$ terminates within $T$ steps and establishes $Q$, in any program and depth context.

This provides a reusable execution rule for array-writing loops.

theorem_title: A loop invariant with an explicit total cost
formal_statement:
theorem Light.Ends.while : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {d : Nat} {σ : Light.State} {c : Light.Cond} {s : Light.Stmt}
  {Q : Light.State → Prop} (I : Nat → Light.State → Prop) (n : Nat) (b : Nat → Nat)
  (hI : I (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) σ)
  (hs :
    ∀ (i : Nat) (σ : Light.State),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i n →

Fix resource limits, a program, a call depth, an initial state $\sigma$, a condition $c$, and a loop body $s$. Let $I_i$ be a state predicate for each $i\in\mathbb N$, let $n$ be the number of iterations, and let $b_i$ bound iteration $i$'s body cost. Assume $I_0(\sigma)$. Whenever $i<n$ and $I_i$ holds, the condition is safe and true, and the body terminates within $b_i$ steps in a state satisfying $I_{i+1}$. Whenever $I_n$ holds, the condition is safe and false and the desired postcondition $Q$ holds.

The loop terminates with $Q$, within the cost

$$T=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\bigl(\operatorname{cost}(c)+1+b_i\bigr)+\operatorname{cost}(c)+1.$$

This rule combines an indexed loop invariant with a finite execution budget, including the final unsuccessful condition test.

natural_language_statement:
Let a Light program contain the recursive sort, halving, merge and copy bodies. Suppose memory $\mu$ stores an integer list $L$ of length $n$ at $a$, with $a+n\le f$, $f+n\le\mathrm{space}\le\mathrm{word}$, $1\le\mathrm{word}$, and current depth $d<\mathrm{depth}$. When $n>1$, assume every stored list of length $m$ with $2m\le n+1$, ending before $f$, satisfies the sorting contract at depth $d+1$ within $S(m)$ steps, for arbitrary initial memory.

Starting the sort body with locals $(n,a,f)$ terminates within
$$
S(n)=61n\lceil\log_2 n\rceil+74(n-1)_++4
$$
steps, where the ceiling-log convention is zero at $n=0$. Its final memory stores a nondecreasing permutation of $L$ at $a$ and preserves every cell below $f$ outside $[a,a+n)$.

This is the compositional induction step for the recursive sorter.

It produces

$$
r=x\bmod M,\qquad \mu'(q)=\mu(q)\quad(q<f).
$$

Here the remainder is Euclidean. This provides the bounded-machine modular arithmetic used throughout the construction.

    @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt

            (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) h

natural_language_statement:
Fix a program containing the halving procedure, resource limits, a call depth, and initial memory $\mu$. Let $h\in\mathbb N$, and suppose $h+1$ fits within the word-magnitude limit. Put $c=\lceil h/2\rceil=(h+1)\mathbin{/}2$. The procedure called on $h$ returns

$$r=c,\qquad\mu'=\mu,\qquad\text{cost}\le10c+10.$$

This gives the exact rounded half used to split recursive subproblems, with a budget valid also at $h=0$.

        (@List.instGetElem?NatLtLength.{0} Light.Stmt) P p)
      (@Option.some.{0} Light.Stmt Light.mergeBody))
  (C : Light.Merge.Pre lim μ a b dst l r),
  Light.Meets lim P p d
    (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt a)
      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (@List.length.{0} Int l))
        (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt b)
          (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (@List.length.{0} Int r))
            (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt dst) (@List.nil.{0} Int))))))
    μ
    (Light.mergeTime
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (@List.length.{0} Int l)
        (@List.length.{0} Int r)))
    fun (x : Int) (μ' : Nat → Int) =>
    And
      (Light.Seg μ' dst
        (@List.merge.{0} Int l r fun (a b : Int) => @Decidable.decide (@LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt a b) (a.decLe b)))
      (Light.SameOutside μ μ' dst
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (@List.length.{0} Int l)
          (@List.length.{0} Int r))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let integer lists $L,R$ be stored in memory $\mu$ at bases $a,b$, and write $n=|L|+|R|$. Assume the two source segments and the destination segment $[z,z+n)$ fit within the machine space bound, the destination is disjoint from each source segment, and space does not exceed the word bound. If the called procedure in $P$ is the merge body, then at any call depth it finishes within $40n+12$ steps with

$$
\nu[z:z+n]=\operatorname{merge}(L,R),\qquad\nu(x)=\mu(x)\quad(x\notin[z,z+n)).
$$

The merge takes the left head unless the right head is smaller. The inputs need not be sorted, and the theorem imposes no numerical bound on their entries. This supplies the exact list-merge primitive used by normalization.

      (@Neg.neg.{0} Int Int.instNegInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt a)) (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt M))
    (@ite.{1} Int
      (@Eq.{1} Nat (@HMod.hMod.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMod.{0} Nat Nat.instMod) a M)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))))
      (instDecidableEqNat (@HMod.hMod.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMod.{0} Nat Nat.instMod) a M)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))))
      (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0)))
      (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHSub.{0} Int Int.instSub) (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt M)
        (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (@HMod.hMod.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMod.{0} Nat Nat.instMod) a M)))) := by

natural_language_statement:
Let $a,M\in\mathbb N$ with $M\ge1$, and let $r=a\bmod M$ be the natural-number remainder. Interpreting $-a$ and $M$ as integers, their Euclidean remainder satisfies

$$(-a)\bmod M=\begin{cases}0,&r=0,\\M-r,&r\ne0.\end{cases}$$

This identity converts a remainder routine for nonnegative inputs into the corresponding calculation for negative inputs.

theorem Light.powTable_ends : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {d : Nat} {μ : Nat → Int} {dst L b : Nat} (e p : Int) (t : List.{0} Int)
  (hw : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt lim.space) lim.word)
  (hdst : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) dst L) lim.space)
  (hpow :
    ∀ (j : Nat),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat j L →
        @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt
            (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
              (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) b j))
          lim.word),
  Light.Ends lim P d Light.powTableBody
    {
      loc :=
        Light.frame
          (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt dst)
            (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt L)
              (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt b)
                (@List.cons.{0} Int e (@List.cons.{0} Int p t))))),
      mem := μ }
    (Light.powTableTime L) fun (σ' : Light.State) =>
    And (Light.Seg σ'.mem dst (Light.powList b L)) (Light.SameOutside μ σ'.mem dst L) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $b,L,\mathrm{dst}$ be natural numbers and $\mu$ an initial memory. Suppose $\mathrm{dst}+L\le\mathrm{space}\le\mathrm{word}$ and $b^j\le\mathrm{word}$ for every $j\le L$. Start the Light power-table body with argument locals $(\mathrm{dst},L,b)$, arbitrary values in its exponent and power scratch locals, and any trailing list of locals.

In any program and depth context it terminates within $17L+8$ steps, with final memory $\nu$ satisfying
$$
\nu(\mathrm{dst}+j)=b^j\quad(0\le j<L),\qquad
\nu(a)=\mu(a)\quad\bigl(a\notin[\mathrm{dst},\mathrm{dst}+L)\bigr).
$$
The bound on powers includes $b^L$, the final multiplication result. This certifies a reusable primitive for constructing positional-power tables.

theorem_title: Concatenation corresponds to adjacent memory segments
formal_statement:
theorem Light.seg_append : ∀ {μ : Nat → Int} {a : Nat} {l₁ l₂ : List.{0} Int},
  Iff
    (Light.Seg μ a
      (@HAppend.hAppend.{0, 0, 0} (List.{0} Int) (List.{0} Int) (List.{0} Int)
        (@instHAppendOfAppend.{0} (List.{0} Int) (@List.instAppend.{0} Int)) l₁ l₂))
    (And (Light.Seg μ a l₁)
      (Light.Seg μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) a (@List.length.{0} Int l₁)) l₂)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ be memory, $a\in\mathbb N$ an address, and $L_1,L_2$ lists of integers. The predicate $\operatorname{Seg}(\mu,a,L)$ means that memory contains $L$ consecutively from address $a$. Then

$$\operatorname{Seg}(\mu,a,L_1\mathbin{+\!+}L_2)\iff\operatorname{Seg}(\mu,a,L_1)\land\operatorname{Seg}(\mu,a+|L_1|,L_2).$$

This equivalence allows a contiguous array representation to be split at a list boundary or assembled from adjacent pieces, including empty pieces.

formal_statement:
theorem Light.seg_cons : ∀ {μ : Nat → Int} {a : Nat} {l : List.{0} Int} {x : Int},
  Iff (Light.Seg μ a (@List.cons.{0} Int x l))

        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) a
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))

natural_language_statement:
Let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ be memory, $a$ a starting address, $x\in\mathbb Z$, and $L$ a list of integers. Write $\operatorname{Seg}(\mu,a,L)$ when memory at addresses $a+i$ contains $L_i$ for every $i<|L|$. Then

$$\operatorname{Seg}(\mu,a,x::L)\iff\mu(a)=x\;\land\;\operatorname{Seg}(\mu,a+1,L).$$

This gives the head-and-tail rule for reading or constructing contiguous memory representations.

theorem_title: Merge sort returns a sorted permutation within its resource budget
formal_statement:
theorem Light.sort_meets : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {pSort pHalf pMerge pCopy : Nat}
  (C : Light.MergeSort.Procs P pSort pHalf pMerge pCopy)
  (hw : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt lim.space) lim.word)
  (h1 : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 1) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 1))) lim.word) {a fr : Nat}
  {L : List.{0} Int} {μ : Nat → Int} (hseg : Light.Seg μ a L)
  (haf :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) a (@List.length.{0} Int L)) fr)
  (hfr :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) fr (@List.length.{0} Int L)) lim.space)
  (d : Nat),
  @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) d
          (Nat.clog (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) (@List.length.{0} Int L)))
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
      lim.depth →
    Light.Meets lim P pSort d
      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (@List.length.{0} Int L))
        (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt a)
          (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt fr) (@List.nil.{0} Int))))
      μ (Light.sortTime (@List.length.{0} Int L)) fun (x : Int) => Light.MergeSort.Sorted μ a fr L := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let a memory segment at address $a$ contain an integer list $L$ of length $n$. Suppose the program contains the specified recursive sort, halving, merge, and copy procedures. Write $S,B,D$ for its space, word, and depth limits, and assume
$$S\le B,\quad 1\le B,\quad a+n\le f,\quad f+n\le S,\quad d+\operatorname{clog}_2n+1\le D.$$
The call at depth $d$ using scratch base $f$ terminates within
$$61n\operatorname{clog}_2n+74(n-1)_++4$$
steps. Here $\operatorname{clog}_2n$ is the natural ceiling logarithm, taking value zero at zero. The output segment contains a nondecreasing list $L'$ with $L'\sim L$ as a permutation. Every cell below $f$ outside $[a,a+n)$ keeps its initial value.

This is the sorting contract used to arrange input values while retaining all indexed occurrences.

formal_statement:
theorem Light.sqrt_meets : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {d p K : Nat}
  (hp :
    @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} Light.Stmt)
      (@GetElem?.getElem?.{0, 0, 0} Light.Program Nat Light.Stmt
        (fun (as : List.{0} Light.Stmt) (i : Nat) => @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i (@List.length.{0} Light.Stmt as))
        (@List.instGetElem?NatLtLength.{0} Light.Stmt) P p)
      (@Option.some.{0} Light.Stmt Light.sqrtBody))
  (μ : Nat → Int)
  (hword :
    @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt
      (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
          (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 3) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 3))) K)
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 4) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 4)))))
      lim.word),
  Light.Meets lim P p d (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt K) (@List.nil.{0} Int)) μ
    (Light.sqrtTime K) fun (r : Int) (μ' : Nat → Int) =>
    And (@Eq.{1} Int r (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt K.sqrt)) (@Eq.{1} (Nat → Int) μ' μ) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Fix a program containing the square-root procedure, resource limits, a call depth, and initial memory $\mu$. Let $K\in\mathbb N$ and suppose $3K+4$ fits within the word-magnitude limit. Put $s=\lfloor\sqrt K\rfloor$. The procedure called on $K$ returns

$$r=s,\qquad\mu'=\mu,\qquad\text{cost}\le18s+12.$$

This contract verifies the exact rounded square root and its finite cost, including $K=0$, for the schedule's arithmetic routines.

theorem_title: Excess incidence mass forces a good owner
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.Arithmetic.early_yes : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype.{u_2} τ] [inst_1 : DecidableEq.{u_2 + 1} τ] (I : Finset.{u_1} ι)
  (owner : ι → τ) (weight : ι → Nat) (good : τ → Prop) [inst_2 : @DecidablePred.{u_2 + 1} τ good] (Rmax H : Nat)
  (hcap :
    ∀ (t : τ),
      Not (good t) →
        @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@ThreeSum.Arithmetic.fiberWeight.{u_1, u_2} ι τ inst_1 I owner weight t) Rmax)
  (hcount : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@Finset.card.{u_2} τ {t : τ | Not (good t)}) H)
  (hlarge :
    @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) Rmax H)
      (∑ i ∈ I, weight i)),
  ∃ (i : ι),
    And
      (@Membership.mem.{u_1, u_1} ι (Finset.{u_1} ι)
        (@SetLike.instMembership.{u_1, u_1} (Finset.{u_1} ι) ι (@Finset.instSetLike.{u_1} ι)) I i)
      (And (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) (weight i))
        (good (owner i))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set of incidences, $\tau$ a finite owner set, $o:I\to\tau$ the owner map, and $w_i\in\mathbb N$ the incidence weights. Let $G\subseteq\tau$ be the good owners, and let $R,H\in\mathbb N$. Suppose each bad owner has fiber weight at most $R$, and there are at most $H$ bad owners:

$$\sum_{i\in I:\,o(i)=t}w_i\le R\quad(t\notin G),\qquad |\tau\setminus G|\le H.$$

If $\sum_{i\in I}w_i>RH$, then

$$\exists i\in I:\quad w_i>0\ \land\ o(i)\in G.$$

This counting criterion justifies an early positive answer when represented mass exceeds the maximum mass attributable to false original candidates.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.Arithmetic.mul_dvd_iff_of_bezout : ∀ {m l x : Int}
  (hbez :
    ∃ (u : Int) (v : Int),
      @Eq.{1} Int
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHAdd.{0} Int Int.instAdd)
          (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHMul.{0} Int Int.instMul) u m)
          (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHMul.{0} Int Int.instMul) v l))
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 1) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 1)))),
  Iff (@Dvd.dvd.{0} Int Int.instDvd (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHMul.{0} Int Int.instMul) m l) x)
    (And (@Dvd.dvd.{0} Int Int.instDvd m x) (@Dvd.dvd.{0} Int Int.instDvd l x)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $m,\ell,x\in\mathbb Z$. Suppose there are integers $u,v$ with $um+v\ell=1$. Then

$$m\ell\mid x\iff(m\mid x\ \land\ \ell\mid x).$$

The hypothesis is a concrete Bézout certificate; no positivity or primality assumption is required. The equivalence combines separate divisibility tests into one test for the product modulus.

theorem ThreeSum.Arithmetic.small_lift_exists : ∀ {P a b c : Int} (hP : @LT.lt.{0} Int Int.instLTInt (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0))) P)

  (hc0 : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0))) c)
  (hcP : @LT.lt.{0} Int Int.instLTInt c P)
  (hdiv :
    @Dvd.dvd.{0} Int Int.instDvd P
      (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHSub.{0} Int Int.instSub)
        (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHSub.{0} Int Int.instSub) c b) a)),
  ∃ (j : Int),
    And (ThreeSum.Arithmetic.SmallLift j)
      (@Eq.{1} Int (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHSub.{0} Int Int.instSub) c b)
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHAdd.{0} Int Int.instAdd) a
          (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHMul.{0} Int Int.instMul) j P))) := by

natural_language_statement:
Let $P,a,b,c\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy $P>0$ and $0\le a,b,c<P$. Assume $P\mid(c-b-a)$, so these canonical residues satisfy the required modular relation. Then

$$\exists j\in\{-1,0,1\}:\qquad c-b=a+jP.$$

Thus the fixed three-element signed-lift list covers every modular candidate formed from canonical residues. The statement supplies the completeness direction needed when modular relations are represented by a short list of integer equations.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.ArithmeticStageBounds.powerBound_of_fifth : ∀ {f g : Nat → Nat} {a : Real} (hg : ThreeSum.StageBounds.PowerBound g a)
  (hfg :
    ∀ (n : Nat),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
        (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
          (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) (f n)
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 5) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 5))))
        (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 256) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 256)))
          (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
            (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) (g n)
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 8) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 8)))))),
  ThreeSum.StageBounds.PowerBound f
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Real Real Real (@instHMul.{0} Real Real.instMul)
      (@HDiv.hDiv.{0, 0, 0} Real Real Real (@instHDiv.{0} Real (@DivInvMonoid.toDiv.{0} Real Real.instDivInvMonoid))
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Real (nat_lit 8)
          (@instOfNatAtLeastTwo.{0} Real (nat_lit 8) Real.instNatCast
            (@Nat.instAtLeastTwoHAddOfNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 7) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 7)))
              (@Nat.instNeZeroSucc (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 6) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 6)))))))
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Real (nat_lit 5)
          (@instOfNatAtLeastTwo.{0} Real (nat_lit 5) Real.instNatCast
            (@Nat.instAtLeastTwoHAddOfNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 4) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 4)))
              (@Nat.instNeZeroSucc (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 3) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 3))))))))
      a) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $f,g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and $a\in\mathbb R$. Say a function has power bound $a$ when, for every $\varepsilon>0$, it is eventually at most $n^{a+\varepsilon}$. Suppose $g$ has power bound $a$ and $f(n)^5\le256g(n)^8$ for every $n$. Then

$$\forall\varepsilon>0,\quad f(n)\le n^{(8/5)a+\varepsilon}\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }n.$$

This converts an exact integer estimate for a rounded arithmetic cost into the real exponent bound used in the runtime ledger.

theorem_title: Every flagged owner record describes a relevant in-range band triple
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.fromOwner_sound : ∀ (A B C : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Family) (o : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Owner A B C)
  (hf :
    @Eq.{1} Nat (ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.fromOwner A B C o).flag
      (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1)))),
  have r := ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.fromOwner A B C o;
  And (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat r.a A.size)
    (And (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat r.b B.size)
      (And (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat r.c C.size)
        (@ThreeSum.Bands.Relevant.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat A.lower A.upper B.lower B.upper C.lower C.upper
          (@Prod.mk.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat) r.a (@Prod.mk.{0, 0} Nat Nat r.b r.c))))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $A,B,C$ be finite ordered families of nonempty, pairwise separated integer intervals. An owner specifies an in-range $BC$, $AB$, or $AC$ index pair. Construct its record by looking up the missing interval at $C_k^--B_j^+$, $A_i^-+B_j^-$, or $C_k^--A_i^-$, respectively, encoding a successful lookup with flag one. If the resulting record $r=(\mathrm{flag},a,b,c)$ has $\mathrm{flag}=1$, then

$$
\begin{gathered}
a<|A|,\qquad b<|B|,\qquad c<|C|,\\
A_a^-+B_b^-\le C_c^+,\qquad C_c^-\le A_a^++B_b^+.
\end{gathered}
$$

Equivalently, its indices are valid and its band triple is relevant. This ensures that accepted physical candidate records satisfy the interval condition used in later counting and reporting arguments.

theorem_title: Every physical band record comes from an owner
natural_language_statement:
Let $A,B,C$ be finite families of sorted, separated integer intervals. Their owner set is the disjoint union of the $BC$, $AB$, and $AC$ index rectangles. Let $\mathcal R(A,B,C)$ be the record list obtained by enumerating these rectangles in that order, and let $\rho(o)$ be the record produced by an owner $o$. For any record $r$,

$$r\in\mathcal R(A,B,C)\ \Longrightarrow\ \exists o:\ \rho(o)=r.$$

The statement applies to all catalog records, including lookup misses. It connects membership in the physical record list to the abstract owner-indexed representation.

theorem_title: Row-major record segments combine into one rectangular array
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.seg_rect : ∀ {μ : Nat → Int} {dst m n : Nat} (F : Nat → Nat → ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record)
  (H :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i m →
        ∀ (j : Nat),
          @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j n →
            Light.Seg μ
              (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) dst
                (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
                  (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 4) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 4)))
                  (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
                    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) i n) j)))
              (F i j).cells),
  Light.Seg μ dst (ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.cells (ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.rect m n F)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $m,n,z\in\mathbb N$, let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ be memory, and let $F(i,j)$ be a record with four natural fields $(\mathrm{flag},a,b,c)$. Write $\operatorname{cells}$ for flattening these fields into an integer list. Suppose that, for every $i<m$ and $j<n$, the four cells at $z+4(in+j)$ contain $F(i,j)$. Then

$$
\mu[z:z+4mn]
=\operatorname{cells}\bigl([F(i,j)\mid 0\le i<m,\ 0\le j<n]\bigr),
$$

where the list is ordered first by row and then by column.

This converts individual record-storage invariants into the segment specification of the full rectangular candidate table.

theorem_title: Successful interval lookup returns a containing band
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Family.lookup_sound : ∀ (A : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Family) (x : Int) (i : A.Index)
  (h : @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} A.Index) (A.lookup x) (@Option.some.{0} A.Index i)),
  And (@LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (A.lo i) x) (@LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt x (A.hi i)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $A$ be a finite family of integer intervals $[\ell_i,u_i]$, indexed by $0\le i<N$. Assume each interval is nonempty, the lower endpoints are nondecreasing, and $u_i<\ell_j$ whenever $i<j<N$. For $x\in\mathbb Z$ and an in-range index $i$, if the family's binary-search lookup returns $i$, then

$$
\operatorname{lookup}_A(x)=\operatorname{some}(i)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \ell_i\le x\le u_i.
$$

The lookup includes a check that its returned index lies in the family.

This supplies the interval-containment guarantee for successful band-candidate lookups.

theorem_title: Every relevant band triple is recovered from its selected owner
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.candidate_owner : ∀ (A B C : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Family) (t : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Triple A B C)
  (ht : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.relevant A B C t),
  @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} (ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Triple A B C))
    (ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.candidate A B C (ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.owner A B C t))
    (@Option.some.{0} (ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Triple A B C) t) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $A,B,C$ be finite families of nonempty, ordered, pairwise separated integer intervals, with endpoints $A_i^-,A_i^+$ and similarly for $B,C$. Let $(i,j,k)$ be in-range indices satisfying
$A_i^-+B_j^-\le C_k^+$ and $C_k^-\le A_i^++B_j^+$. Select its owner as $BC(j,k)$ if $A_i^-<C_k^--B_j^+$; otherwise choose $AC(i,k)$ when $A_i^-+B_j^-\le C_k^-$ and $AB(i,j)$ in the remaining case. The candidate operation reconstructs the missing index by interval lookup at, respectively, $C_k^--B_j^+$, $C_k^--A_i^-$, or $A_i^-+B_j^-$. Then

$$
\operatorname{candidate}(\operatorname{owner}(i,j,k))
=\operatorname{some}(i,j,k).
$$

Thus the quadratic owner catalog includes every relevant triple of bands.

theorem_title: Repeated greedy prime selection contracts the aggregate band score
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandPrimeChoice.modulus_score_bound : ∀ (primes : Nat → Nat) (s nA nB nC g y U r : Nat) (A B C : Nat → Int) (rs : List.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record)
  (hy : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))) y)
  (hprime : ∀ (i : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i s → Nat.Prime (primes i))
  (hinj :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i s →
        ∀ (j : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j s → @Eq.{1} Nat (primes i) (primes j) → @Eq.{1} Nat i j)
  (hlo : ∀ (i : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i s → @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat y (primes i))
  (hA :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i nA →
        @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup (A i))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt U))
  (hB :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i nB →
        @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup (B i))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt U))
  (hC :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i nC →
        @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup (C i))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt U)),
  @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
      (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
        (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) s r)
      (ThreeSum.BandWeightedScore.score primes s (ThreeSum.BandPrimeChoice.modulus primes s nA nB nC g A B C rs r) nA nB
        nC g A B C rs))
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
      (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
        (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid)))
        (Nat.log y
          (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 3) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 3))) U))
        r)
      (ThreeSum.BandWeightedScore.score primes s (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))) nA nB nC
        g A B C rs)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $(p_i)_{i\in\mathbb N}$ be a natural-number sequence whose first $s$ entries are distinct primes at least $y>1$. Let $A,B,C$ be integer arrays of lengths $n_A,n_B,n_C$ with absolute values at most a natural number $U$, and let $g,r$ be natural numbers. Fix a list of band-owner records, each with three band indices and a flag. For modulus $q$, let $S(q)$ sum, over records flagged $1$ and triples in their truncated bands, the indicator of $q\mid\delta$ times the number of pool primes not dividing $\delta$, where $\delta=C(c)-B(b)-A(a)$. Repeated records retain their multiplicity.

Set $q_0=1$ and choose $q_{k+1}=q_kp_i$ using the least-index minimizer of $S(q_kp_i)$ among the pool, with index zero for an empty pool. Then
$$s^rS(q_r)\le\bigl(\operatorname{log}^{\mathbb N}_y(3U)\bigr)^rS(1),$$
where the integer logarithm is zero at argument zero.

This establishes contraction for one modulus sequence shared by the complete owner catalog.

theorem_title: A finite budget for aggregate band scoring
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandPrimeCosts.aggregate_time_le : ∀ (p g R s U : Nat),
  @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (ThreeSum.LightBandWeightedScore.time p g R s U)
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
      (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
        (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2)))
          (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) R
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1)))))
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) s
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1)))))
      (ThreeSum.BandPrimeCosts.unit p g U)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $p,g,R,s,U\in\mathbb N$ be, respectively, the modulus bound, band-size bound, number of owner records, number of auxiliary primes, and input-magnitude bound. Write $T_{\mathrm{count}}(p,g,g,g,U)$ for the modular-counting budget and $T_{\mathrm{joint}}(p)$ for the auxiliary modulus budget. Set $u(p,g,U)=T_{\mathrm{count}}(p,g,g,g,U)+T_{\mathrm{joint}}(p)+1000$. The aggregate weighted-score budget satisfies

$$T_{\mathrm{aggregate}}(p,g,R,s,U)\le2(R+1)(s+1)u(p,g,U).$$

This is an unconditional inequality between the defined natural-number budgets. It charges the catalog scan and its fixed overhead to the same unit used for each scoring call.

theorem_title: Appending three arrays preserves their stored prefixes
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandRawA.Stored.keep_before_append : ∀ {μ ν : Nat → Int} {vals owners positions capacity len : Nat} {f : Nat → Int} {ls : List.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label}
  (H : ThreeSum.BandRawA.Stored μ vals owners positions f ls)
  (hk :
    ThreeSum.LightBandRawARow.KeptOthers μ ν
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) vals
        (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label ls))
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) owners
        (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label ls))
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) positions
        (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label ls))
      len)
  (hvals :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) vals capacity) owners)
  (howners :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) owners capacity)
      positions)
  (hfit :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label ls)
        len)
      capacity),
  ThreeSum.BandRawA.Stored ν vals owners positions f ls := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\mu,\nu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ be memories and $L$ a list of labels, each with an owner and a position. Write $\ell=|L|$. Suppose three arrays starting at $v,o,p$ in $\mu$ store, respectively, the values $f$ at these positions, the owners, and the positions, where $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$. Let capacity $C$ and append length $h$ satisfy $v+C\le o$, $o+C\le p$, and $\ell+h\le C$. Assume $\mu$ and $\nu$ agree outside the union of the three length-$h$ intervals starting at $v+\ell,o+\ell,p+\ell$. Then

$$\operatorname{Stored}(\mu,v,o,p,f,L)\Longrightarrow\operatorname{Stored}(\nu,v,o,p,f,L).$$

This preservation rule allows new rows to be appended without invalidating the already stored parallel-array prefixes.

theorem_title: Reading an incidence from its three stored arrays
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandRawA.Stored.read : ∀ {μ : Nat → Int} {vals owners positions n g k : Nat} {rs : List.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record} {f : Nat → Int}
  (H : ThreeSum.BandRawA.Stored μ vals owners positions f (ThreeSum.BandRawA.items n g rs))
  (hk : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat k (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label (ThreeSum.BandRawA.items n g rs))),
  And
    (@Eq.{1} Int (μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) vals k))
      (f (ThreeSum.BandRawA.labelAt n g rs k).position))
    (And
      (@Eq.{1} Int (μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) owners k))
        (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.BandRawA.labelAt n g rs k).owner))
      (@Eq.{1} Int (μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) positions k))
        (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.BandRawA.labelAt n g rs k).position))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $n,g\in\mathbb N$ and let $\mathcal R$ be a list of band records. Let $L$ be the incidence-label list obtained by concatenating their active A-band rows. Suppose memory $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ stores $f$-values, owners, and positions of $L$ in parallel arrays starting at $v,o,p$, where $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$. For $k<|L|$, write $L_k=(\omega_k,x_k)$. Then

$$\mu(v+k)=f(x_k),\qquad\mu(o+k)=\omega_k,\qquad\mu(p+k)=x_k,$$

with natural-number owner and position labels interpreted as integers. This gives the exact correspondence between a physical incidence index and its three memory fields.

theorem_title: An index inside concatenated band rows retains its coordinates
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandRawA.firstRows_getD : ∀ {n g s i j : Nat} {rs : List.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record} (hs : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat s i)
  (hj :
    @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j
      (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label
        (ThreeSum.BandRawA.row n g s
          (@List.getD.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record rs s
            (@Inhabited.default.{1} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record
              ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.instInhabitedRecord))))),
  @Eq.{1} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label
    (@List.getD.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label (ThreeSum.BandRawA.firstRows n g rs i)
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (ThreeSum.BandRawA.count n g rs s) j)
      (@Inhabited.default.{1} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label ThreeSum.BandRawA.instInhabitedLabel))
    { owner := s,
      position :=
        @HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
          (ThreeSum.BandPartition.start g
            (@List.getD.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record rs s
                (@Inhabited.default.{1} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record
                  ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.instInhabitedRecord)).a)
          j } := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $n,g,s,i,j\in\mathbb N$ and let $\mathcal R$ be a list of band records. Use a zero record for any index beyond its length. Let $L_t$ be row $t$: when that record is active, its labels are $(t,ga_t+q)$ for positions in its truncated A band; otherwise it is empty. Let $F_i=L_0\mathbin{+\!+}\cdots\mathbin{+\!+}L_{i-1}$ and $C_s=\sum_{t<s}|L_t|$. If $s<i$ and $j<|L_s|$, then

$$(F_i)_{C_s+j}=(s,ga_s+j).$$

This indexing identity records both the physical owner slot and the original A-array coordinate of each emitted incidence.

theorem_title: Physical A-incidence indices are exactly their owner fiber
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandRawA.mem_aIndices_iff_owner : ∀ {n g s k : Nat} {rs : List.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record}
  (hs : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat s (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record rs)),
  Iff
    (@Membership.mem.{0, 0} Nat (Finset.{0} Nat)
      (@SetLike.instMembership.{0, 0} (Finset.{0} Nat) Nat (@Finset.instSetLike.{0} Nat))
      (ThreeSum.BandRawA.aIndices n g rs s) k)
    (And (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat k (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label (ThreeSum.BandRawA.items n g rs)))
      (@Eq.{1} Nat (ThreeSum.BandRawA.labelAt n g rs k).owner s)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $n,g\in\mathbb N$ and let $R$ be a list of band-owner records. The physical A-incidence list concatenates, for each record flagged one, its truncated A-band positions, labeling every entry with its owner slot. For a valid slot $s<|R|$, let $A_s$ be the contiguous set of physical indices contributed by that record, and let $I$ be the entire incidence list. Then, for any $k\in\mathbb N$,

$$
k\in A_s\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad k<|I|\ \land\ \operatorname{owner}(I_k)=s.
$$

This exactly identifies each owner's counting domain while retaining separate physical incidences for different owners, even when their values agree.

theorem ThreeSum.BandRawA.mem_allProducts : ∀ {nA nB nC g : Nat} {rs : List.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record} {t : Prod.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat)},
  Iff

        (Prod.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat)) (@Finset.instSetLike.{0} (Prod.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat))))
      (ThreeSum.BandRawA.allProducts nA nB nC g rs) t)
    (And
      (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@Prod.fst.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat) t)
        (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label (ThreeSum.BandRawA.items nA g rs)))
      (And
        (@Membership.mem.{0, 0} Nat (Finset.{0} Nat)
          (@SetLike.instMembership.{0, 0} (Finset.{0} Nat) Nat (@Finset.instSetLike.{0} Nat))

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandRawA.mem_row : ∀ {n g owner : Nat} {r : ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record} {l : ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label},
  Iff
    (@Membership.mem.{0, 0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label (List.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label)
      (@List.instMembership.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label) (ThreeSum.BandRawA.row n g owner r) l)
    (And (@Eq.{1} Nat r.flag (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
      (And (@Eq.{1} Nat l.owner owner)
        (And (@LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (ThreeSum.BandPartition.start g r.a) l.position)
          (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat l.position (ThreeSum.BandPartition.stop n g r.a))))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $n,g,o\in\mathbb N$, let $r$ be a band record with flag $r_f$ and A-band index $r_a$, and let $\lambda=(\lambda_o,\lambda_x)$ be an owner-position label. The row generated by $r$ for owner $o$ contains exactly the labels specified by

$$\lambda\in\operatorname{row}(n,g,o,r)\iff r_f=1\ \land\ \lambda_o=o\ \land\ gr_a\le\lambda_x<\min\{n,(r_a+1)g\}.$$

The characterization applies without a positive-band-size assumption. It connects list membership to the active-record flag, physical owner, and truncated interval of valid A positions.

theorem_title: Each owner’s physical incidence product has its block score
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandRawA.owner_weightedFalseCount : ∀ (primes : Nat → Nat) (aux q nA nB nC g : Nat) (A B C : Nat → Int) (rs : List.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record)
  {s : Nat} (hs : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat s (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record rs)),
  @Eq.{1} Nat
    (@ThreeSum.Arithmetic.weightedFalseCount.{0} (Prod.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat))
      (ThreeSum.BandRawA.ownerProduct nA nB nC g rs s)
      (ThreeSum.ModuloCounts.difference (ThreeSum.BandRawA.valueAt nA g rs A) B C)
      (ThreeSum.Auxiliary.moduli (ThreeSum.WeightedScore.auxiliarySet primes aux)) (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt q))
    (ThreeSum.BandWeightedScore.block primes aux q nA nB nC g A B C
      (@List.getD.{0} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record rs s
        (@Inhabited.default.{1} ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.instInhabitedRecord))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $A,B,C$ be integer arrays with natural lengths $n_A,n_B,n_C$, let $g$ be the band size, and let $R$ be a record list with $s<|R|$. Let $p:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, $a,q\in\mathbb N$, and let $\Lambda=\{p(i):i<a\}$ be the auxiliary modulus set. Define $w(z)=|\{\ell\in\Lambda:\ell\nmid z\}|$. Let $\mathcal P_s$ pair the physical A-incidence indices owned by $s$ with that record's B- and C-band positions; write $\widetilde A$ for the corresponding physical values. Then

$$
\sum_{\substack{(i,j,k)\in\mathcal P_s\\q\mid C_k-B_j-\widetilde A_i}}w(C_k-B_j-\widetilde A_i)=\operatorname{blockScore}(R_s).
$$

The block score is the same weighted count on the three original truncated bands when the flag is one, and zero otherwise. No primality or injectivity hypothesis on $p$ is needed for this identity.

        (fun (i : Nat) => @List.getD.{0} Int A i (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0))))
        (@Prod.fst.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat) t)))

          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0)))))) := by

natural_language_statement:
Let $A,B,C$ be finite integer lists, $g\in\mathbb N$, and $R$ any list of band records carrying flags. Form the raw-A incidence list by concatenating each flagged record's truncated A band, retaining the physical owner and source position. Let $\mathcal P$ be the union of the corresponding physical A-index, original B-band, and original C-band products. If $(i,j,k)\in\mathcal P$ and $a_i$ is the A value selected by raw incidence $i$, then

$$
a_i\in A,\qquad B.\operatorname{getD}(j,0)\in B,\qquad C.\operatorname{getD}(k,0)\in C.
$$

The lookup notation supplies zero only for an out-of-range index; membership in $\mathcal P$ guarantees that these accesses are in range.

theorem_title: Every relevant band product appears in its physical owner domain
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandRawA.relevant_product_complete : ∀ {A B C : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Family} {nA nB nC g pA pB pC : Nat} (t : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.Triple A B C)
  (ht : ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.relevant A B C t)
  (ha :
    And
      (@LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
        (ThreeSum.BandPartition.start g (@Fin.val A.size (@Prod.fst.{0, 0} A.Index (Prod.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index) t)))
        pA)
      (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat pA
        (ThreeSum.BandPartition.stop nA g
          (@Fin.val A.size (@Prod.fst.{0, 0} A.Index (Prod.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index) t)))))
  (hb :
    And
      (@LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
        (ThreeSum.BandPartition.start g
          (@Fin.val B.size
            (@Prod.fst.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index (@Prod.snd.{0, 0} A.Index (Prod.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index) t))))
        pB)
      (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat pB
        (ThreeSum.BandPartition.stop nB g
          (@Fin.val B.size
            (@Prod.fst.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index (@Prod.snd.{0, 0} A.Index (Prod.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index) t))))))
  (hc :
    And
      (@LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
        (ThreeSum.BandPartition.start g
          (@Fin.val C.size
            (@Prod.snd.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index (@Prod.snd.{0, 0} A.Index (Prod.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index) t))))
        pC)
      (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat pC
        (ThreeSum.BandPartition.stop nC g
          (@Fin.val C.size
            (@Prod.snd.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index (@Prod.snd.{0, 0} A.Index (Prod.{0, 0} B.Index C.Index) t)))))),
  ∃ (k : Nat),
    And
      (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat k
        (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label
          (ThreeSum.BandRawA.items nA g (ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.records A B C))))
      (And
        (@Eq.{1} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label (ThreeSum.BandRawA.labelAt nA g (ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.records A B C) k)
          { owner := ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.slot A B C (ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.owner A B C t), position := pA })
        (@Membership.mem.{0, 0} (Prod.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat))
          (Finset.{0} (Prod.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat)))
          (@SetLike.instMembership.{0, 0} (Finset.{0} (Prod.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat)))
            (Prod.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat)) (@Finset.instSetLike.{0} (Prod.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat))))
          (ThreeSum.BandRawA.ownerProduct nA nB nC g (ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.records A B C)
            (ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.slot A B C (ThreeSum.BandEnumeration.owner A B C t)))
          (@Prod.mk.{0, 0} Nat (Prod.{0, 0} Nat Nat) k (@Prod.mk.{0, 0} Nat Nat pB pC)))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $A,B,C$ be finite, ordered families of nonempty, pairwise separated integer intervals. Let $t=(i,j,\ell)$ satisfy $A_i^{\rm lo}+B_j^{\rm lo}\le C_\ell^{\rm hi}$ and $C_\ell^{\rm lo}\le A_i^{\rm hi}+B_j^{\rm hi}$. For natural lengths $n_A,n_B,n_C$ and band width $g$, choose positions $p_A,p_B,p_C$ in the corresponding half-open index bands $[ag,\min(n,(a+1)g))$. Let $r$ be the canonical owner-record list, $s$ the physical slot of the owner of $t$, and $I$ its flattened $A$-incidence list. Then
$$
\exists k<|I|:\quad \operatorname{label}(k)=(s,p_A),\qquad
(k,p_B,p_C)\in\operatorname{ownerProduct}(r,s).
$$
Here the owner product combines that owner's physical $A$ indices with its original $B/C$ positions. Thus every relevant coordinate triple is retained with its physical incidence identity.

theorem_title: Cellwise equations establish storage of an A-band row
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandRawA.row_stored : ∀ {μ : Nat → Int} {vals owners positions n g owner : Nat} {r : ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record} {f : Nat → Int}
  (H :
    ∀ (j : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j (@List.length.{0} ThreeSum.BandRawA.Label (ThreeSum.BandRawA.row n g owner r)) →
        And
          (@Eq.{1} Int (μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) vals j))
            (f
              (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (ThreeSum.BandPartition.start g r.a) j)))
          (And
            (@Eq.{1} Int (μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) owners j))
              (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt owner))
            (@Eq.{1} Int (μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) positions j))
              (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt
                (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (ThreeSum.BandPartition.start g r.a)
                  j))))),
  ThreeSum.BandRawA.Stored μ vals owners positions f (ThreeSum.BandRawA.row n g owner r) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ be memory, $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ a value array, and $v,o,p,n,g,\omega\in\mathbb N$. For a band record $r$, let $L=\operatorname{row}(n,g,\omega,r)$ and $a=gr_a$, its A-band starting position. Suppose every $j<|L|$ satisfies

$$\mu(v+j)=f(a+j),\qquad\mu(o+j)=\omega,\qquad\mu(p+j)=a+j.$$

Then

$$\operatorname{Stored}(\mu,v,o,p,f,L).$$

Here storage means that the three parallel arrays contain the values, owner labels, and position labels of $L$. The rule packages the routine's individual cell guarantees into this reusable array representation.

theorem_title: Uniform weighted-score bound for one band-owner block
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BandWeightedScore.block_bound : ∀ (primes : Nat → Nat) (s q nA nB nC g : Nat) (A B C : Nat → Int) (r : ThreeSum.BandCandidateRows.Record)
  (hprime : ∀ (i : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i s → Nat.Prime (primes i))
  (hinj :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i s →
        ∀ (j : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j s → @Eq.{1} Nat (primes i) (primes j) → @Eq.{1} Nat i j),
  @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (ThreeSum.BandWeightedScore.block primes s q nA nB nC g A B C r)
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) s
      (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
        (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) g
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 3) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 3))))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $A,B,C:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ have declared lengths $n_A,n_B,n_C$, let $g,s,q\in\mathbb N$, and let $p_0,\ldots,p_{s-1}$ be distinct primes. A record $r=(\mathrm{flag},a,b,c)$ selects the three truncated bands starting at $ag,bg,cg$, each of length at most $g$. Its block score is zero unless $\mathrm{flag}=1$; otherwise it sums, over triples in those bands with $q\mid C_k-B_j-A_i$, the number of selected primes that do not divide $C_k-B_j-A_i$. Then

$$
\operatorname{block}(p,s,q,n_A,n_B,n_C,g,A,B,C,r)\le s g^3.
$$

All lengths and the base modulus may be zero. This is the uniform initial charge for each physical candidate record, retaining catalog multiplicities.

theorem_title: Interval lookup finds every containing separated interval
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BinarySearch.locate_complete : ∀ (lo hi : Nat → Int) (n : Nat) (x : Int)
  (hsorted :
    ∀ (i j : Nat),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat i j → @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j n → @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (lo i) (lo j))
  (hseparated :
    ∀ (i j : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i j → @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j n → @LT.lt.{0} Int Int.instLTInt (hi i) (lo j))
  {i : Nat} (hin : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i n) (hil : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (lo i) x)
  (hih : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt x (hi i)),
  @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} Nat) (ThreeSum.BinarySearch.locate lo hi n x) (@Option.some.{0} Nat i) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\ell,h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ describe $n$ closed intervals. Suppose their lower endpoints are nondecreasing, and whenever $i<j<n$ the strict separation $h(i)<\ell(j)$ holds. If $i<n$ and $\ell(i)\le x\le h(i)$, then the binary-search interval locator returns

$$
\operatorname{locate}(\ell,h,n,x)=\operatorname{some}(i).
$$

The locator first finds the upper-bound position among the lower endpoints and then checks the preceding interval's upper endpoint. This establishes completeness of the interval access used to identify a matching band.

theorem_title: Every returned interval contains the query
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BinarySearch.locate_sound : ∀ (lo hi : Nat → Int) (n : Nat) (x : Int)
  (hsorted :
    ∀ (i j : Nat),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat i j → @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j n → @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (lo i) (lo j))
  {i : Nat} (h : @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} Nat) (ThreeSum.BinarySearch.locate lo hi n x) (@Option.some.{0} Nat i)),
  And (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i n)
    (And (@LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (lo i) x) (@LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt x (hi i))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\ell,h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$, let $n\in\mathbb N$, and assume $\ell$ is nondecreasing on indices below $n$. For an integer query $x$, if the binary-search interval locator returns index $i$, then

$$
\operatorname{locate}(\ell,h,n,x)=\operatorname{some}(i)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad i<n\ \land\ \ell(i)\le x\le h(i).
$$

No separation assumption on the intervals is needed for this soundness result. It certifies every successful band lookup even before uniqueness or completeness is used.

theorem_title: Correctness of the upper-bound binary search
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BinarySearch.upperSearch_correct : ∀ (f : Nat → Int) (x : Int) (n fuel lo hi : Nat)
  (hsorted :
    ∀ (i j : Nat),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat i j → @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j n → @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (f i) (f j))
  (hlo : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat lo hi) (hhi : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat hi n)
  (hwidth :
    @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHSub.{0} Nat instSubNat) hi lo)
      (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@instPowNat.{0} Nat instNatPowNat))
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) fuel))
  (hlower : ∀ (i : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i lo → @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (f i) x)
  (hupper :
    ∀ (i : Nat), @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat hi i → @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i n → @LT.lt.{0} Int Int.instLTInt x (f i)),
  ThreeSum.BinarySearch.Partition f x n (ThreeSum.BinarySearch.upperSearch f x fuel lo hi) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ be nondecreasing on its first $n$ entries, and let $x\in\mathbb Z$. Choose natural numbers $b,\ell,h$ with $\ell\le h\le n$ and $h-\ell<2^b$. Assume every index below $\ell$ has value at most $x$, and every index from $h$ to $n-1$ has value strictly above $x$. If $k$ is the result of the upper-bound search with fuel $b$ and interval $[\ell,h)$, then

$$
k\le n,\qquad (\forall i<k,\ f(i)\le x),\qquad (\forall k\le i<n,\ x<f(i)).
$$

Thus the bounded search returns the correct partition point, including when the result is the end of the array.

theorem_title: Flattening the constructed coefficient rows
natural_language_statement:
Let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ be memory, with array bases $d_0,d_1$, and let $J,L,p\in\mathbb N$. Let $s:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ select rows and let $w_0,w_1:\mathbb N^2\to\mathbb N$ be their coefficients. Assume the stored row invariant: for $a<J$, $b<L$, and $e\in\{0,1\}$, memory at $d_e+aL+b$ contains $p^a w_e(s(a),b)$. Define the flattened function by $F_e(aL+b)=p^a w_e(s(a),b)$ on the $JL$ positions. Then

$$
\forall e\in\{0,1\}\ \forall i<JL,\qquad \mu(d_e+i)=F_e(i).
$$

The equality identifies the constructor's row layout with the flat array read by the mask evaluator, including empty dimensions.

theorem_title: Disjointness of the forced-prefix decomposition
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BlockForced.forced_disjoint : ∀ {J L : Nat} (I : Finset.{0} (Fin J)) (Q u : Fin J → Finset.{0} (Fin L))
  (x : Finset.{0} (ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L))
  (hx :
    @LE.le.{0} (Finset.{0} (ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L))
      (@Preorder.toLE.{0} (Finset.{0} (ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L))
        (@PartialOrder.toPreorder.{0} (Finset.{0} (ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L))
          (@Finset.instPartialOrder.{0} (ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L))))
      x (@ThreeSum.BlockForced.remaining J L I Q)),
  @Disjoint.{0} (Finset.{0} (ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L))
    (@Finset.instPartialOrder.{0} (ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L))
    (@Finset.instOrderBot.{0} (ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L))
    (@Union.union.{0} (Finset.{0} (ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L))
      (@Finset.instUnion.{0} (ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L) fun (a b : ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L) =>
        @Sigma.instDecidableEqSigma.{0, 0} (Fin J) (fun (_i : Fin J) => Fin L) (instDecidableEqFin J)
          (fun (a : Fin J) => instDecidableEqFin L) a b)
      (@ThreeSum.BlockForced.prefixLeft J L I u) x)
    (@Union.union.{0} (Finset.{0} (ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L))
      (@Finset.instUnion.{0} (ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L) fun (a b : ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L) =>
        @Sigma.instDecidableEqSigma.{0, 0} (Fin J) (fun (_i : Fin J) => Fin L) (instDecidableEqFin J)
          (fun (a : Fin J) => instDecidableEqFin L) a b)
      (@ThreeSum.BlockForced.prefixRight J L I Q u)
      (@SDiff.sdiff.{0} (Finset.{0} (ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L))
        (@Finset.instSDiff.{0} (ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L) fun (a b : ThreeSum.BlockRows.Coord J L) =>
          @Sigma.instDecidableEqSigma.{0, 0} (Fin J) (fun (_i : Fin J) => Fin L) (instDecidableEqFin J)
            (fun (a : Fin J) => instDecidableEqFin L) a b)
        (@ThreeSum.BlockForced.remaining J L I Q) x)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $J,L\in\mathbb N$, let $I\subseteq\{0,\ldots,J-1\}$, and let $Q_i,u_i\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$. Define $P_L=\{(i,a):i\in I,\ a\in u_i\}$, $P_R=\{(i,a):i\in I,\ a\in Q_i\setminus u_i\}$, and $R=\{(i,a):i\notin I,\ a\in Q_i\}$. For every $X\subseteq R$,

$$
(P_L\cup X)\cap(P_R\cup(R\setminus X))=\varnothing.
$$

No containment assumption on the $u_i$ is required for this disjointness claim. Together with the corresponding coverage identity, it supports the exact left/right decomposition used in prefix reporting.

theorem_title: Remaining blocks become a contiguous suffix
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BlockIndexedQuery.index_suffixDomain : ∀ {J L k : Nat} (hk : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat k J),
  @Eq.{1} (Finset.{0} (Fin (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) J L)))
    (@ThreeSum.BlockIndex.indexSet J L (@ThreeSum.BlockForced.suffixDomain J L (ThreeSum.BlockRows.prefixIndices J k)))
    (ThreeSum.SubsetStages.suffix (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) J L)
      (ThreeSum.BlockIndexedQuery.suffixStage J L k)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $J,L,k\in\mathbb N$ with $k\le J$. View the coordinates as pairs $(i,a)$ with $i<J$ and $a<L$, flattened by the row-major index $iL+a$. The suffix domain after fixing the first $k$ blocks consists of all pairs with $i\ge k$. Its image is

$$
\{iL+a:k\le i<J,\ 0\le a<L\}=\{q\in\mathbb N:kL\le q<JL\}.
$$

Equivalently, this is the subset-transform suffix of length $(J-k)L$ in the ground set of size $JL$. The identity aligns the block reporting query with the contiguous suffix processed by the stored transform stages.

theorem_title: Boolean update for the greedy uncovered set
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BooleanGreedy.active_succ : ∀ {matrix : Nat → Nat → Nat} {rows cols : Nat}
  (hrows : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) rows)
  (hmatrix :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i rows →
        ∀ (j : Nat),
          @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j cols →
            @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (matrix i j) (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
  (t j : Nat) (hj : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j cols),
  @Eq.{1} Nat
    (ThreeSum.BooleanGreedy.active matrix rows cols
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) t
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
      j)
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
      (ThreeSum.BooleanGreedy.active matrix rows cols t j)
      (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHSub.{0} Nat instSubNat)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1)))
        (matrix (ThreeSum.BooleanGreedy.choice matrix rows cols t) j))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $M:\mathbb N^2\to\mathbb N$ be a matrix with $R>0$ rows and $C$ columns, and assume $M_{ij}\le1$ for $i<R$ and $j<C$. At greedy step $t$, let $q_t$ be the row selected to cover the most currently uncovered columns, and let $a_t(j)\in\{0,1\}$ indicate whether column $j$ remains uncovered. For every $t\in\mathbb N$ and $j<C$,

$$
a_{t+1}(j)=a_t(j)\bigl(1-M_{q_tj}\bigr).
$$

This exact recurrence identifies the finite-set deletion performed by greedy covering with the Boolean-array update used by the implementation.

theorem_title: Greedy row selection equals the scan of negated scores
natural_language_statement:
Let $M:\mathbb N^2\to\mathbb N$ have $R>0$ rows and $C$ columns, with $M_{ij}\le1$ for valid row and column indices. Let $a_t(j)$ indicate whether column $j$ remains uncovered after $t$ greedy steps, and define the row score $s_t(i)=\sum_{j<C}M_{ij}a_t(j)$. Then

$$
\operatorname{choice}(M,R,C,t)=\operatorname{least}_{i<R}\bigl(-s_t(i)\bigr).
$$

The right side is the left-to-right integer minimum scan, retaining the earliest index on ties. This identifies the finite greedy covering choice with the score computation and scan used by the implementation.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.BoxBounds.boxSum_abs_le : ∀ {L cut U : Nat} (flags free : Finset.{0} (Fin L)) (weight : Finset.{0} (Fin L) → Int)
  (hflags : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@Finset.card.{0} (Fin L) flags) cut)
  (hweight :
    ∀ (S : Finset.{0} (Fin L)),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@Finset.card.{0} (Fin L) S) cut →
        @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup (weight S))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt U)),
  @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt
    (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup
      (@ThreeSum.SparseBoxes.boxSum.{0} (Fin L) (@Fin.instLinearOrder L) flags free weight))
    (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt
      (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
        (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
          (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid)))
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) L)
        U)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $L,c,U\in\mathbb N$, and let $F,R\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$. Let $w$ assign an integer weight to every subset of this ground set. Assume $|F|\le c$ and $|w(S)|\le U$ whenever $|S|\le c$. The box sum ranges over subsets between the required set $F\setminus R$ and the allowed set $F$. It satisfies

$$
\left|\sum_{F\setminus R\subseteq S\subseteq F}w(S)\right|\le 2^L U.
$$

This gives an explicit integer bound for stored box values, without requiring $R\subseteq F$ or any sign restriction on the weights.

$$

=\operatorname{boxSum}(F,F\cap P,w).
$$

Thus the processed coordinates are exactly the free coordinates of the box, while unprocessed flagged coordinates remain required. This bridges the stored transform invariant and the sparse-box query specification.

natural_language_statement:
Let $n>0$ and let $x:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb Z$ be an input array. The triple enumerator decodes each index below $n^3$ into three positions. Let $\operatorname{Hit}(x,t)$ mean that some decoded index below both $t$ and $n^3$ gives pairwise distinct positions whose values sum to zero. Then

$$
\operatorname{Hit}(x,n^3)\iff\exists i,j,k<n:\ i\ne j,\ i\ne k,\ j\ne k,\ x_i+x_j+x_k=0.
$$

This certifies completeness of the brute-force fallback over distinct positions. Repeated input values are permitted.

Let $x:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb Z$ and let $W\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $n\le2^W$. A coloring parameter selects two of the $W$ index-bit positions and a map from their Boolean pair to three colors. $$\exists\text{ pairwise distinct }i,j,k:\ x_i+x_j+x_k=0\iff\exists p,\ a\in A_p,\ b\in B_p,\ c\in C_p:\ a+b=c.$$

The lists preserve repeated values. The equivalence concerns distinct original positions and works for any sufficient index width, which connects the machine's class filtering to the original 3SUM problem.

theorem_title: Every coloring parameter has a bounded code
natural_language_statement:
Let $W\in\mathbb N$. A coloring parameter consists of two coordinate positions $i,j<W$ and a map from the four binary pairs to three colors. Write its four color values as $a,b,c,d\in\{0,1,2\}$ in the order $00,01,10,11$. The parameter code satisfies

$$
\operatorname{index}(p)=81(iW+j)+27a+9b+3c+d<81W^2.
$$

Thus every parameter lies within the declared range of $81W^2$ integer slots. This supports the explicit enumeration of the coordinate-and-color-map family.

theorem_title: Two coordinates distinguish three binary words
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.Coloring.two_coordinates_separate : ∀ {α : Type u_1} {s t u : α → Bool} (hst : @Ne.{u_1 + 1} (α → Bool) s t) (hsu : @Ne.{u_1 + 1} (α → Bool) s u)
  (htu : @Ne.{u_1 + 1} (α → Bool) t u),
  ∃ (i : α) (j : α),
    And
      (@Ne.{1} (Prod.{0, 0} Bool Bool) (@Prod.mk.{0, 0} Bool Bool (s i) (s j)) (@Prod.mk.{0, 0} Bool Bool (t i) (t j)))
      (And
        (@Ne.{1} (Prod.{0, 0} Bool Bool) (@Prod.mk.{0, 0} Bool Bool (s i) (s j))
          (@Prod.mk.{0, 0} Bool Bool (u i) (u j)))
        (@Ne.{1} (Prod.{0, 0} Bool Bool) (@Prod.mk.{0, 0} Bool Bool (t i) (t j))
          (@Prod.mk.{0, 0} Bool Bool (u i) (u j)))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\alpha$ be any coordinate type, and let $s,t,u:\alpha\to\{0,1\}$ be three pairwise distinct binary words. There exist coordinates $i,j\in\alpha$ for which their two-coordinate restrictions are pairwise distinct:

$$
(s_i,s_j)\ne(t_i,t_j),\qquad (s_i,s_j)\ne(u_i,u_j),\qquad (t_i,t_j)\ne(u_i,u_j).
$$

No finiteness assumption on $\alpha$ is needed. This separation fact supplies the small family of coordinate projections used in the deterministic three-color reduction.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.Cover.greedyState_geometric : ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {U : Type u_2} [inst : Inhabited.{u_1 + 1} Ω] [DecidableEq.{u_2 + 1} U] [inst_2 : Fintype.{u_1} Ω]
