Suppose memory at $m$ contains $n$ natural masks $q_i<2^L$. Let $a$ be the Boolean-table destination and $w$ the scratch base. For the specified table, mask-bit, powers, and erasure procedures, assume
$$m+n\le a,\quad a+nL\le w,\quad w+L+1\le S\le B,\quad2^{L+1}\le B,\quad d+L+2\le D.$$
The constructor terminates within $n(100L^2+127L+145)+6$ steps and writes
$$\nu(a+iL+j)=\operatorname{bit}_j(q_i)\qquad(i<n,\ j<L),$$
where $\operatorname{bit}_j$ is the $j$th binary digit, valued in $\{0,1\}$. Every cell below $w$ outside the $nL$-cell destination remains unchanged.

This turns the compact subset enumeration into the literal Boolean rows used by local overlap tests.

Let $m_i<2^L$, $i<n$, be masks stored at $A$, and let natural coefficient rows $w_0,w_1\le U$ on $L$ coordinates be stored at $C_0,C_1$. Assume $A+n,C_0+L,C_1+L\le D$, $D+n\le F$, and $F+L+1\le\mathrm{space}\le\mathrm{word}$. Require $2^{L+1}+(L+1)U\le\mathrm{word}$, $d+L+1\le\mathrm{depth}$, and the mask-hash, power-table and recursive one-hot bodies.

The call terminates within $100n(L+1)+17L+75$ steps and satisfies
$$
\nu(D+i)=\sum_{j<L}w_{\operatorname{bit}_j(m_i)}(j)\quad(i<n),\qquad
\nu(F+j)=2^j\quad(j\le L).
$$
All cells below $F$ outside $[D,D+n)$ are preserved.

This computes raw one-hot hashes while retaining the input masks and both coefficient rows.

Let $A,B\subseteq\{0,\ldots,W-1\}$, with masks $m(S)=\sum_{i\in S}2^i$. Suppose a Light program contains the union body, power-table body and recursive mask-clearing body. For result cell $D$ and scratch address $F$, assume $D+1\le F$, $F+W+1\le\mathrm{space}\le\mathrm{word}$, $2^{W+1}\le\mathrm{word}$, and $d+W+1\le\mathrm{depth}$.

The call with $(W,|A|,m(A),m(B),D,F)$ terminates within $200W^2+257W+225$ steps and yields
$$
r=m(A\cup B),\qquad \nu(D)=|A\cup B|,\qquad \nu(F+i)=2^i\quad(i\le W).
$$
Every cell below $F$, except $D$, is preserved.

This implements union for arbitrary, possibly overlapping masks while tracking the exact cardinality.

Let $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$. Define the running-minimum index $m_0=0$ and, recursively, $m_{n+1}=n$ if $f(n)<f(m_n)$, with $m_{n+1}=m_n$ otherwise. For natural numbers $i<n$,

$$f(m_n)\le f(i).$$

The strict update rule keeps the previous index when values tie. This establishes the value comparison needed for the minimum-selection routine.

Let $n>0$ and let memory $\mu$ store an integer array $f$ of length $n$ at address $A$, with $A+n\le\mathrm{space}\le\mathrm{word}$. Suppose the Light program contains the minimum-index body. Define $q_0=0$, and set $q_{j+1}=j$ when $f(j)<f(q_j)$, retaining $q_j$ otherwise.

$$
r=q_n,\qquad \nu=\mu.
$$
Here $q_n$ is the first index attaining the minimum value, since equal values do not replace the current index. This supplies a deterministic minimum-selection primitive on a nonempty stored array.

$$f+13q+N+\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+2\le S\le W,\quad128q^3(N+1)^2+4U+4p+16+N^3\le W,\quad d+\lceil\log_2p\rceil+3\le D.$$
The routine returns the exact count
$$r=\#\{(i,j,k):i<n_A,\ j<n_B,\ k<n_C,\ p\mid C_k-B_j-A_i\}.$$
It preserves all memory below $f$. The finite time budget includes capacity computation, two residue histograms, cyclic convolution, source residues, and the final lookup sum, with $400$ additional steps.

This turns modular triple counting into verified arithmetic on the original signed values.

Let $b,e\in\mathbb N$, let $\mu$ be any memory, and suppose the Light program contains the natural-power body. Assume $e\le\mathrm{word}$ and $b^i\le\mathrm{word}$ for every $0\le i\le e$.

$$
r=b^e,\qquad \nu=\mu.
$$
The conclusion includes exponent zero, for which the result is one. This certifies the scalar exponentiation routine used to compute finite layout and enumeration sizes.

natural_language_statement:
Let an integer list $L$ of length $n$ occupy memory at source address $s$. Assume the program contains the specified sorting and deduplication procedures. Reserve an output buffer at $a$ and scratch at $f$ with $s+n\le a$, $a+n\le f$, and $f+n\le S\le W$. Require $1\le W$ and entry depth $d+n+\lceil\log_2 n\rceil+2\le D$.

The routine returns the length of a list $L'$ stored at $a$, where
$$L'\text{ is strictly increasing},\qquad |L'|\le n,\qquad z\in L'\iff z\in L.$$
Its step bound is $61n\lceil\log_2n\rceil+74(n-1)+200n+114$, with natural subtraction and the formal logarithm convention at zero. Memory below $f$ outside both reserved source and output intervals is preserved.

This provides sorted, duplicate-free values while retaining the exact membership information needed by later band constructions.

Assume $S\le W$, $1\le W$, and $d+n\le D$ for word bound $W$, depth limit $D$, and starting depth $d$. $$
\mathrm{result}=|\operatorname{dedup}(L)|,\qquad\nu[z:]=\operatorname{dedup}(L),\qquad\nu(x)=\mu(x)\ (x\notin[z,z+n)).
$$

The segment equality refers to the output-list length. Deduplication retains the last occurrence of each value, matching the list specification and preserving sorted color-class membership.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.LightOriginalOffset.Procs.meets : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {d pMain a b nLeft nRight p N free U : Nat}
  [inst : @NeZero.{0} Nat (@MulZeroClass.toZero.{0} Nat Nat.instMulZeroClass) p] {μ : Nat → Int}
  (C : ThreeSum.LightOriginalOffset.Procs P pMain)
  (hw : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt lim.space) lim.word)
  (ha : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) a nLeft) free)
  (hb : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) b nRight) free)
  (hnLeft : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat nLeft N) (hnRight : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat nRight N)
  (hspace : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (ThreeSum.LightOriginalOffset.space free p N U) lim.space)
  (hword :
    @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.LightOriginalOffset.word p N U)) lim.word)
  (hd :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) d
          (Nat.clog (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) p))
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 4) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 4))))
      lim.depth)
  (hLeft :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i nLeft →
        @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt
          (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup
            (μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) a i)))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt U))
  (hRight :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i nRight →
        @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt
          (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup
            (μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) b i)))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt U)),
  Light.Meets lim P pMain d
    (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt a)
      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt b)
        (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt nLeft)
          (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt nRight)
            (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt p)
              (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt N)
                (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt free) (@List.nil.{0} Int))))))))
    μ (ThreeSum.LightOriginalOffset.time p nLeft nRight U) fun (r : Int) (ν : Nat → Int) =>
    And
      (@Eq.{1} Int r
        (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt
          (@ThreeSum.LightOriginalOffset.selected p inst
            (fun (i : Nat) => μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) a i))
            (fun (i : Nat) => μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) b i)) nLeft nRight)))
      (Light.Kept μ ν free) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let two integer arrays $A,B$ of lengths $n_A,n_B\le N$ lie below scratch base $f$, with entry magnitudes at most $U$. Fix $p>0$, put $q=2^{\lceil\log_2p\rceil}$, and assume the specified capacity, signed-histogram, and balanced-offset procedures. Require $f+13q+N+\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+2\le S\le W$, $128q^3(N+1)^2+4U+4p+16\le W$, and $d+\lceil\log_2p\rceil+4\le D$.

For residues $z$, let $H_A(z),H_B(z)$ count the original entries modulo $p$. The routine returns
$$r=\min\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{0\le t<p}\sum_z H_B(z)H_A(z-t).$$
It preserves all memory below $f$ and meets the capacity, two histogram, and balanced-offset time budgets plus $300$.

This constructs the deterministic balancing offset directly from signed input values, with multiplicities retained.

Let $p,n_L,n_R,U\in\mathbb N$. Write $c=\lceil\log_2 p\rceil_{\mathbb N}$ for the natural ceiling logarithm, with value zero for $p\le1$, and let $C=2^c$ be the padded capacity. Let $T$ be the defined time budget for the original-array offset constructor, and let $T_K(c)$ be the Karatsuba time budget at depth $c$. Then

$$
T(p,n_L,n_R,U)\le T_K(c)+252C+131(n_L+n_R)(\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+1)+12c+642.
$$

The budget includes capacity computation, both residue histograms, and correlation-minimum selection. The inequality is a statement about the budget functions for all natural parameters.

$$
r\in\{0,1\},\qquad
r=1\iff i,j,k\text{ are pairwise distinct and }x_i+x_j+x_k=0,
\qquad \nu=\mu.
$$

This checks an original-index witness after decoding a single index in the cubic enumeration.

$$w+\lfloor\log_2(V+1)\rfloor+2\le S\le B,\quad d+2<D,$$
$$32(V+TM+T+M+J+T^J+U+10)\le B.$$
For the specified digit, step, and division procedures, the decoder writes
$$\nu(a+j)=\lfloor b_j/M\rfloor,\qquad\nu(a+J+j)=f(b_j\bmod M),$$
and returns $\sum_{j<J}\lfloor b_j/M\rfloor T^{J-1-j}$. Its budget is $J(200\lfloor\log_2(V+1)\rfloor+700)+130$, and cells below $a$ are preserved.

This separates each fixed-width local-record digit into its occurrence index and retained mask, in original block order.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.LightOutputDecodeDivide.meets : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {d : Nat} {μ : Nat → Int} {a Mo V fr pMain : Nat}
  (hmain :
    @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} Light.Stmt)
      (@GetElem?.getElem?.{0, 0, 0} Light.Program Nat Light.Stmt
        (fun (as : List.{0} Light.Stmt) (i : Nat) => @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i (@List.length.{0} Light.Stmt as))
        (@List.instGetElem?NatLtLength.{0} Light.Stmt) P pMain)
      (@Option.some.{0} Light.Stmt ThreeSum.LightOutputDecodeDivide.body))
  (F : Light.Emod.Pre lim Mo V fr) (haV : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat a V),
  Light.Meets lim P pMain d
    (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt a)
      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt Mo)
        (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt fr) (@List.nil.{0} Int))))
    μ (ThreeSum.LightOutputDecodeDivide.time a Mo) fun (q : Int) (ν : Nat → Int) =>
    And
      (@Eq.{1} Int q
        (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (@HDiv.hDiv.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHDiv.{0} Nat Nat.instDiv) a Mo)))
      (Light.Kept μ ν fr) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $a,M,V,f$ be natural numbers with $M\ge1$ and $a\le V$, and let $\mu$ be integer memory. For machine space and word bounds $S,W$, assume $S\le W$, $4V+4M+16\le W$, and $f+\lfloor\log_2(V+1)\rfloor+2\le S$. If the called procedure in $P$ is the output-decoding divider, execution on $(a,M,f)$ at any depth finishes within $80K+100$ steps, where $K$ is the binary bit length of $\lfloor a/M\rfloor$ and the bit length of zero is zero. Its result and final memory satisfy

$$
q=\left\lfloor\frac aM\right\rfloor,\qquad
\nu(x)=\mu(x)\quad(x<f).
$$

The free region beginning at $f$ provides scratch space for division while preserving previously constructed data.

natural_language_statement:
Fix resource limits with memory bound $S$ and word-magnitude bound $W$, a program, and a call depth. Let $M,V,f,a\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $M\ge1$, $a\le V$, $S\le W$, $4V+4M+16\le W$, and $f+\log_2^{\mathrm{nat}}(V+1)+2\le S$. Put $K=\operatorname{bits}(a\mathbin{/}M)$. $$([a,M,f,a,K,t,0],\nu)\longrightarrow([a,M,f,a\bmod M,0,t,a\mathbin{/}M],\nu)$$

within $60K+4$ steps. This supplies both quotient and remainder for the occurrence-index decoder.

Let $T,M\ge1$, $x<TM$, $x\le V$, and let $a,p,U$ be natural accumulator, positional multiplier, and mask bound. Suppose memory $\mu$ stores a natural array $f(s)\le U$ for $s<M$ at base $b$. Let $o,t$ be distinct output addresses and $w$ a scratch base, with $b+M\le w$, $o,t<w$, and $w+\lfloor\log_2(V+1)\rfloor+2\le S\le W$. Assume $4(V+T+M+a+pT+U+10)\le W$, $d+1<D$, and the decoder and binary-divider bodies are present in $P$. Execution takes at most $100(\lfloor\log_2(V+1)\rfloor+2)+100$ steps and yields

$$
r=a+p\lfloor x/M\rfloor,\quad
\nu(o)=\lfloor x/M\rfloor,\quad \nu(t)=f(x\bmod M).
$$

Every address below $w$ other than $o,t$ is preserved. This separates an occurrence digit from its retained mask and updates the occurrence-only index.

Let $n,p>0$, let $b_i\in\{0,1\}^L$, and let $\ell_i,r_i<p$ for $i<n$. Let $H_L,H_R:[p]\to\mathbb N$ be supplied count tables bounded by $n$, and let $c$ be a cutoff. Suppose memory stores the bit matrix, both code arrays, and both count tables in segments ending at or before destination $z$. Assume $z+2n^2\le S\le W$, $100(n^2+p^2+c+L+n+p+1)\le W$, and $d<D$. If $P$ contains the pair constructor and its division, Boolean-dot, and trimming helpers, execution takes at most $n^2(20n+32L+412)+30$ steps and, for $i,j<n$, stores

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mu'(z+in+j)&=p\ell_i+r_j,\\
\mu'(z+n^2+in+j)&=\mathbf1_{\langle b_i,b_j\rangle=0\,\land\,H_L(\ell_i)\le c\,\land\,H_R(r_j)\le c}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Memory outside the two output arrays is preserved. This constructs the literal key and retained-pair tables used by the local cover matrix.

Let $L$ and the destination address $a$ be natural numbers. Assume the program contains the specified Pascal-table, row, fill, and linear-array procedures. With space, word, and depth limits $S,B,D$, suppose
$$a+(L+1)^2\le S\le B,\quad2^{L+1}\le B,\quad d+1<D.$$
Starting from any memory, the constructor terminates within $23L^2+139L+119$ steps and produces
$$\nu\bigl(a+i(L+1)+j\bigr)=\binom ij\qquad(0\le i,j\le L).$$
This includes the zero entries above each row's diagonal. Every address outside the $(L+1)^2$-cell table retains its original value.

The contract supplies a complete table of exact binomial coefficients for later finite enumeration and indexing routines.

natural_language_statement:
Let $p_0,\ldots,p_{s-1}$ be distinct primes with $p_i\ge y>1$, and let $q,n_A,n_B,n_C,M$ be natural numbers. Let $A,B,C$ be integer arrays on their respective index ranges. For each triple $(a,b,c)$ in those ranges, put $\delta=C(c)-B(b)-A(a)$ and assume $|\delta|\le M$. Define $w(\delta)$ as the number of these $s$ primes that do not divide $\delta$, and let
$$S(q)=\sum_{a<n_A,\ b<n_B,\ c<n_C}\mathbf1_{q\mid\delta}\,w(\delta).$$
Then
$$\sum_{i=0}^{s-1}S(qp_i)\le\operatorname{log}_y^{\mathbb N}(M)\,S(q),$$
where the integer logarithm is $\lfloor\log_y M\rfloor$ for $M\ge1$ and is zero for $M=0$.

This bounds the aggregate weighted false-triple score over all candidate prime extensions.

Let $y>0$ be natural and $a$ a free address. Assume the program contains the specified prime-pool and primality-test procedures, including their division and powers-table routines. For machine limits $S,B,D$, suppose
$$a+3y+\lfloor\log_2(4y+1)\rfloor+2\le S\le B,\quad32y+16\le B,\quad d+1<D.$$
The routine writes in increasing order exactly the list
$$\mathcal P_y=[p\in\mathbb N:y<p\le4y,\ p\text{ prime}],$$
returns its length, and preserves every address below $a$. With $\lambda=\lfloor\log_2(4y+1)\rfloor$, its step budget is
$$3y\bigl[(4y-2)(43\lambda+147)+170\bigr]+100.$$

This constructs the actual finite candidate-prime array used in the later search, rather than assuming that a list of primes is supplied.

theorem_title: Every scanned prime prefix is strictly increasing
natural_language_statement:
For $y,i\in\mathbb N$, let $S_{y,i}$ be the list obtained by scanning $y+1,\ldots,y+i$ in order and appending exactly the prime values. Then

$$0\le j<k<|S_{y,i}|\quad\Longrightarrow\quad(S_{y,i})_j<(S_{y,i})_k.$$

Thus every scan prefix is strictly increasing, including the empty prefix. This ordering property supports the prime-pool interface and rules out repeated candidate values.

$$r=\sum_{F\setminus E\subseteq T\subseteq F}w(T),$$

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.LightQueryEnumeration.meets : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {pMain pWeights pPowers pErase pEnum : Nat}
  (hmain :
    @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} Light.Stmt)

        (fun (as : List.{0} Light.Stmt) (i : Nat) => @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i (@List.length.{0} Light.Stmt as))
        (@List.instGetElem?NatLtLength.{0} Light.Stmt) P pMain)
      (@Option.some.{0} Light.Stmt (ThreeSum.LightQueryEnumeration.body pWeights pEnum)))
  (hweights :
    @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} Light.Stmt)

  (hpowers :
    @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} Light.Stmt)
      (@GetElem?.getElem?.{0, 0, 0} Light.Program Nat Light.Stmt
        (fun (as : List.{0} Light.Stmt) (i : Nat) => @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i (@List.length.{0} Light.Stmt as))
        (@List.instGetElem?NatLtLength.{0} Light.Stmt) P pPowers)
      (@Option.some.{0} Light.Stmt Light.powTableBody))
  (herase :
    @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} Light.Stmt)
      (@GetElem?.getElem?.{0, 0, 0} Light.Program Nat Light.Stmt
        (fun (as : List.{0} Light.Stmt) (i : Nat) => @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i (@List.length.{0} Light.Stmt as))
        (@List.instGetElem?NatLtLength.{0} Light.Stmt) P pErase)
      (@Option.some.{0} Light.Stmt (ThreeSum.LightMaskErase.body pErase)))
  (henum :
    @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} Light.Stmt)
      (@GetElem?.getElem?.{0, 0, 0} Light.Program Nat Light.Stmt
        (fun (as : List.{0} Light.Stmt) (i : Nat) => @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i (@List.length.{0} Light.Stmt as))
        (@List.instGetElem?NatLtLength.{0} Light.Stmt) P pEnum)
      (@Option.some.{0} Light.Stmt (ThreeSum.LightSubsetEnumeration.body pEnum)))
  {μ : Nat → Int} {W t dst work d : Nat} (Q : Finset.{0} (Fin W))
  (hw : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt lim.space) lim.word)
  (hspace :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) work
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
          (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)

  (hword :

        (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat

      lim.word)
  (ht :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat t
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (@Finset.card.{0} (Fin W) Q)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1)))))
  (hdst :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) dst ((@Finset.card.{0} (Fin W) Q).choose t))
      work)
  (hd :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) d W)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))))

      (And
        (Light.SegN μ' dst
          (@List.map.{0, 0} (Finset.{0} (Fin W)) Nat (@ThreeSum.SubsetAddress.subsetMask W)
            (@ThreeSum.QueryCoordinates.missingSets W Q t)))
        (And
          (ThreeSum.LightWeightedEnumeration.Weights μ' work (@Finset.card.{0} (Fin W) Q)
            (@ThreeSum.QueryCoordinates.weights W Q))

natural_language_statement:
Let $Q\subseteq\{0,\ldots,W-1\}$ have size $c$, and let $t\le c+1$. For a destination $a$ and scratch base $w$, assume
$$a+\binom ct\le w,\quad w+2W+2\le S\le B,\quad2^{W+1}\le B,\quad d+W+2\le D.$$
With the specified weight builder, powers, erasure, and recursive subset procedures, the call returns $\binom ct$ and writes the masks of exactly the $t$-element subsets of $Q$, in the defined recursive enumeration order. It also retains at $w$ the weights $2^{q_0},\ldots,2^{q_{c-1}}$, for the increasing coordinates of $Q$. Its budget is
$$100W^2+147W+185+150\mathcal E(c,t),$$
where $\mathcal E$ is the defined recursive enumeration-work count, including recursive calls and emitted-list lengths. Cells below $w$ outside the destination are preserved.

This enumerates query subsets using only the compact coordinate set, with the zero-output case $t=c+1$ included.

Let $Q\subseteq\{0,\ldots,W-1\}$ and $m(Q)=\sum_{j\in Q}2^j$. Suppose the Light program contains the query-weight body, power-table body and recursive mask-clearing body. Let $D+W\le F$, $F+W+1\le\mathrm{space}\le\mathrm{word}$, $2^{W+1}\le\mathrm{word}$, and $d+W+1\le\mathrm{depth}$.

The call with $(W,m(Q),D,F)$ terminates within $100W^2+147W+125$ steps. If $q_0<\cdots<q_{|Q|-1}$ enumerate $Q$, then
$$
r=|Q|,\qquad \nu(D+i)=2^{q_i}\quad(i<|Q|),\qquad
\nu(F+j)=2^j\quad(j\le W).
$$
Memory below $F$ outside the reserved interval $[D,D+W)$ is preserved.

This supplies the compact coordinate weights for enumerating subsets of the query itself.

natural_language_statement:
Let $k,b,p$ be natural numbers and $\mu$ any integer memory. Let $W,D$ be the machine word and depth bounds, assume $4(k+b+p+2)\le W$, and let the starting depth satisfy $d<D$. Suppose program $P$ contains the radix-digit body and the specified small-divider helper. Execution on $(k,b,p)$ terminates within $40(k+1)+100$ steps with

$$
r=(k/b)\bmod p,\qquad \mu'=\mu.
$$

Division and remainder are the total natural operations, so $u/0=0$ and $u\bmod0=u$; positivity of either radix parameter is not required. This extracts an encoded coordinate without allocating or modifying memory.

$$s+m\le a,\quad a+o_J+1+m^J\le S\le B,\quad U+pU(p+1)^J+p+1\le B,\quad d+J+2\le D.$$
The constructor returns $H=a+o_J$ and writes
$$\nu(H)=m^J,\qquad \nu(H+1+i)=(V_J)_i\quad(i<m^J).$$

The output retains every product occurrence, including repeated integer keys.

natural_language_statement:
Let $d,J\in\mathbb N$ and let $m\ge1$ be a natural number. The positional-key construction stores a length header and an array of $m^j$ keys at each stage $j=0,\ldots,J$, beginning at address $d$. Its declared end address $S(d,m,J)$ satisfies

$$
S(d,m,J)\le d+(J+1)(m^J+1).
$$

The bound includes the headers and all intermediate product stages, not only the final array. Equal key values are still stored as separate entries.

This gives a simple bound on the address range required by the complete Cartesian-product key constructor.

$$

natural_language_statement:
Let an integer list $X$ of length $n$ be stored at $s$, with $|x|\le U$ for all its entries, and let $p>0$. Choose a free address $a$ with $s+n\le a$. Assume the specified residue, affine, and integer-remainder procedures and machine bounds
$$a+3n+\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+2\le S\le B,\quad4U+4p+16\le B,\quad d+2\le D.$$
The constructor returns $a$ and writes the lift-major concatenation
$$[x\bmod p-p:x\in X]\;\mathbin{+\!+}\;[x\bmod p:x\in X]\;\mathbin{+\!+}\;[x\bmod p+p:x\in X].$$
It terminates within $n(43\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+153)+168$ steps and preserves every address below $a$.

The three rows retain the original list order and every repeated input occurrence, supplying the guarded A-side keys for reporting.

natural_language_statement:
Let $0\le k\le n$ be natural numbers and let $f$ be a scratch address. For machine limits $(S,V,L)$, assume $S\le V$, $f+(n+1)^2\le S$, $2^{n+1}\le V$, and $d+3\le L$. The reporting-binomial program, called with $(n,k,f)$ at depth $d$, returns
$$
r=\binom nk
$$
within $\operatorname{buildTime}(n)+100$ steps. Its final memory agrees with the initial memory outside the scratch interval $[f,f+(n+1)^2)$.

This supplies an actual arithmetic procedure for the combinatorial counts used by reporting children and terminal candidates.

Let $i<n\le2^{2w}$, and let $\ell_j,r_j<2^w$ for $j<n$, with distinct keys $k_j=\ell_j+2^wr_j$. Suppose memory $\mu$ stores at base $s$ a sorted permutation of $[k_j(n+1)+j:j<n]$. Put $V=2^{2w}(n+1)$ and $B=4V+4(n+1)+n+2^{2w+2}+2^{w+1}+16$. For machine limits $S,W,D$, assume $s+n\le f$, $f+\max\{2w+2,\lfloor\log_2(V+1)\rfloor+2\}\le S\le W$, $B\le W$, and $d+2w+2\le D$. The fixed lookup program on $(w,n,s,\ell_i,r_i,f)$ takes at most $274w+392+100(\lfloor\log_2(V+1)\rfloor+2)$ steps and yields

$$
r=i,\qquad \mu'(a)=\mu(a)\quad(a<f).
$$

This retrieves the original catalog position using its unique pair key.

natural_language_statement:
Let $c:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be a length-$n$ count array stored in memory $\mu$ at address $A$, with $c(i)\le\mathrm{word}$ for every $i<n$. Assume the source interval $[A,A+n)$ and destination interval $[B,B+n)$ are disjoint, both fit within $\mathrm{space}\le\mathrm{word}$, and the Light program contains the reporting-filter body.

Define the ordered list $L=[i\mid 0\le i<n,\ c(i)>0]$. The call with arguments $(n,A,B)$ terminates within $100n+40$ steps and satisfies
$$
r=|L|,\qquad \nu(B+j)=L_j\quad(j<|L|).
$$
Every memory cell outside $[B,B+n)$ is preserved.

This converts positive count entries into a compact list of their original indices.

$$

$$
It preserves all memory outside the two length-$t$ output intervals.

This preserves alignment between the selected left and right reporting masks.

natural_language_statement:
Let integer arrays $\ell,r$ have lengths $N_L,N_R$ and correct stored index buckets for keys $k_L,k_R<M$, where $M>0$. Let flags $f_L,f_R\le1$, endpoint magnitudes $|x_L|,|x_R|\le U$, and target $a$ be given. All source and bucket arrays end by scratch $w$. Assume space for $4+\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+2$ cells from $w$, depth $d+3$, space fitting in a word, and word bounds for $4U+4M+16$, $N_LN_R$, all original values, $a$, and every $a+\ell_i$. The fixed leaf returns $b\in\{0,1\}$ with
$$
b=1\iff f_L=f_R=1\ \land\ \exists i<N_L,\ j<N_R:
\ k_L(i)=x_L\bmod M,\ k_R(j)=x_R\bmod M,\ r_j=\ell_i+a.
$$
It preserves memory below $w$ within its explicit bucket-test and residue budget.

This checks original values after independent endpoint trimming.

$$w+\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+6\le S\le W,\quad4U+4M+16\le W,\quad d+n+4\le D.$$

$$r=1\iff\exists s<n,\ i<N_L,\ j<N_R:\ f_s=g_s=1,\ \kappa_L(i)=x_s\bmod M,\ \kappa_R(j)=y_s\bmod M,\ a+L_i=R_j.$$

natural_language_statement:
Let $n,g\in\mathbb N$, $R$ be band-owner records, and $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ the source array. Suppose memory $\mu$ stores the physical incidence list's values, owner labels, and position labels, and stores the four-cell records at base $r$. Let $N$ be the incidence count and $i<N$. Assume the value and owner arrays of length $N$, record array of length $4|R|$, and four-cell destination at $z$ fit in space $S$. Assume $S\le W$, the selected value has absolute value at most $W$, and the selected record's B/C band indices are at most $S$. At any call depth, the selector finishes within $700$ steps with

$$
\mathrm{result}=z,\qquad\nu[z:z+4]=[f(\mathrm{position}_i),\mathrm{owner}_i,R_{\mathrm{owner}_i}.b,R_{\mathrm{owner}_i}.c].
$$

It preserves every cell outside the destination. This recovers the original value and independent band choices from a physical incidence index.

Let natural arrays $\ell_i,r_i<R$, $i<n$, be stored at addresses $A,B$. Suppose both source arrays end at or before $D$, $D+n\le\mathrm{space}\le\mathrm{word}$, and
$$
R^2(n+1)+n+R+2\le\mathrm{word}.
$$
If the Light program contains the packing body, its call with $(A,B,n,R,D)$ terminates within $50n+10$ steps and writes
$$
\nu(D+i)=(\ell_i+Rr_i)(n+1)+i\quad(i<n).
$$
Every cell outside $[D,D+n)$ is preserved.

The packed integer records both the paired key and its original catalog index, allowing later sorting to retain the index payload.

natural_language_statement:
Let $2h\le L$. Reserve an array for $\binom Lh$ left masks, then two separated arrays of length $P=\binom Lh\binom{L-h}h$, all before scratch $f$. Assume $f+2L+2$ fits in space, space fits in a word, $2^{L+1}$ fits in a word, and $d+L+3$ fits in depth. The fixed program enumerates each $h$-subset $A$ and, within its row, every $h$-subset $B$ of its complement. It writes the corresponding mask pairs and returns
$$
r=P=\binom L{2h}\binom{2h}h.
$$
The original left-layer enumeration is also stored, and memory below its base is preserved. Execution satisfies the explicit pair-row time budget.

This constructs the local balanced-pair catalog with its precise physical ordering.

natural_language_statement:
Let $2h\le L$ and $k\in\mathbb N$. Enumerate all ordered disjoint pairs $(A,B)$ of $h$-subsets of an $L$-element set, first by $A$ and then by $B$. Their number is $m=\binom L{2h}\binom{2h}h$. Let $X,Y$ be the resulting left and right mask lists, and define $V_0(Z)=[0]$, $V_{j+1}(Z)=[z+2^Ly:z\in Z,\ y\in V_j(Z)]$ in nested list order.

The fixed program uses nonoverlapping ordered regions for the initial $h$-subset list, both $m$-cell pair arrays, both complete radix-stage constructions, and scratch. Assume their stated endpoints fit $S$, $S\le W$, $2^{L+1}\le W$, the radix word budget for $(2^L,2^L,k)$ fits $W$, and $d+L+k+4\le D$. It writes headers $m^k$ followed by
$$V_k(X)\quad\text{and}\quad V_k(Y),$$
returns the left header address, preserves cells below the initial subset-list base, and meets the defined prefix-array budget.

Both outputs retain the same ordered pair-occurrence indexing.

    (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 6) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 6))) d
    (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt W)
      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt inL)
        (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt inR)

              (ThreeSum.ReportingHostPackedCatalog.codes
                (fun (i : Nat) =>
                  ThreeSum.ReportingHostPackedCatalog.pairKey
                    (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
                      (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid)))
                      (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) W)
                    (left i) (right i))
                n))
            (@List.Pairwise.{0} Int (fun (x1 x2 : Int) => @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt x1 x2) S)))

natural_language_statement:
Let $\ell_i,r_i<2^W$ be natural masks stored in two length-$n$ arrays ending by destination $z$. Define $c_i=(\ell_i+2^Wr_i)(n+1)+i$, which retains physical index $i$ as a low digit. Assume $z+n\le f$, scratch of both $W+1$ and $n$ cells fits from $f$, space fits in a word, and the catalog's word budget fits. Require $d+\operatorname{clog}_2n+2$ available depth. The fixed program produces a list $S$ with
$$
\mu'[z:z+n]=S,\qquad S\sim[c_0,\ldots,c_{n-1}],\qquad S\text{ is nondecreasing}.
$$
It preserves memory below $z$ and uses the power-table cost plus packing cost, merge-sort cost, and $120$ steps. This constructs the searchable catalog index while retaining multiplicities and original row identities.

  (hw : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt lim.space) lim.word)
  (hs : ThreeSum.ReportingHostSourceSelection.Fits X pair bank cover srcB srcC i j code J dst lim.space),
  Light.Meets lim ThreeSum.LightReportingSourceSelect.program
    (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) d
    (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt pair)
      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt bank)
        (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt cover)
          (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt srcB)
            (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt srcC)
              (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt i)
                (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt j)
                  (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt code)
                    (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt J)
                      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt dst) (@List.nil.{0} Int)))))))))))
    μ (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 6000) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 6000))) fun (result : Int) (ν : Nat → Int) =>
    And (@Eq.{1} Int result (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt dst))
      (And (Light.SegN ν dst (ThreeSum.ReportingHostSourceSelection.values X srcB srcC code J))
        (Light.SameOutside μ ν dst (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 15) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 15))))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\mu$ be integer memory, and fix natural addresses for the pair, bank, and cover headers, the original $B,C$ arrays, and a destination $z$. Fix band indices $i,j$, occurrence code $c$, block count $J$, call depth $d$, and a pointer record $X$. Assume the header reads agree with $X$ and the exact individual fitting conditions hold within space bound $S$: the pair, bank, and cover headers of lengths $3,5,16$, both six-cell band headers, both selected stage cells, the fifteen output cells, the occurrence address, every output value, and $J+X.\mathrm{bankSpan}+20$ fit. Assume also $S\le W$, the word bound. The fixed selector terminates within $6000$ steps with

$$
\mathrm{result}=z,\qquad \nu(z+t)=\mathcal V_t\ (t<15),\qquad \nu(a)=\mu(a)\ (a\notin[z,z+15)).
$$

Here $\mathcal V$ contains the two source addresses, bucket offsets and flat arrays, band sizes, stage pointers, occurrence row, maps, candidates, and two histograms prescribed by $X$. This materializes the exact controls for wanted reporting.

natural_language_statement:
Let $\iota:[V]\hookrightarrow[W]$ shift coordinates by an offset, and let $s,c\le W$. Suppose all suffix zeta stages of integer functions $f,g$ are stored through width $W$, with $|f(T)|\le B$ and $|g(T)|\le D$ for $|T|\le c$. Let prefixes $P_L,P_R$ satisfy $|P_L|+b,|P_R|+b\le c$, and let the supplied masks encode sets of one cardinality $k\le b$. Define
$$
\lambda(S)=(-1)^{|S|}Z_sf(P_L\cup\iota S)Z_sg(P_R\cup\iota S).
$$
Here $Z_s$ transforms the last $s$ coordinates. Assume the destination downset table is disjoint from both source banks and the mask array, all lie below scratch, the prescribed scratch and control bounds fit, $(2^sB)(2^sD)$ fits in a word, space fits in a word, and depth $d+W+8$ is available. The routine writes $\lambda(S)$ for listed masks and retains every other destination entry. Its time is one cell cost plus $65$ per mask, then $20$; below scratch only the destination may change.

This builds a selected layer of the signed leaf table.

Write $S,\Omega,\Delta$ for machine space, word magnitude, and depth limits. Let bounded integer set functions $f,g$ on $W$ coordinates have retained source-zeta tables through cutoff $c\le W$. Fix stage $s\le W$, offset $o$ and width $V$ with $o+V\le W$, box cutoff $b\le V$, and $n$ stored prefix pairs $(A_i,B_i)$ with constant cardinalities $c_L,c_R$. Assume $c_L+b,c_R+b\le c$. For $\iota(T)=o+T$, define
$$F_i(T)=(-1)^{|T|}Z_sf(A_i\cup\iota(T))Z_sg(B_i\cup\iota(T)).$$
Let $K=\sum_{j\le b}\binom Vj$ and $\sigma=(V+1)K$. Under the contract's ordered source, input, pointer, box, and scratch regions; space and word bounds, including $2^V(2^sB_0)(2^sD_0)$ for source bounds $B_0,D_0$; and $d+W+12\le\Delta$, the routine stores
$$\nu(p+i)=q+i\sigma\quad(i<n)$$
and every forward zeta stage of $F_i$ in the indicated family. It retains both source families and preserves all cells below $p$. Its time is $n(T_{\rm setup}+200)+30$.

This constructs a reusable suffix-table catalog, including the empty-catalog case.

theorem_title: Suffix-catalog setup has quartic overhead per retained downset entry
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.LightReportingSuffixCatalogSetup.time_bound : ∀ {W V cut offset n : Nat}
  (hfit : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) offset V) W)
  (hcut : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat cut V),
  @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (ThreeSum.LightReportingSuffixCatalogSetup.time W V cut offset n)
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
      (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
        (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 23000) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 23000)))
          (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
            (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid)))
            (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) W
              (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 4) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 4)))))
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (ThreeSum.SubsetAddress.downsetCap V cut)
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1)))))
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) n
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $W,V,c,o,N$ be natural numbers satisfying $o+V\le W$ and $c\le V$. Here $W$ is the global width, $V$ the local suffix width, $o$ its coordinate offset, $c$ the box cutoff, and $N$ the number of prefix-pair records. Put $D(V,c)=\sum_{j=0}^{c}\binom{V}{j}$. The time budget for suffix-catalog setup, including computation of the physical table stride and construction of all $N$ suffix tables, satisfies
$$T_{\mathrm{setup}}(W,V,c,o,N)\le23000(W+1)^4\bigl(D(V,c)+1\bigr)(N+1).$$

This accounts for the executable stride calculation as well as construction of the contiguous catalog, including the empty-record case.

natural_language_statement:
Embed a local universe $[V]$ into $[L]$ by $\iota(i)=o+i$, where $o+V\le L$. Let $j,c\le L$, let $P,Q\subseteq[L]$, and take $T\subseteq[V]$ with $|T|\le b$. Suppose $|P\cup\iota T|,|Q\cup\iota T|\le c$. Integer functions $f,g$ are bounded by $B,C$ on the source downset, whose complete suffix-zeta tables lie below scratch $z$. A local destination table of capacity $\sum_{i=0}^{\min(b,V)}\binom Vi$ also ends below $z$.

Assume the specified leaf and address procedures, $z+1+(L+1)^2+L+1\le S\le W$, $(L+1)2^{L+1},(2^jB)(2^jC)\le W$, and $d+L+7\le D$. Then
$$\nu(\mathrm{dst}+\operatorname{rank}(T))=(-1)^{|T|}(Z_jf)(P\cup\iota T)(Z_jg)(Q\cup\iota T).$$
Execution takes the signed-leaf budget plus the width-$V$ address budget plus $90$, and preserves every other cell below $z$.

This stores global signed-leaf data in local suffix coordinates.

natural_language_statement:
Let $Q\subseteq[V]$ be embedded into $[W]$ by a coordinate shift $\iota$, and let $t\le|Q|+1$. Suppose suffix stages $s\le W$ of $f,g$ are retained on the $c$-downset, $c\le W$, with magnitude bounds $B,D$, and both $P_L\cup\iota Q$ and $P_R\cup\iota Q$ have size at most $c$. Set $\lambda(S)=(-1)^{|S|}Z_sf(P_L\cup\iota S)Z_sg(P_R\cup\iota S)$ and $A=\sum_{j<t}\binom{|Q|}{j}$. With source banks before an $A$-cell mask buffer, sufficient scratch, space fitting in a word, the control and $(A+1)(2^sB)(2^sD)$ word bounds, and depth $d+W+8$, the program returns
$$
\sum_{\substack{U\subseteq Q\\|U|<t}}\lambda(Q\setminus U).
$$
Its budget is $t(10500(W+1)^2(A+1)+30)+40$. Below scratch only the mask buffer may change.

The cutoff counts missing coordinates, providing the explicit part of the reporting query.

natural_language_statement:
Let $o,V,W\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $o+V\le W$, and let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,V-1\}$. Its lifted mask is $M=\sum_{i\in S}2^{o+i}$. Suppose the Light program contains the suffix-lowering body, power-table body and recursive mask-clearing body. For scratch address $F$, assume $F+W+1\le\mathrm{space}\le\mathrm{word}$, $2^{W+1}\le\mathrm{word}$, and $d+W+1\le\mathrm{depth}$.

The call with $(W,V,o,M,F)$ terminates within $V(100W+130)+17W+125$ steps and satisfies
$$
r=\sum_{i\in S}2^i,\qquad \nu(F+j)=2^j\quad(j\le W),\qquad
\nu(a)=\mu(a)\quad(a<F).
$$
This converts a lifted reporting suffix into its local subset-mask representation.

natural_language_statement:
Embed $[V]$ into $[W]$ by a coordinate shift $\iota$. Let $Q\subseteq[V]$, $s,c\le W$, $t\le|Q|+1$, and $|Q|-t\le b\le|Q|$. Prefixes $P_L,P_R$ are disjoint from $\iota Q$, and their unions with it have size at most $c$. Suppose $f,g$ have bounds $B,D$ on this downset, all suffix stages are retained, and all prefix box stages of $\lambda(S)=(-1)^{|S|}Z_sf(P_L\cup\iota S)Z_sg(P_R\cup\iota S)$ are stored through width $V$ with cutoff $b$. Under the prescribed separated tables, query-mask capacity, scratch, control and sparse-query magnitude bounds, space fitting in a word, and depth $d+W+9$, the program returns
$$
\sum_{T\subseteq\iota Q}(-1)^{|Q|-|T|}Z_sf(P_L\cup T)Z_sg(P_R\cup T).
$$
It meets the suffix-query time budget; below scratch only the query-mask buffer may change.

This computes the required Möbius value using the explicit/box partition.

theorem_title: The suffix-query budget is cubic in width per enumerated query item
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.LightReportingSuffixQuery.time_bound : ∀ {W V c t : Nat} (hV : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat V W) (hc : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat c V)
  (ht :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat t
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) c
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))),
  @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (ThreeSum.LightReportingSuffixQuery.time W V c t)
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
      (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 17000) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 17000)))
        (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
          (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid)))
          (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) W
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 3) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 3)))))
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (ThreeSum.LightSparseQuery.queryItems c t)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $W,V,c,t$ be natural numbers with $c\le V\le W$ and $t\le c+1$. Here $W$ is the ambient encoding width, $V$ the suffix width, $c$ the query-set cardinality, and $t$ the split between explicitly enumerated small subsets and canonical boxes. Define
$$Q(c,t)=\sum_{r=0}^{t-1}\binom{c}{r}+\binom{c}{t},$$
where the first sum is empty when $t=0$ and binomial coefficients beyond $c$ are zero. The executable suffix-query time budget satisfies
$$T_{\mathrm{suffix}}(W,V,c,t)\le17000(W+1)^3\bigl(Q(c,t)+1\bigr).$$

This gives a uniform bound for both portions of the signed suffix-query computation, including the boundary choice $t=c+1$.

natural_language_statement:
Let $\iota:[V]\hookrightarrow[W]$ shift coordinates by an offset and let $Q\subseteq[V]$. Fix $c,s\le W$, $t\le|Q|+1$, and $|Q|-t\le b\le|Q|$. Prefixes $P_L,P_R$ are disjoint from $\iota Q$, with both unions inside the $c$-downset. Assume retained suffix-stage banks for bounded functions $f,g$ and a retained prefix box-stage bank for their signed leaf weights. The global mask supplied to the program is the mask of $\iota Q$. Under the stated table/mask/scratch layout, control and sparse-query magnitude bounds, space fitting in a word, and depth $d+W+10$, the program returns
$$
\sum_{T\subseteq\iota Q}(-1)^{|Q|-|T|}Z_sf(P_L\cup T)Z_sg(P_R\cup T).
$$
Its budget is global-mask lowering plus the suffix-query budget and $100$ steps. Below scratch only the query-mask buffer may change.

The host computes the local mask and shift power needed by the query from the global mask itself.

$$
\lambda(S)=(-1)^{|S|}Z_sf(P_L\cup\iota S)Z_sg(P_R\cup\iota S).
$$
Both source banks end before box base $z$. Reserve $(V+1)\operatorname{downsetCap}(V,b)$ box-stage cells, a downset mask buffer, and sufficient ranking scratch. Assume the control word bound, $2^V(2^sB)(2^sD)$ fitting in a word, space fitting in a word, and depth $d+W+10$. The core routine stores every prefix zeta stage of $\lambda$ through width $V$, retains both source banks, and meets the suffix-setup core time budget. Below the mask buffer only the box-stage region may change.

natural_language_statement:
Write $S,\Omega,\Delta$ for machine space, word magnitude, and depth limits. Let $f,g$ be integer functions on subsets of $W$ coordinates, bounded respectively by $B_0,D_0$ on sets of size at most $c\le W$. Their complete partial suffix-zeta tables are stored. Fix $s\le W$, an interval of $V$ coordinates starting at $o$ with $o+V\le W$, prefixes $A_0,B_0'$ and cutoff $b\le V$, with $|A_0|+b,|B_0'|+b\le c$. Write $\iota(T)=o+T$ and
$$F(T)=(-1)^{|T|}Z_sf(A_0\cup\iota(T))\,Z_sg(B_0'\cup\iota(T)).$$
Here $Z_s$ sums over deletions in the last $s$ ambient coordinates.

Assume the ordered source, box, mask, and scratch regions, the stated address-space and address-word bounds, $S\le\Omega$, $2^V(2^sB_0)(2^sD_0)\le\Omega$, and $d+W+11\le\Delta$. The routine stores every forward partial zeta transform of $F$, for all $V+1$ stages and $|T|\le b$, in the box family. It retains both source families and preserves cells below the mask base outside the box family, within the specified setup time.

This prepares the signed suffix data used by sparse reporting queries.

natural_language_statement:
Embed $[V]$ into $[L]$ by $\iota(i)=o+i$, with $o+V\le L$. Fix $j,c\le L$, prefixes $P,Q\subseteq[L]$, a local query $X\subseteq[V]$, and a list $\mathcal U$ of subsets of $X$, all of cardinality $t$. Require $|P\cup\iota X|,|Q\cup\iota X|\le c$. Functions $f,g$ are bounded by $B,C$ on the source downset; memory stores their full suffix-zeta stages and the list masks below scratch $z$.

Assume the specified leaf procedures, $z+1+(L+1)^2+L+1\le S\le W$, $(L+1)2^{L+1},M,|\mathcal U|M\le W$ for $M=(2^jB)(2^jC)$, and $d+L+7\le D$. The routine returns
$$r=\sum_{U\in\mathcal U}(-1)^{|X\setminus U|}(Z_jf)(P\cup\iota(X\setminus U))(Z_jg)(Q\cup\iota(X\setminus U)).$$
List repetitions are counted. Time is $|\mathcal U|(T_{\rm leaf}(L)+100)+40$, and all memory below $z$ is preserved.

This evaluates the explicit suffix-leaf contribution to a reporting query.

natural_language_statement:
Let $\iota:[V]\hookrightarrow[W]$ be a coordinate shift, $c,s\le W$, and $b\le V$. Suppose both full suffix-stage banks for $f,g$ are stored on the $c$-downset, with $|f(T)|\le B$, $|g(T)|\le D$, and $|P_L|+b,|P_R|+b\le c$. Reserve a $\operatorname{downsetCap}(V,b)$-cell destination disjoint from both source banks, followed by a mask buffer and ranking scratch. Assume the specified space and control bounds, $(2^sB)(2^sD)$ fitting in a word, space fitting in a word, and depth $d+W+9$. The program fills every destination entry with
$$
\lambda(S)=(-1)^{|S|}Z_sf(P_L\cup\iota S)Z_sg(P_R\cup\iota S),\qquad |S|\le b.
$$
It meets the signed-suffix-table time budget. Below the mask buffer only the destination interval may change.

The result is the base table for prefix box transforms used in reporting.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.LightReportingSuffixTable.time_bound : ∀ {W V cut : Nat} (hV : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat V W) (hcut : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat cut V),
  @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (ThreeSum.LightReportingSuffixTable.time W V cut)
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
      (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 12000) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 12000)))
        (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
          (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid)))
          (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) W
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 3) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 3)))))
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (ThreeSum.SubsetAddress.downsetCap V cut)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $W,V,c\in\mathbb N$ with $c\le V\le W$. Let $D(V,c)=\sum_{r=0}^{c}\binom Vr$ be the number of subsets of the suffix ground set of size at most $c$. The concrete suffix-table construction has time budget

$$
T(W,V,c)\le12000(W+1)^3\bigl(D(V,c)+1\bigr).
$$

The table enumerates the cardinality layers at width $V$ and evaluates them against source transforms of width $W$. The estimate keeps the subset count tied to the shrinking suffix width while allowing polynomial overhead in the full width.

theorem_title: A counting-loop rule with summed iteration budgets
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.LightSharedReportingLoop.forSum : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {d : Nat} {σ : Light.State} {i : Nat} {hi : Light.Expr} {body : Light.Stmt}
  {T : Nat} {Q : Light.State → Prop} (I : Nat → Light.State → Prop) (n : Nat) (b : Nat → Nat)
  (start :
    I (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0)))
      {
        loc :=
          @Function.update.{1, 1} Nat (fun (a : Nat) => Int) instDecidableEqNat σ.loc i
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0))),
        mem := σ.mem })
  (round :
    ∀ (j : Nat) (σ : Light.State),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j n →
        @Eq.{1} Int (σ.loc i) (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt j) →
          I j σ →
            Light.Ends lim P d body σ (b j) fun (σ' : Light.State) =>
              And (@Eq.{1} Int (σ'.loc i) (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt j))
                (I
                  (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) j
                    (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
                  {
                    loc :=
                      @Function.update.{1, 1} Nat (fun (a : Nat) => Int) instDecidableEqNat σ'.loc i
                        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHAdd.{0} Int Int.instAdd)
                          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt j)
                          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 1) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 1)))),
                    mem := σ'.mem }))
  (done : ∀ (σ : Light.State), @Eq.{1} Int (σ.loc i) (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt n) → I n σ → Q σ)
  (bound :
    ∀ (j : Nat) (σ : Light.State),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat j n →
        @Eq.{1} Int (σ.loc i) (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt j) →
          I j σ →
            And (Light.Expr.Safe lim σ hi) (@Eq.{1} Int (Light.Expr.val σ hi) (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt n)))
  (hn : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt n) lim.word)
  (hT :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
          (∑ j ∈ Finset.range n,
            @HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
              (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) hi.cost (b j))
              (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 7) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 7))))
          hi.cost)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 5) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 5))))
      T),
  Light.Ends lim P d (Light.Stmt.for i hi body) σ T Q := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Fix a program, resource limits, and a call depth. Let a counting loop use counter register $i$, upper-bound expression $e$, body, and invariant predicates $I_j$, with $n\in\mathbb N$ iterations and individual body budgets $b_j\in\mathbb N$. Assume initialization establishes $I_0$; a body execution at counter $j<n$ costs at most $b_j$, preserves the counter, and establishes $I_{j+1}$ after incrementing it; and the terminal invariant implies $Q$. Assume $e$ is safe and equals $n$ at every invariant state through $j=n$, and $n$ fits in a word. If

$$\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\bigl(\operatorname{cost}(e)+b_j+7\bigr)+\operatorname{cost}(e)+5\le T,$$

the loop terminates within $T$ steps with $Q$. This preserves per-iteration cost information in traversal budgets.

theorem ThreeSum.LightSign.meets : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {pMain e d : Nat} {x : Int} {μ : Nat → Int}
  (hmain :
    @Eq.{1} (Option.{0} Light.Stmt)
      (@GetElem?.getElem?.{0, 0, 0} Light.Program Nat Light.Stmt
        (fun (as : List.{0} Light.Stmt) (i : Nat) => @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i (@List.length.{0} Light.Stmt as))
        (@List.instGetElem?NatLtLength.{0} Light.Stmt) P pMain)
      (@Option.some.{0} Light.Stmt ThreeSum.LightSign.body))
  (hw : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt lim.space) lim.word)

  (hvalue : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup x) lim.word),
  Light.Meets lim P pMain d
    (@List.cons.{0} Int x (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt e) (@List.nil.{0} Int))) μ
    (ThreeSum.LightSign.time e) fun (r : Int) (μ' : Nat → Int) =>
    And
      (@Eq.{1} Int r
        (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHMul.{0} Int Int.instMul)
          (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Int Nat Int
            (@instHPow.{0, 0} Int Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Int (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Int Int.instMonoid)))
            (@Neg.neg.{0} Int Int.instNegInt (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 1) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 1)))) e)
          x))
      (@Eq.{1} (Nat → Int) μ' μ) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $x\in\mathbb Z$, $e\in\mathbb N$, and $\mu$ be an arbitrary memory. Suppose a Light program contains the sign body, $e\le\mathrm{space}\le\mathrm{word}$, and $|x|\le\mathrm{word}$.

The call with arguments $(x,e)$ terminates within $20e+20$ steps and satisfies
$$
r=(-1)^e x,\qquad \nu=\mu.
$$
This supplies the signed scalar operation used in alternating-sum calculations, with an explicit cost linear in the exponent.

Let $f,g$ be integer subset functions on $[L]$, bounded in absolute value by $B,C$ on subsets of size at most $c\le L$. Let $j\le L$, and let $P,Q,T\subseteq[L]$ satisfy $|P\cup T|,|Q\cup T|\le c$. Memory stores all suffix-zeta stages of $f,g$ in two $(L+1)D_c$-cell areas below scratch $z$, where $D_c=\sum_{i=0}^{c}\binom Li$. Write $Z_jf$ for the transform processing the last $j$ coordinates.

Assume the specified union, lookup, and sign procedures, $z+1+(L+1)^2+L+1\le S\le W$, $(L+1)2^{L+1}\le W$, $(2^jB)(2^jC)\le W$, and $d+L+6\le D$. The return value is
$$r=(-1)^{|T|}(Z_jf)(P\cup T)(Z_jg)(Q\cup T).$$
Time is two union calls, two stage lookups, the sign call, and $160$ extra steps; memory below $z$ is unchanged.

This supplies the signed leaf values used by sparse reporting queries.

natural_language_statement:
Let $O$ be an integer list, let $v,e,g\in\mathbb N$, and let $\mu,\mu'$ be integer memories. The predicate $\mathcal P_\mu(v,e,g;O)$ means that some strictly increasing list of the same values as $O$, of length at most $|O|$, is stored at $v$, with the prescribed length and band-count headers and lower/upper endpoints at $e$. Suppose the memories agree throughout
$[v,v+|O|)$ and $[e,e+2+2|O|)$. Then

$$
\mathcal P_\mu(v,e,g;O)\Longrightarrow
\mathcal P_{\mu'}(v,e,g;O).
$$

The band-size parameter $g$ is any natural number.

This specifies exactly which regions must be retained when later machine stages modify other parts of memory.

Let an integer list $X$ of length $n$ be stored at source $s$, and let $g>0$ be the band width. Reserve, in order, the source, an $n$-cell values buffer, an endpoint region of $2+2n$ cells, and $n$ scratch cells. Assume space fits in a word, $n+g+2$ fits in a word, and $d+n+\operatorname{clog}_2n+3$ fits in depth. The installed program constructs a strictly increasing list $L$ with
$$
|L|\le n,\qquad z\in L\iff z\in X,
$$
stores $L$, and writes its length and band count in the endpoint header. For each nonempty consecutive $g$-band it stores the first and last values, returning the band count. Time is $\operatorname{Normalize.time}(n)+200n+300$.

Below scratch, memory outside the source, values, and endpoint regions is preserved. This prepares an original color class for interval-based owner enumeration.

Let $n$ original integers $f(j)$, with $|f(j)|\le U$, be stored before base $b$. Fix $g,p,m>0$ and an integer shift $|\delta|\le E$. Put $q=\lceil n/g\rceil$, $c=\min(n,g)$, and $z=b+6q+q(3m+1+2c)$. The packed layout reserves six header cells and one histogram, code, offset, cursor, and stable-index block per band.

Assume the specified band-step procedures, $S\le W$, $d+4<D$, the source-residue scratch bound at $z$, and word allowance $4U+8p+4E+4m+32+n+g+2\le W$. The completed memory satisfies
$$\text{every band }i<q\text{ has the exact codes, histogram, offsets, and stable buckets for }((f(ig+j)\bmod p)+\delta)\bmod m.$$
Its time is $q(T_{\rm step}+180)+20$, where $T_{\rm step}$ is the stated one-band budget, and memory below $b$ is unchanged.

This constructs all physical source fibers once for the original band partition.

Suppose memory $\mu$ stores the source-band pair catalog at address $b$ for integer value functions $f_L,f_R$, lengths $N_L,N_R$, band size $g$, initial modulus $p$, positive bucket modulus $m$, and integer shift. Let $i$ be any natural band index and $z$ the destination. Assume the catalog's declared end is at most $z$, $z+2\le S\le W$, and $N_L+N_R+i+6\le W$, where $S,W$ are the machine memory and word limits.

If procedure $q$ contains the fixed histogram-selector body, its call on $(b,i,z)$ at any depth ends within $400$ steps with memory $\nu$ satisfying

$$
\nu(z)=H_L(i),\qquad \nu(z+1)=H_R(i),\qquad
\forall a<z,\ \nu(a)=\mu(a).
$$

Here each $H$ is the selected histogram address, or the shared zero-histogram address when that side has no band $i$. This supports independent band selection with empty padding.

$$
k_L(x)=((x\bmod p)\bmod m),\qquad k_R(x)=((x\bmod p+\sigma)\bmod m).

Each band retains its header, codes, histogram, and physical-position fibers. An eight-cell pair header records the two band bases and counts, shared zero-bucket base, next address, and original lengths. The routine also stores $m+1$ zero cells, returns the next address, and preserves memory below $b$.

Its time is the two setup costs plus zero filling and $2000$ steps. This provides both source orientations for bandwise queries.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.LightSourceBandSetup.Procs.meets : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {d pMain : Nat} (C : ThreeSum.LightSourceBandSetup.Procs P pMain)
  {μ : Nat → Int} {src n g p m base U D : Nat} {shift : Int} (f : Nat → Int)
  (hw : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt lim.space) lim.word)
  (hd :
    @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) d
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 5) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 5))))
      lim.depth)
  (hg : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) g)
  (hp : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) p)
  (hm : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) m)
  (hsrc : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) src n) base)
  (hspace :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (ThreeSum.LightSourceResidues.space (ThreeSum.SourceBandLayout.work base n g m) p U D)
      lim.space)
  (hshift :
    @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup shift)
      (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt D))
  (hword :
    @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.LightSourceBandStep.word n g p m U D))
      lim.word)
  (hread :
    ∀ (j : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j n →
        @Eq.{1} Int (μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) src j)) (f j))
  (hvalues :
    ∀ (j : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j n →
        @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup (f j))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt U)),
  Light.Meets lim P pMain d
    (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt src)
      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt n)
        (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt g)
          (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt p)
            (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt m)
              (@List.cons.{0} Int shift
                (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt base) (@List.nil.{0} Int))))))))
    μ (ThreeSum.LightSourceBandSetup.time n g p m U D) fun (r : Int) (ν : Nat → Int) =>
    And (@Eq.{1} Int r (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.SourceBandLayout.work base n g m)))
      (And
        (∀ (i : Nat),
          @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i (ThreeSum.BandPartition.size n g) →
            ThreeSum.SourceBandData.At ν f base n g p m shift i)
        (Light.Kept μ ν base)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $f_0,\ldots,f_{n-1}$ be stored integers with $|f_j|\le U$, and let $g,p,m>0$ and $|\sigma|\le D$. Split the array into $K=0$ bands when $n=0$, otherwise $K=\lfloor(n-1)/g\rfloor+1$, each of length at most $g$. Assume the source ends before destination $b$, the installed band procedures and their residue workspace and word budgets fit, space fits in a word, and $d+5$ is below the depth limit. For each band $i$, the routine constructs a six-cell header, codes, histogram, and exact physical-position buckets for
$$
k_{i,j}=((f_{ig+j}\bmod p+\sigma)\bmod m),\qquad j<\min(g,n-ig).
$$
It returns $w=b+6K+K(3m+1+2\min(n,g))$, preserves memory below $b$, and meets the source-band setup time budget.

The retained fibers distinguish repeated source values by position.

natural_language_statement:
Let $f(0),\ldots,f(n-1)$ be stored below base $b$, with $|f(j)|\le U$. Fix $g,p,m>0$, $|\delta|\le E$, and a valid band $i<q=\lceil n/g\rceil$. Its start is $s_i=ig$ and length $\ell_i=\min(n,(i+1)g)-ig$. Put $c=\min(n,g)$, $\sigma=3m+1+2c$, $H_i=b+6q+i\sigma$, and $z=b+6q+q\sigma$.

Assume the specified source-bucket procedures, $S\le W$, $d+3<D$, $z+\max(\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+2,\lfloor\log_2(p+E+1)\rfloor+2)\le S$, and $4U+8p+4E+4m+32+n+g+2\le W$. The routine constructs codes
$$k_j=((f(s_i+j)\bmod p)+\delta)\bmod m\qquad(j<\ell_i),$$
their histogram, prefix offsets, and stable physical index buckets. Its six-field header stores the start, length, and four array addresses. It preserves memory below $H_i$ outside this header and takes at most $498c(\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+\lfloor\log_2(p+E+1)\rfloor+1)+233m+1533$ steps.

This constructs one packed source band from its original integer values.

formal_statement:

  (hsrc : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) src n) base)
  (hlast : @Eq.{1} Nat last (ThreeSum.BandPartition.stop n g i))
  (hspace :

      lim.space)
  (hshift :
    @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup shift)
      (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt D))
  (hword :
    @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.LightSourceBandStep.word n g p m U D))
      lim.word)
  (hread :
    ∀ (j : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j n →
        @Eq.{1} Int (μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) src j)) (f j))
  (hvalues :
    ∀ (j : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j n →
        @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup (f j))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt U)),
  Light.Ends lim P d (ThreeSum.LightSourceBandStep.tailBody pOriginal)
    {
      loc :=
        Light.frame
          (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt src)
            (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt n)
              (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt g)
                (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt p)
                  (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt m)
                    (@List.cons.{0} Int shift
                      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt base)
                        (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.SourceBandLayout.cap n g))
                          (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.BandPartition.size n g))
                            (@List.cons.{0} Int
                              (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.SourceBandLayout.data base n g))
                              (@List.cons.{0} Int
                                (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.SourceBandLayout.stride n g m))
                                (@List.cons.{0} Int
                                  (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.SourceBandLayout.work base n g m))
                                  (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt i)
                                    (@List.cons.{0} Int
                                      (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.BandPartition.start g i))
                                      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt last)
                                        (@List.nil.{0} Int)))))))))))))))),
      mem := μ }
    (ThreeSum.LightSourceBandStep.tailTime n g p m U D) fun (σ : Light.State) =>
    And (ThreeSum.SourceBandData.At σ.mem f base n g p m shift i)
      (Light.KeptBut μ σ.mem (ThreeSum.SourceBandLayout.hist base n g m i)
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) base
          (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 6) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 6))) i))
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 6) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 6)))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $g,p,m>0$, and let a stored length-$n$ integer array $f$ have $|f(j)|\le U$. Fix a valid band $i<\lceil n/g\rceil$, with start $s=ig$ and end $t=\min(n,(i+1)g)$, and a shift $|\delta|\le\Delta$. Start the tail body in its specified frame containing these endpoints and the defined packed-band pointers; the source ends before the band-record base.

Assume the original-source bucket procedures are present, their residue scratch fits space $S$, $S\le W$, $4U+8p+4\Delta+4m+n+g+34\le W$, and $d+3<D$. The output contains the six-field band header and exact code, histogram, and stable bucket arrays for
$$\kappa_j=((f(s+j)\bmod p)+\delta)\bmod m\qquad(j<t-s).$$
It preserves cells below this band's histogram except its six header cells. Its budget is
$$498\min(n,g)(\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+\lfloor\log_2(p+\Delta+1)\rfloor+1)+233m+1333.$$

This completes one packed source band while protecting earlier retained bands.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.LightSourceBucketBuild.Procs.meets : ∀ {lim : Light.Limits} {P : Light.Program} {d pMain : Nat} (C : ThreeSum.LightSourceBucketBuild.Procs P pMain)

  (hw : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt lim.space) lim.word)

    @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat

        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
      lim.depth)
  (hkeys : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) keys N) offsets)
  (hhist : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) hist M) offsets)
  (hsep : Light.Apart keys N hist M)
  (hoffsets :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) offsets M)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
      cursor)
  (hcursor : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) cursor M) flat)
  (hspace : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) flat N) lim.space)
  (hkey : ∀ (i : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i N → @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (key i) M)
  (hread :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i N →
        @Eq.{1} Int (μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) keys i))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (key i))),
  Light.Meets lim P pMain d
    (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt keys)
      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt hist)
        (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt offsets)
          (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt cursor)
            (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt flat)
              (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt N)
                (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt M) (@List.nil.{0} Int))))))))
    μ (ThreeSum.LightSourceBucketBuild.time N M) fun (x : Int) (ν : Nat → Int) =>
    And (ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.Stored ν key N M offsets flat)
      (And
        (∀ (r : Nat),
          @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat r M →
            @Eq.{1} Int (ν (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) hist r))
              (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.LightHistogram.count key r N)))
        (And (Light.Kept μ ν hist)
          (Light.SameOutside μ ν hist
            (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHSub.{0} Nat instSubNat)
              (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) flat N) hist)))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let memory store natural labels $\kappa_i<M$ for $i<N$ at base $k$. Choose histogram, offset, cursor, and flat-index bases $h,o,c,f$. The key and histogram intervals are disjoint, and
$$k+N\le o,\quad h+M\le o,\quad o+M+1\le c,\quad c+M\le f,\quad f+N\le S\le B.$$
Assume $d+1<D$ and the specified histogram and bucket-building procedures. Within $144N+133M+287$ steps, the routine constructs
$$\nu(h+r)=\#\{i<N:\kappa_i=r\},\qquad\nu(o+r)=\#\{i<N:\kappa_i<r\},$$
for $r<M$ and $r\le M$, respectively. The flat array stores each index $i$ at position $\#\{j<N:\kappa_j<\kappa_i\}+\#\{j<i:\kappa_j=\kappa_i\}$, preserving source order within every bucket. Only addresses in $[h,f+N)$ may change.

This derives exact contiguous bucket layouts from the stored codes themselves.

\nu(f+O(k_i)+|\{j<i:k_j=k_i\}|)=i\ (i<N).

Memory below $o$ and outside $[o,f+N)$ is preserved. These equations give the exact stored-bucket representation used by source scans and joins.

$$

Let memory $\mu$ contain the stored bucket representation of $N$ keys, each below $M$, with offset-array base $o$ and flat-index base $f$. Let $r<M$, let $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}$, and let $z$ be the two-cell output base. Assume $o+M+1\le z$, $f+N\le z$, $z+2\le S$, and $S\le W$, where $S,W$ are the machine space and word bounds. $$
\nu(z)=f+O(r),\qquad\nu(z+1)=\varepsilon C(r),\qquad\nu(a)=\mu(a)\quad(a\notin[z,z+2)),

  (hM : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) M)
  (hkeys : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) keys N) base)
  (hspace : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (ThreeSum.LightSourceBucketSetup.next base N M) lim.space)
  (hkey : ∀ (i : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i N → @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (key i) M)
  (hread :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i N →
        @Eq.{1} Int (μ (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) keys i))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (key i))),
  Light.Meets lim P pMain d
    (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt keys)
      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt N)
        (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt M)
          (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt base) (@List.nil.{0} Int)))))
    μ (ThreeSum.LightSourceBucketSetup.time N M) fun (r : Int) (ν : Nat → Int) =>
    And (@Eq.{1} Int r (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.LightSourceBucketSetup.next base N M)))
      (And
        (ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.Stored ν key N M (ThreeSum.LightSourceBucketSetup.offsets base M)
          (ThreeSum.LightSourceBucketSetup.flat base M))
        (And
          (∀ (j : Nat),
            @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j M →
              @Eq.{1} Int
                (ν
                  (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)

natural_language_statement:
Let $N$ stored natural keys $k_i$ lie below a positive residue count $M$, and let the key array end by free address $f$. Assume $f+3M+1+N$ fits in space, space fits in a word, and $d+2$ is below the depth limit. The installed bucket-setup program computes its own histogram, offsets, cursors, and flat-index addresses. It returns
$$
r=f+3M+1+N,\qquad \mu'(f+j)=|\{i<N:k_i=j\}|\quad(j<M).
$$
The offset array starts at $f+M$ and the flat original-index array at $f+3M+1$; together they satisfy the exact bucket-storage contract. Memory below $f$ is preserved, and time is the bucket-builder budget plus $200$.

This supplies reusable physical residue fibers for source and wanted data.

  (hp :

        (fun (as : List.{0} Light.Stmt) (i : Nat) => @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i (@List.length.{0} Light.Stmt as))
        (@List.instGetElem?NatLtLength.{0} Light.Stmt) P p)
      (@Option.some.{0} Light.Stmt ThreeSum.LightSourceControlsMax.body))
  (μ : Nat → Int)
  (hword : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (@Max.max.{0} Nat Nat.instMax a b)) lim.word),
  Light.Meets lim P p d
    (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt a)
      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt b) (@List.nil.{0} Int)))
    μ (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 40) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 40))) fun (r : Int) (ν : Nat → Int) =>
    And (@Eq.{1} Int r (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (@Max.max.{0} Nat Nat.instMax a b))) (@Eq.{1} (Nat → Int) ν μ) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $a,b\in\mathbb N$ and let a program contain the fixed two-argument maximum procedure at index $p$. If its word-magnitude limit is at least $\max(a,b)$, then for every initial integer memory $\mu$ and every call depth $d$, the procedure satisfies

$$
P_p(a,b;\mu)\text{ returns }\max(a,b)
\text{ within }40\text{ steps, with final memory }\mu.
$$

The two inputs may be zero or equal. There is no memory-space assumption because this procedure only compares and assigns local variables.

The contract supplies the scalar maximum operation used to combine independently computed shared-bank dimensions.

        (@List.instGetElem?NatLtLength.{0} Light.Stmt) P pMax)
      (@Option.some.{0} Light.Stmt ThreeSum.LightSourceControlsMax.body))
  (μ : Nat → Int) (hd : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat d lim.depth)
  (hword :
    @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt
      (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.SourceControlLayout.word J W K S logP logE)) lim.word),
  Light.Meets lim P pMain d
    (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt J)
      (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt W)
        (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt K)
          (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt S)
            (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt logP)
              (@List.cons.{0} Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt logE) (@List.nil.{0} Int)))))))
    μ (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1000) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1000))) fun (r : Int) (ν : Nat → Int) =>
    And (@Eq.{1} Int r (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt (ThreeSum.SourceControlLayout.span J W K S logP logE)))
      (@Eq.{1} (Nat → Int) ν μ) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $J,W,K,S,\ell_P,\ell_E$ be natural control parameters for block count, width, capacity, occurrence count and two logarithmic bounds. Define
$$
A=\max\{(W+1)^2+W+1,\ell_E+2,\ell_P+5,J+1\},\qquad
D=5K+2W+4+2(W+1)K,
$$
and $V=SD+K+W+2+A$. Suppose a Light program contains the span routine and its maximum subroutine, the current depth $d$ is below the call-depth limit, and the word limit is at least
$V+D+J+W+K+S+\ell_P+\ell_E+(W+1)^2+30$.

For any initial memory $\mu$, the call with these six parameters terminates within $1000$ steps and satisfies
$$
r=V,\qquad \nu=\mu.
$$
This certifies the arithmetic routine that determines the exact extent of the shared source bank.

natural_language_statement:
Fix $p>0$, $h\le L$, and $J$ selected occurrences $s_j<M$, each mapped to a candidate $c(s_j)<K$. Memory stores these selectors, two coefficient rows per occurrence bounded by $U$, two $K\times p$ count tables bounded by $V$, and $n$ masks $q_i<2^{JL}$. For each block, a mask orientation passes when its block has $h$ set bits and its one-hot hash residue indexes a count at most the cap. Define $F_L(q)$ as the product of these block flags, and $F_R(q)$ using the swapped coefficients and right counts.

All inputs end before $a$; require $a+2n+2\le b$, $b+JL\le r$, $r+2\le w$, the specified single-mask scratch and word budgets, $S\le W$, and $d+JL+4\le D$. The stated procedures write
$$\nu(a+i)=F_L(q_i),\qquad\nu(a+n+i)=F_R(q_i)\quad(i<n)$$
within $n(T_{\mathrm{mask}}(J,L,U)+200)+10$ steps. Below $b$, only the $2n+2$-cell output/work interval may change.

This retains both endpoint decisions independently for later bucket selection.

natural_language_statement:
Let $c,r,n,b\in\mathbb N$ denote a measured cardinality, required cardinality, bucket count, and cap. Suppose procedure $p$ contains the fixed flag-test body and the machine word-magnitude limit is at least $c+r+n+b+2$. For any initial integer memory $\mu$ and call depth, it returns within $25$ steps with

$$
\mathrm{result}=\begin{cases}
1,&c=r\text{ and }n\le b,\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad \mathrm{final\ memory}=\mu.
$$

All four parameters may be zero.

This contract implements the two independent retention conditions used in the source construction: the prescribed subset cardinality and a sufficiently small hash bucket.

Let $x_i=\mu(s+i)$, $i<n$, satisfy $|x_i|\le U$. Fix positive moduli $p,m$ and an integer shift $\delta$ with $|\delta|\le E$. The program contains the source-residue and histogram procedures. $$f+\max\{\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+2,\lfloor\log_2(p+E+1)\rfloor+2\}\le S,\qquad4U+8p+4E+4m+32\le W.$$
Writing $k_i=((x_i\bmod p)+\delta)\bmod m$, the routine produces
$$\nu(b+i)=k_i,\qquad\nu(a+r)=\#\{i<n:k_i=r\}\quad(r<m).$$
It takes at most $n(R_U+R_{p+E}+124)+13m+63$ steps, with $R_z=43(\lfloor\log_2(z+1)\rfloor+1)+34$, and preserves memory below $b$ outside the histogram.

Let $m<2^{JL}$ be a global mask, with $h\le L$ and positive modulus $p$. Memory contains $J$ selected occurrence indices, their valid candidate indices, coefficient rows bounded by $U$, and two candidate bucket-count tables bounded by $V$. These inputs and the two-cell output end before bit scratch; reserve $JL$ bit cells, two row cells, and the specified arithmetic scratch in order. Assume the program's space and word budgets fit, space fits in a word, and $d+JL+3$ fits in depth. For each block, let $F^L_j$ test cardinality $h$ and the left bucket cap, and let $F^R_j$ use swapped coefficients and the right table. The program writes
$$
\mu'(z)=\prod_{j<J}F^L_j,\qquad \mu'(z+1)=\prod_{j<J}F^R_j.
$$
It satisfies the bit-decoding-plus-trimming time budget and preserves memory below bit scratch outside these two output cells.

This constructs both endpoint flags from the actual global mask.
