natural_language_statement:
Let $N,J$ be natural numbers and $m\ge1$ a radix. Assume the specified digit decoder and division procedure are available. For output base $a$, scratch base $w$, and machine limits $S,B,D$, require
$$a+NJ\le w,\quad w+\lfloor\log_2(N+1)\rfloor+2\le S\le B,\quad4N+4m+4J+32\le B,\quad d+2<D.$$
The constructor writes the last $J$ base-$m$ digits of each index in most-significant-first order:
$$\nu(a+iJ+j)=\left\lfloor\frac{i}{m^{J-1-j}}\right\rfloor\bmod m\qquad(i<N,\ j<J).$$
It preserves all cells below $a$ and terminates within
$$N\bigl[J(100\lfloor\log_2(N+1)\rfloor+300)+180\bigr]+10$$
steps.

This supplies the physical occurrence-index rows used by block construction, with fixed-width truncation valid even when $N$ exceeds $m^J$.

          (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) N
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1)))))

          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1)))))
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
        (Nat.log (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2)))
          (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) N
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1)))))

natural_language_statement:
Let $N,J\in\mathbb N$ be the number of bank indices and the number of radix digits stored for each index. Let $T(N,J)$ be the defined time budget of the occurrence-array routine, which invokes the logarithmic quotient-based decoder once for each row. Then

$$T(N,J)\le300(N+1)(J+1)\bigl(\log_2^{\mathrm{nat}}(N+1)+2\bigr),$$

where $\log_2^{\mathrm{nat}}$ is the natural-number floor logarithm. This bound charges all decoded coordinates and loop overhead, including the zero-size cases, to the source-catalog construction.

natural_language_statement:
Fix $J$ blocks of width $L$, required row size $h\le L$, modulus $p>0$, and $n$ masks below $2^{JL}$. Memory stores valid block selections into $M$ pairs of weight rows, a valid map-to-candidate table into $K$ histogram pairs, weights bounded by $U$, and histogram entries bounded by $V$. All inputs precede two coefficient arrays of length $JL$, then two raw arrays of length $n$, a flag area of length $2n+2$, $JL$ bit cells, two row-result cells, and scratch $z$, in that order.

Assume the specified procedures, $S\le W$, $d+JL+5\le D$, and the defined source-preparation space and word budgets fit $S,W$. For mask $m_i$, let $H_\ell(m_i)$ be the one-hot sum with coefficients $p^jw_{\mathrm{bit}}(\mathrm{sel}(j),a)$, and let $H_r$ interchange the two weight rows. The output satisfies
$$\mathrm{raw}_\ell[i]=H_\ell(m_i),\quad\mathrm{raw}_r[i]=H_r(m_i),\quad\mathrm{flags}_\ell[i]=F_\ell(m_i),\quad\mathrm{flags}_r[i]=F_r(m_i).$$
Each flag requires row cardinality $h$ and the corresponding bucket cap in every block. Execution meets the defined preparation time budget and preserves memory below the first coefficient array.

This constructs endpoint arithmetic and trimming decisions together.

natural_language_statement:
Let $p,m>0$, let $\delta\in\mathbb Z$ satisfy $|\delta|\le D_0$, and let integer memory $\mu$ have $|\mu(s+i)|\le U$ for $i<n$. Source and destination segments $[s,s+n)$ and $[z,z+n)$ are disjoint and end at or before work base $f$. Define $R_v=43(\lfloor\log_2(v+1)\rfloor+1)+34$. For machine limits $S,W,D$, assume $S\le W$, $d<D$,
$f+\max\{\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+2,\lfloor\log_2(p+D_0+1)\rfloor+2\}\le S$, and $4U+8p+4D_0+4m+32\le W$. With the specified Euclidean-remainder helper, the source-residue body on $(s,z,n,p,m,f,\delta)$ finishes within $n(R_U+R_{p+D_0}+100)+6$ steps and gives

$$
\mu'(z+i)=\bigl(\mu(s+i)\bmod p+\delta\bigr)\bmod m\quad(i<n).
$$

Memory below $f$ outside the destination is preserved. This constructs the exact shifted source codes used by histogram and join stages.

natural_language_statement:
Let $b_i\in\{0,1\}$ and $w_0(i),w_1(i)\le U$ for $i<L$, with $h\le L$ and modulus $p>0$. Let bucket tables $H_L,H_R:[p]\to\mathbb N$ be bounded by $V$, and let $c$ be the trimming cap. Suppose memory stores the bit row, both weight rows, and both bucket tables in segments ending at or before $f$, with $z+2\le f$. Assume $S\le W$, $d<D$, $f+\lfloor\log_2(LU+1)\rfloor+5\le S$, and $(L+1)(U+1)+4LU+4p+2L+V+c+19\le W$. If $P$ contains the row-flag body and its scan, remainder, and flag-test helpers, it stores

$$
\begin{aligned}
\nu(z)&=\mathbf1_{\sum b_i=h\,\land\,H_L((\sum w_{b_i}(i))\bmod p)\le c},\\
\nu(z+1)&=\mathbf1_{\sum b_i=h\,\land\,H_R((\sum w_{1-b_i}(i))\bmod p)\le c}.
\end{aligned}
$$

All sums range over $i<L$. The time is at most $150L+2R_{LU}+310$, where $R_v=43(\lfloor\log_2(v+1)\rfloor+1)+34$; memory below $f$ outside the two outputs is preserved. This constructs separate endpoint-retention flags.

natural_language_statement:
Let $b_i\in\{0,1\}$ and $w_0(i),w_1(i)\le U$ be natural numbers for $i<L$. Suppose memory $\mu$ stores these three arrays at bases $s,s_0,s_1$. Let $z$ be the output base and $S,W$ the machine space and word bounds. Assume $s+L,s_0+L,s_1+L,z+3\le S\le W$ and $(L+1)(U+1)+1\le W$. If the called procedure is the specified row scan, execution on $(s,s_0,s_1,L,z)$ at any depth finishes within $150L+100$ steps and stores

$$
\bigl[\nu(z),\nu(z+1),\nu(z+2)\bigr]
=\left[\sum_{i<L}b_i,\ \sum_{i<L}w_{b_i}(i),\ \sum_{i<L}w_{1-b_i}(i)\right].
$$

Every cell outside $[z,z+3)$ is preserved. This computes a row's cardinality and both one-hot hash sums in one traversal.

natural_language_statement:
Consider $J$ bit rows of length $L$, a required weight $h\le L$, and a positive modulus $p$. Each row selects one of $M$ pairs of weight rows, whose entries are at most $U$; that selection chooses one of $K$ left and right histograms, bounded by $V$. Assume memory stores these arrays exactly, all selection indices are valid, and all bits are Boolean. Their reserved intervals end before the two-cell row-result buffer at $r$; the final two-cell output ends by $r$, and scratch starts at $f\ge r+2$. Require $S\le W$, $d+1<D$, $f+\lfloor\log_2(LU+1)\rfloor+5\le S$, and $(L+1)(U+1)+4LU+4p+2L+V+\mathrm{cap}+19\le W$.

Let $F_j^\ell,F_j^r$ be the row flags: the row has $h$ ones and its corresponding residue bucket contains at most $\mathrm{cap}$ elements, with the two weight rows interchanged for the right flag. The specified procedures write
$$\nu(a)=\prod_{j<J}F_j^\ell,\qquad\nu(a+1)=\prod_{j<J}F_j^r.$$
They take at most $J(150L+2R_{LU}+560)+100$ steps, where $R_z=43(\lfloor\log_2(z+1)\rfloor+1)+34$, and preserve memory below $r$ outside the output.

The products implement simultaneous acceptance over every block.

Fix a program containing the recursive rank procedure. Memory $\mu$ stores Pascal coefficients through width $w$ in a rectangular $(w+1)^2$ table at $t$, and powers $2^i$ for $i\le w$ at $p$. For memory and word limits $S,W$, assume $t+(w+1)^2\le S$, $p+w+1\le S$, $S\le W$, and $2^{w+1}\le W$. Let $L\le w$ and let $m<2^L$ have exactly $k$ selected bits. $$r=\operatorname{layerRank}(L,k,m),\qquad\mu'=\mu,\qquad\text{cost}\le100L+30.$$

This gives an executable compact address calculation with cost linear in mask width.

$$
r=N,\qquad \nu(D+i)=\operatorname{enumerateLayer}(L,k)_i\quad(i<N),\qquad
\nu(F+j)=2^j\quad(j\le L).
$$
The output lists exactly the masks with $k$ set bits in recursive lower-half-first order. Cells below $F$ outside $[D,D+N)$ are preserved.

This gives a complete layer enumerator with its lookup table constructed internally.

natural_language_statement:
Let $L,k,w$ be natural numbers with $L,k\le w$. Suppose integer memory $\mu$ contains the rectangular Pascal table at base $a$: for all $i,j\le w$, $\mu(a+i(w+1)+j)=\binom{i}{j}$. For machine space and word bounds $S,W$, assume $a+(w+1)^2\le S\le W$ and $(w+1)2^{w+1}\le W$. If the called procedure in $P$ is the offset-scan body, execution on $(a,L,k,w)$ at any depth takes at most $30k+20$ steps and returns

$$
r=\operatorname{layerOffset}(L,k)=\sum_{j<k}\binom Lj,\qquad \mu'=\mu.
$$

The offset locates the start of the cardinality-$k$ layer in a compact enumeration ordered by subset size.

natural_language_statement:
Let $m$ be an $L$-bit natural mask with exactly $k$ set bits. Suppose the installed procedures implement Pascal construction, powers of two, and subset ranking. From scratch base $f$, reserve $(L+1)^2+(L+1)$ cells; assume space fits in a word, $2^{L+1}$ fits in a word, and $d+L+3$ fits in the depth limit. The complete setup-and-rank routine returns
$$
r=\operatorname{layerRank}(L,k,m).
$$
It also leaves a correct Pascal table at $f$ and the powers $2^0,\ldots,2^L$ immediately after that table, preserving all memory below $f$. Its time budget is the sum of table construction, power construction, ranking, and $60$ steps.

Thus ranking requires no preexisting lookup tables.

natural_language_statement:
Let $k,v:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ describe keys and validity flags stored in length-$n$ arrays at $K,F$, with $k(i)<p$ for $i<n$. Suppose both input intervals and the length-$p$ destination at $D$ fit within $\mathrm{space}\le\mathrm{word}$; each input interval is disjoint from the destination; and $1\le\mathrm{word}$. Assume the support and fill bodies are present and $d<\mathrm{depth}$.

The call with $(K,F,D,n,p)$ terminates within $40n+13p+22$ steps and gives
$$
\nu(D+r)=\mathbf1_{\{\exists i<n:\ v(i)=1\ \land\ k(i)=r\}}\quad(r<p),
$$
preserving all memory outside $[D,D+p)$.

Flags are enabled by equality to one. Repeated enabled keys contribute a single support bit.

natural_language_statement:
Let $B\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $B\ge2$, and let $\sigma$ be a machine state whose every local variable has absolute value at most $B$. Let $e$ be an expression built from natural literals at most $B$, local variables, and addition, subtraction, or multiplication, with no memory loads. Write $c(e)$ for its syntax-tree cost, charging one for each leaf and operation. If the machine's word-magnitude limit is $W$ and $B^{c(e)}\le W$, then

$$
e\text{ is safe to evaluate in }\sigma\text{ under the machine limits}.
$$

Safety includes the bounds required for all intermediate arithmetic expressions.

This gives a reusable structural check for the fixed scalar formulas implementing the cubic switch.

natural_language_statement:
Let natural right keys $r_j<M$ for $j<N_R$ and left keys $\ell_i<M$ for $i<n$. Suppose integer memory $\mu$ stores the left-key array at $a$ and the exact right-index bucket representation at offset and flat bases $o,f$. Let $z$ be the pair-output base, with $a+n,o+M+1,f+N_R\le z$. Put $C=\sum_{i<n}|\{j<N_R:r_j=\ell_i\}|$. Assume $z+2C\le S\le W$, $d+n+2\le D$, and that $P$ contains the recursive join and wanted-row copier. Execution on $(a,o,f,n,N_R,M,z)$ finishes within $120C+270n+50$ steps and yields

$$
r=C,\qquad \nu[z:z+2C]=\operatorname{flatten}\bigl([(i,j):i<n,\ j\text{ in stored bucket }\ell_i]\bigr).
$$

Rows follow left-index order and each row follows bucket order. Memory below $z$ is preserved. This enumerates exactly the matching physical index pairs.

$$

Memory outside $[z+2p,z+2(p+n))$ is preserved. This appends a fixed left label paired with every entry of a selected source bucket.

Let stored integer arrays $L_i$ ($i<N_L$) and $R_j$ ($j<N_R$) have absolute values at most $U$, let $M>0$, and let the integer shift satisfy $|s|\le\Delta$. Both input arrays end before free address $f$. Define
$$\mathcal P=\{(i,j):i<N_L,\ j<N_R,\ M\mid L_i+s-R_j\},\qquad H=|\mathcal P|,$$
and $b=f+N_L+2N_R+3M+5$. Assume $S\le W$, $4U+12M+4\Delta+32\le W$, $d+N_L+5\le D$, and enough space for both $[b,b+2H)$ and the residue scratch ending at $b+\max(\lfloor\log_2(U+1)\rfloor+2,\lfloor\log_2(M+\Delta+1)\rfloor+2)$.

The fixed setup program returns $f$, writes the header $[H,b,b+2H,s]$, and stores a duplicate-free list of exactly the pairs in $\mathcal P$ at $b$. It preserves all cells below $f$ and meets its defined setup budget.

This constructs the physical wanted-pair list directly from the signed input arrays.

natural_language_statement:
Let $L,k$ be natural numbers and let the radix satisfy $p\ge1$. The output at $a$ reserves $2L$ cells, followed by scratch at $f\ge a+2L$. Assume the specified power-table and strided digit-decoding procedures, and resource limits satisfying $S\le W$, $d+2<D$, $f+2L+1\le S$, and $4(k+p^{2L+1}+p+2L+5)\le W$.

For $i<L$, define the length-$2L$ digit $d_j=\lfloor k/p^{2L-1-j}\rfloor\bmod p$. The routine writes
$$\nu(a+i)=d_{2i},\qquad\nu(a+L+i)=d_{2i+1},\qquad\nu(f+e)=p^e\ (e\le2L).$$
Its step bound is $2L(40(k+1)+200)+34L+157$, and it preserves memory below $f$ outside the output interval.

This realizes the interleaved encoding of the two weight coordinates as two contiguous arrays.

Suppose a Light program contains the row-gather body and its copy subroutine. Let a table of $N$ rows of width $W$ start at $A$, and let $s_i<N$, $i<R$, be selection indices stored at $I$. Assume $I+R,A+NW\le D$, $D+RW\le\mathrm{space}\le\mathrm{word}$, $N+R+W+1\le\mathrm{word}$, and $d<\mathrm{depth}$.

The call with $(I,A,D,R,W)$ terminates within $R(16W+106)+6$ steps and satisfies
$$
\nu(D+iW+j)=\mu(A+s_iW+j)\quad(i<R,\ j<W),
$$
while preserving memory outside $[D,D+RW)$.

This copies the selected coefficient rows in occurrence order, including repeated selections.

Let $p\ge1$ and let $w,k,a,s,n,z,b\in\mathbb N$. Suppose memory $\mu$ stores $p^e$ at $b+e$ for every $e\le w$, and $a+si<w$ for every $i<n$. The power-table segment $[b,b+w+1)$ and output segment $[z,z+n)$ are disjoint and within space $S\le W$. Assume $4(k+p^{w+1}+p+w+a+s+2)\le W$ and $d+1<D$. If $P$ contains the row extractor, radix-digit helper, and small divider, execution on $(w,p,k,b,a,s,z,n)$ takes at most $n(40(k+1)+200)+6$ steps and stores

$$
\mu'(z+i)=\left\lfloor\frac{k}{p^{w-1-(a+si)}}\right\rfloor\bmod p\quad(i<n).
$$

Every cell outside the output row is preserved. This reads selected coordinates in the most-significant-first coefficient enumeration.

            powers →

Let $w:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and natural parameters $L,k,B,a,z,p,U,d$ be given. Assume $L\le B$, $k\le B+1$, $a+\sum_{i<L}w(i)\le U$, and $z+\binom Lk\le p$. Memory stores $w(i)$ at $p+i$ for $i<B$. For space, word, and depth bounds $S,W,D$, assume $S\le W$, $p+B+1\le S$, $U\le W$, and $d+L\le D$. Suppose the called procedure is the same self-recursive body as subset enumeration. Execution produces

$$
\mathrm{result}=\binom Lk,\qquad\nu[z:]=\left[a+\sum_{i\in A}w(i): A\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\},\ |A|=k\right]
$$

in the defined recursive order, within $150\operatorname{enumerationWork}(L,k)$ steps. It preserves every cell outside the output block. Equal subset sums remain separate list entries, so the output count depends only on the coordinate count and cardinality.

$$r=sC(q)-\sum_{i<s}C(j_i).$$

This certifies the weighted score with all modular counts computed from the original signed arrays.

natural_language_statement:
Let integer arrays $A,B,C$ of lengths $n_A,n_B,n_C\le N\le S$ and an array of $s$ distinct primes $p_i$ be stored wholly below free address $f$. Let $0<q\le M$ and $qp_i\le M$. Assume $S\le W$, $f+\lfloor\log_2(M+1)\rfloor+2\le S$, $(s+1)N^3+8M+16\le W$, and $d+1<D$. Suppose $P$ contains the weighted-score and joint-modulus bodies, the Euclidean-remainder helper, and a backend which, for every $0<v\le M$ and every memory agreeing with the initial memory below $f$, counts all triples with $v\mid C_k-B_j-A_i$ within $T_c$ steps at depth $d+1$, preserving that prefix. The score procedure returns

$$
r=\sum_{i<n_A,j<n_B,k<n_C}\mathbf1_{q\mid\Delta_{ijk}}
|\{u<s:p_u\nmid\Delta_{ijk}\}|,
\quad\Delta_{ijk}=C_k-B_j-A_i.
$$

It preserves memory below $f$ and takes at most $T_c+s(T_c+R_M+140)+100$ steps, where $R_M=43(\lfloor\log_2(M+1)\rfloor+1)+34$.

This composes exact counting calls into the auxiliary-prime score.

natural_language_statement:
Let $f$ be an integer function on subsets of $[L]$, with $|f(T)|\le U$ for $|T|\le c$, and fix a coordinate $a\in[L]$. A list $\mathcal M$ contains valid masks of one cardinality $k\le c$, with repetitions permitted. Set $C=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(c,L)}\binom Lj$. The source table, destination table, and mask list end below scratch $z$; the destination interval is disjoint from both source and masks. Memory stores $f$ at the source and $\mathcal M$ at the mask base.

For the specified cell and setup procedures, require $z+(L+1)^2+L+1\le S\le W$, $(L+1)2^{L+1},2U\le W$, and $d+L+5\le D$. The resulting destination table represents
$$g(T)=\begin{cases}f(T)+f(T\setminus\{a\}),&\operatorname{mask}(T)\in\mathcal M,\ a\in T,\\f(T),&\operatorname{mask}(T)\in\mathcal M,\ a\notin T,\\\mu(\mathrm{dst}+\operatorname{rank}(T)),&\operatorname{mask}(T)\notin\mathcal M.\end{cases}$$
Execution takes $|\mathcal M|(T_{\rm cell}(L)+40)+10$ steps, where $T_{\rm cell}$ is the defined zeta-cell budget, and preserves memory below $z$ outside the destination.

This certifies partial batches of a compact zeta pass.

  (hw : @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt lim.space) lim.word)
  (hsrc :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat

  (hdst :

natural_language_statement:
Let $f$ be an integer function on subsets of $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$, with $|f(T)|\le U$ whenever $|T|\le c$. A source table stores $f(T)$ at compact address $s+\rho(T)$. Fix $A$ with $|A|\le c$ and a coordinate $a<L$. Both source and destination tables of capacity $K=\sum_{i\le\min(c,L)}\binom Li$ end before scratch $w$.

Assume the specified setup, offset, mask-erasure, and rank procedures, and
$$w+(L+1)^2+(L+1)\le S\le W,\quad(L+1)2^{L+1}\le W,\quad2U\le W,\quad d+L+4\le D.$$
Within $23L^2+516L+534$ steps, the procedure writes
$$\nu(t+\rho(A))=\begin{cases}f(A)+f(A\setminus\{a\}),&a\in A,\\f(A),&a\notin A.\end{cases}$$
Every other cell below $w$ is preserved.

This realizes a single subset-zeta addition using computed compact addresses.

natural_language_statement:
Let $f$ be an integer function on subsets of $[L]$, bounded by $U$ in absolute value on the downset $|T|\le c\le L$, and fix $a\in[L]$. Put $C=\sum_{j=0}^{c}\binom Lj$. Disjoint source and destination tables of $C$ cells end below mask buffer $b$, and $b+C\le z$, where $z$ is scratch. Memory initially stores the source table for $f$.

Assume the specified enumeration and zeta-cell procedures, $z+(L+1)^2+L+1\le S\le W$, $(L+1)2^{L+1},2U\le W$, and $d+L+6\le D$. The output table represents
$$g(T)=\begin{cases}f(T)+f(T\setminus\{a\}),&a\in T,\\f(T),&a\notin T.\end{cases}$$
The time bound is $(c+1)((800(L+1)+2100(L+1)^2)(C+1)+80)+20$. Memory below $b$ outside the destination is preserved.

This executes one complete coordinate pass using cardinality layers of the compact downset.

natural_language_statement:
Let $L,c\in\mathbb N$ with $c\le L$, and let

$$D(L,c)=\sum_{r=0}^{c}\binom{L}{r}$$

be the number of subsets of an $L$-element ground set having cardinality at most $c$. The defined budget $T_{\zeta}(L,c)$ for one coordinate pass of the zeta-transform routine satisfies

$$T_{\zeta}(L,c)\le4000(L+1)^3\bigl(D(L,c)+1\bigr).$$

This charges the cardinality-layer enumeration and batch updates within a pass to the size of the stored downset, with a polynomial factor in the ground-set width.

natural_language_statement:
Let $f$ be integer valued on subsets of $[L]$, with $|f(S)|\le U$ for $|S|\le c\le L$. Write $D_c=\sum_{i\le c}\binom Li$. Suppose its rank-indexed downset table is stored at $b$, followed by space for $L$ further stages, a $D_c$-cell mask buffer, and Pascal/ranking scratch. Assume the specified procedures are installed, the layout fits, space fits in a word, both $(L+1)2^{L+1}$ and $2^LU$ fit in a word, and depth $d+L+7$ is available. The routine stores
$$
\mu'(b+jD_c+\operatorname{rank}S)=\sum_{T\subseteq S\cap E_j}f((S\setminus E_j)\cup T)
\quad(j\le L,\ |S|\le c),
$$
where $E_j$ comprises the last $j$ coordinates. Its budget is $\operatorname{sizeTime}(L)+L(\operatorname{passTime}(L,c)+80)+80$. Below the mask buffer, only the stage region changes.

Retaining intermediate stages supplies later suffix queries with the required transform level.

$$D(L,c)=\sum_{r=0}^{c}\binom{L}{r}$$
for the number of masks of cardinality at most $c$. This bounds the source-stage preprocessing used to answer queries with a forced prefix and a remaining suffix.

natural_language_statement:
For arbitrary natural numbers $c$ and $r$,

$$
c^r\le \binom{cr}{r}.
$$

The right side counts all subsets of size $r$ in a set of $cr$ positions. The left side counts choices of one position in each of $r$ labeled blocks, each containing $c$ positions. This exact finite estimate supplies a lower bound for the number of local subset outputs without using asymptotic factorial estimates.

$$q^{2L}\le320(2h+1)\,\#\{w:w\text{ covers }(u,v)\}.$$

  (B : Nat) (w : ThreeSum.LocalHashMoments.Weight.{u_1} L K) (target : Prod.{u_1, u_1} K K),
  @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@ThreeSum.LocalHashMoments.hitCount.{u_1} K inst inst_1 inst_2 L h B w target)
    (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
      (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) B
      (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2)))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $K$ be a finite field, let $L,h,B\in\mathbb N$, and assign weights $w:\{0,\ldots,L-1\}\times\{0,1\}\to K$. The local graph has ordered pairs of disjoint $h$-subsets as edges, with the left word equal to one on its subset and the right word equal to zero on its subset. A word $s$ has hash $\sum_i w(i,s(i))$. Fix any target $(a,b)\in K^2$. Count edges whose endpoint hashes are $a,b$ and whose corresponding left and right hash buckets both contain at most $B$ vertices. This retained hit count satisfies

$$
\operatorname{hits}_{L,h,B}(w;a,b)\le B^2.
$$

The two target values may be equal, and no positivity or separation hypothesis on $L,h,B$ is required.

This supplies a pointwise representation cap for every retained target, complementing the averaged hash-moment estimates.

theorem_title: Erasing a mask coordinate never increases its value
natural_language_statement:
Let $L,a,m\in\mathbb N$ with $m<2^L$. The recursive operation $\operatorname{eraseMask}(L,a,m)$ inspects the binary positions below $L$ and removes position $a$ if present. Then

$$
\operatorname{eraseMask}(L,a,m)\le m.
$$

The coordinate $a$ need not lie below $L$. This gives a numerical bound on the mask-erasure result that can be used in subsequent word-size and address checks.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.MassScales.candidateCount_log_rate : @Filter.Tendsto.{0, 0} Nat Real
  (fun (n : Nat) =>
    @HDiv.hDiv.{0, 0, 0} Real Real Real (@instHDiv.{0} Real (@DivInvMonoid.toDiv.{0} Real Real.instDivInvMonoid))
      (Real.log (@Nat.cast.{0} Real Real.instNatCast (ThreeSum.Scales.candidateCount n)))
      (Real.log (@Nat.cast.{0} Real Real.instNatCast n)))
  (@Filter.atTop.{0} Nat Nat.instPreorder)
  (@nhds.{0} Real
    (@UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace.{0} Real (@PseudoMetricSpace.toUniformSpace.{0} Real Real.pseudoMetricSpace))
    (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Real (nat_lit 0) (@Zero.toOfNat0.{0} Real Real.instZero))) := by

natural_language_statement:
For positive input sizes $n$, let $b(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ and $y(n)=2^{\lfloor\sqrt{b(n)}\rfloor+1}$. Let $C(n)$ be the number of primes in the interval $(y(n),4y(n)]$, namely the executable candidate pool's count. Then

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log C(n)}{\log n}=0.
$$

The logarithms are real logarithms of the natural counts. This identifies the candidate-pool factor as contributing zero to the polynomial exponent in the false-mass bounds.

    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
      (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 10000) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 10000)))
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (ThreeSum.ModuloCosts.roundedPower p)
          (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) N
            (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
              (Nat.log (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2)))
                (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) U
                  (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1)))))
              (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))))
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))) := by

natural_language_statement:
Let $p,n_A,n_B,n_C,N,U\in\mathbb N$, where $n_A,n_B,n_C$ are array lengths, $p$ is the modulus parameter, and $U$ is the input-magnitude parameter. Assume $n_A,n_B,n_C\le N$. Put $K(p)=3^{\operatorname{clog}_2(p)}$, using the natural ceiling logarithm. The modular-counting time budget satisfies

$$T_{\mathrm{count}}(p,n_A,n_B,n_C,U)\le10000\bigl(K(p)+N(\log_2^{\mathrm{nat}}(U+1)+1)+1\bigr),$$

where $\log_2^{\mathrm{nat}}$ is the natural-number floor logarithm. This inequality includes capacity computation, histogram initialization, Karatsuba multiplication, folding, and residue lookups in a single arithmetic-operation bound.

theorem_title: Reverse-position formula for the recursive radix decoder
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.OutputDecodeOrder.indices_getD_reverse : ∀ (m J k : Nat) {j : Nat} (hj : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j J),
  @Eq.{1} Nat
    (@List.getD.{0} Nat (ThreeSum.OutputDecodeOrder.indices m J k)
      (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHSub.{0} Nat instSubNat)
        (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHSub.{0} Nat instSubNat) J
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
        j)
      (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))))
    (@HMod.hMod.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMod.{0} Nat Nat.instMod)
      (@HDiv.hDiv.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHDiv.{0} Nat Nat.instDiv) k
        (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
          (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) m j))
      m) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
For natural numbers $m,J,k$, define an index list recursively by $D_{m,0}(k)=[]$ and $D_{m,J+1}(k)=D_{m,J}(k\mathbin{/}m)\mathbin{+\!+}[k\bmod m]$, where division is natural-number division. For every $j<J$,

$$
D_{m,J}(k)[J-1-j]=\left(\frac{k}{m^j}\right)\bmod m.
$$

List access is the default-zero access used by the decoder, though the indicated position is valid. No positivity assumption on $m$ or bound on $k$ is needed; the natural division and remainder conventions apply at zero. This identifies each physical tuple index with its positional digit.

theorem_title: Physical tuple indices decode as fixed-length radix digits
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.OutputDecodeOrder.tuples_getD_indices : ∀ {α : Type u_1} (base : List.{u_1} α) (da : α)
  (hm :
    @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) (@List.length.{u_1} α base))
  (J k : Nat)
  (hk :
    @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat k
      (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
        (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid)))
        (@List.length.{u_1} α base) J)),
  @Eq.{u_1 + 1} (List.{u_1} α)
    (@List.getD.{u_1} (List.{u_1} α) (@ThreeSum.RadixKeyLists.tuples.{u_1} α base J) k (@List.nil.{u_1} α))
    (@List.map.{0, u_1} Nat α (fun (i : Nat) => @List.getD.{u_1} α base i da)
      (ThreeSum.OutputDecodeOrder.indices (@List.length.{u_1} α base) J k)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $A=[a_0,\ldots,a_{m-1}]$ be a nonempty list of elements of any type, and let $J,k\in\mathbb N$ with $k<m^J$. Enumerate all length-$J$ tuples from this list in the product order with the first coordinate outermost. Let $(d_0,\ldots,d_{J-1})$ be the length-$J$ base-$m$ digit list of $k$, with leading zeros and the last digit obtained by remainder. Then

$$
\operatorname{tuples}(A,J)[k]=[a_{d_0},\ldots,a_{d_{J-1}}].
$$

The formal lookup may use any default element; the index bounds ensure it is never needed. Repeated values in $A$ are allowed.

This ties quotient/remainder decoding to exact physical enumeration order rather than merely to the set of tuple values.

theorem_title: A uniform two-parameter polynomial bound from an eventual power bound
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.PolynomialResources.pair_polyBound_of_powerBound : ∀ {f : Nat → Nat} {a : Real} (hf : ThreeSum.StageBounds.PowerBound f a) (e : Nat),
  ∃ (s : Nat) (k : Nat),
    ∀ (n U : Nat),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
        (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) (f n)
          (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
            (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid)))
            (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) U
              (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
            e))
        (Light.polyBound s k (@List.cons.{0} Nat n (@List.cons.{0} Nat U (@List.nil.{0} Nat)))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, let $a\in\mathbb R$, and suppose that for every $\varepsilon>0$, one has $f(n)\le n^{a+\varepsilon}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. For every fixed $e\in\mathbb N$, there exist $s,k\in\mathbb N$ such that

$$
\forall n,U\in\mathbb N,\qquad
f(n)(U+1)^e\le 2^s\bigl((n+1)(U+1)\bigr)^k.
$$

The expression on the right is the compiler's polynomial resource bound for the two parameters $n$ and $U$. Its constants are independent of both parameters, and the inequality holds at every input size, including the finitely many sizes excluded by the eventual hypothesis.

This converts asymptotic resource envelopes into the uniform polynomial limits required for compilation.

Let $C$ be a finite set of natural primes, let $y>1$ be a natural number, and assume $p\ge y$ for every $p\in C$. For any nonzero integer $z$,

$$
\bigl|\{p\in C:p\mid |z|\}\bigr|\le\lfloor\log_y |z|\rfloor.
$$

The absolute value is interpreted as a natural number in the divisibility test. This bounds how many candidate primes can divide one nonzero difference, providing the divisor-count input to the deterministic modular-score argument.

theorem_title: Averaging bound for weighted modular scores
natural_language_statement:
Let $T$ be a finite index set, $d:T\to\mathbb Z$ an integer difference assignment, and $w:\mathbb Z\to\mathbb N$ a weight function with $w(0)=0$. For $q\in\mathbb N$, set $S(q)=\sum_{i\in T,\ q\mid |d(i)|}w(d(i))$. Let $C\subseteq\mathbb N$ be finite and $K\in\mathbb N$. Suppose each nonzero $d(i)$ is divisible in absolute value by at most $K$ members of $C$. Then

$$
\sum_{p\in C}S(qp)\le K S(q).
$$

Neither primality of the members of $C$ nor positivity of $q$ is required. Zero differences contribute no weight, so the estimate remains valid when genuine zero-sum witnesses are present.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.QueryCoordinates.output_missingSets : ∀ {W : Nat} (Q : Finset.{0} (Fin W)) (k : Nat),

    (ThreeSum.LightWeightedEnumeration.output (@ThreeSum.QueryCoordinates.weights W Q) (@Finset.card.{0} (Fin W) Q) k
      (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))))
    (@List.map.{0, 0} Nat Int (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt)
      (@List.map.{0, 0} (Finset.{0} (Fin W)) Nat (@ThreeSum.SubsetAddress.subsetMask W)
        (@ThreeSum.QueryCoordinates.missingSets W Q k))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $W,k\in\mathbb N$ and $Q\subseteq\{0,\ldots,W-1\}$. List the elements of $Q$ in increasing order and assign the weight $2^a$ to coordinate $a$. Let $\mathcal M_k(Q)$ be the canonical list of $k$-element subsets obtained from fixed-length sublists of the reversed coordinate list. The weighted enumerator, with $|Q|$ weights and initial offset zero, returns exactly

$$
\operatorname{output}(w_Q,|Q|,k,0)=\left[\sum_{a\in S}2^a\ :\ S\text{ in }\mathcal M_k(Q)\right].
$$

The equality is of ordered integer lists, with the subset masks cast from natural numbers. It supplies the exact list semantics required by the query-coordinate implementation.

      (@ThreeSum.Radix.representations.{u_1} Ω inst inst_1 p left right j a b) xs)
    (And (@Eq.{1} Nat (@List.length.{u_1} Ω xs) j)
      (And
        (@Dvd.dvd.{0} Int Int.instDvd
          (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Int Nat Int
            (@instHPow.{0, 0} Int Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Int (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Int Int.instMonoid))) p j)
          (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHSub.{0} Int Int.instSub) a
            (@ThreeSum.Radix.positionalHash.{u_1} Ω p left xs)))
        (@Dvd.dvd.{0} Int Int.instDvd

natural_language_statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $p\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, and let $\ell,r:\Omega\to\mathbb Z$ be endpoint maps. For a list $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{s-1})$, define the low-digit-first positional hash $H_u(x)=\sum_{i<s}p^i u(x_i)$.

The recursive family $R_j(a,b)$ chooses a first symbol whose two endpoint differences are divisible by $p$, then recurses on the quotient targets; $R_0(a,b)=\{[]\}$. For all natural $j$, integer targets $a,b$, and lists $x$,
$$
x\in R_j(a,b)\iff |x|=j\ \land\ p^j\mid a-H_\ell(x)\ \land\ p^j\mid b-H_r(x).
$$
This identifies the recursive candidate family with exactly the simultaneous positional congruences, including the original local choices.

$$
p^{j+1}\mid a-(h+pt)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
p\mid a-h\ \text{ and }\ p^j\mid\frac{a-h}{p}-t.
$$

The quotient is integer division; on the right, the first divisibility condition makes it exact. The radix may be negative, and the statement includes $j=0$.

This algebraic equivalence underlies the recursive radix representation rule, determining the next quotient target from the current digit without introducing an independent carry choice.

natural_language_statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, $p\in\mathbb Z$, and $\ell,r:\Omega\to\mathbb Z$. Suppose every local fiber
$F(a,b)=\{\omega:p\mid a-\ell(\omega),\ p\mid b-r(\omega)\}$ has at most $B\in\mathbb N$ elements. Define the recursive representation set $R_0(a,b)=\{[]\}$; at the next level, choose $\omega\in F(a,b)$ and recurse on the quotient targets $(a-\ell(\omega))/p$ and $(b-r(\omega))/p$. Then for all $j\in\mathbb N$ and $a,b\in\mathbb Z$,

$$
|R_j(a,b)|\le B^j.
$$

The definition uses total integer division, with quotient zero when $p=0$; no nonzero-radix assumption is needed for this counting statement.

The estimate bounds global representation multiplicity without adding a separate branching factor for carries.

theorem_title: Cartesian tuple enumeration has no duplicate records
natural_language_statement:
Let $B$ be a list of elements of any type, with no repeated element. Define $\mathcal T_0(B)=[[]]$ and construct $\mathcal T_{j+1}(B)$ by prepending each element of $B$, in order, to every tuple in $\mathcal T_j(B)$. For every $j\in\mathbb N$,

$$
\operatorname{Nodup}(B)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Nodup}(\mathcal T_j(B)).
$$

This preserves distinct record sequences before they are mapped to positional integer keys, even if that later key map has collisions.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.Reporting.frontier_length_le_mass : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq.{u_2 + 1} α] (I : Finset.{u_1} ι) (word : ι → List.{u_2} α)
  (weight : ι → Nat) (children : Nat → List.{u_2} α) (query : Nat → List.{u_2} α → Nat) (J k : Nat)
  (hlen :
    ∀ (i : ι),
      @Membership.mem.{u_1, u_1} ι (Finset.{u_1} ι)
          (@SetLike.instMembership.{u_1, u_1} (Finset.{u_1} ι) ι (@Finset.instSetLike.{u_1} ι)) I i →
        @Eq.{1} Nat (@List.length.{u_2} α (word i)) J)
  (hchildren :
    ∀ (i : ι)
      (hi :
        @Membership.mem.{u_1, u_1} ι (Finset.{u_1} ι)
          (@SetLike.instMembership.{u_1, u_1} (Finset.{u_1} ι) ι (@Finset.instSetLike.{u_1} ι)) I i)
      (j : Nat) (hj : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j J),
      @Membership.mem.{u_2, u_2} α (List.{u_2} α) (@List.instMembership.{u_2} α) (children j)
        (@GetElem.getElem.{u_2, 0, u_2} (List.{u_2} α) Nat α
          (fun (as : List.{u_2} α) (i : Nat) => @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i (@List.length.{u_2} α as))
          (@List.instGetElemNatLtLength.{u_2} α) (word i) j
          (@Eq.mpr.{0} (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j (@List.length.{u_2} α (word i))) (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j J)
            (@id.{0}
              (@Eq.{1} Prop (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j (@List.length.{u_2} α (word i))) (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j J))
              (@congrArg.{1, 1} Nat Prop (@List.length.{u_2} α (word i)) J
                (fun (_a : Nat) => @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j _a) (hlen i hi)))
            hj)))
  (hquery :
    ∀ (j : Nat),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat j J →
        ∀ (pre : List.{u_2} α),
          @Eq.{1} Nat (query j pre) (@ThreeSum.Reporting.mass.{u_1, u_2} ι α inst I word weight j pre))
  (hc : ∀ (k : Nat), @List.Nodup.{u_2} α (children k)) (hk : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat k J),
  @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@List.length.{u_2} (List.{u_2} α) (@ThreeSum.Reporting.frontier.{u_2} α children query k))
    (∑ i ∈ I, weight i) := by

natural_language_statement:
Let $I$ be a finite set of incidences, each carrying a length-$J$ word $w_i$ over an alphabet with decidable equality and a natural weight $a_i$. Let the child list at each depth contain every symbol appearing there in these words, and assume every child list has no repetitions. Suppose the query returns the exact prefix mass at every depth $j\le J$:
$$
Q(j,u)=\sum_{\substack{i\in I\\\operatorname{take}_j(w_i)=u}}a_i.
$$
Starting with the empty prefix when its query is positive, form each frontier by appending the supplied children and retaining only positive-query prefixes. For every $k\le J$,
$$
|\operatorname{frontier}_k|\le\sum_{i\in I}a_i.
$$
This bounds the number of visited prefixes even when distinct incidences have identical words.

theorem_title: Positive reporting frontiers contain no duplicate prefixes
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.Reporting.frontier_nodup : ∀ {α : Type u_2} [DecidableEq.{u_2 + 1} α] (children : Nat → List.{u_2} α) (query : Nat → List.{u_2} α → Nat)
  (hc : ∀ (k : Nat), @List.Nodup.{u_2} α (children k)) (k : Nat),
  @List.Nodup.{u_2} (List.{u_2} α) (@ThreeSum.Reporting.frontier.{u_2} α children query k) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a type with decidable equality. At each depth $k$, let $C_k$ be a list of possible next symbols, and let $q(k,P)\in\mathbb N$ be a query value for a prefix $P$. Starting with the empty prefix when its query is positive, form each frontier by appending every symbol in $C_k$ to the previous frontier and retaining positive-query prefixes. If every $C_k$ has no duplicates, then

$$\forall k\in\mathbb N,\qquad\operatorname{Nodup}(F_k).$$

This structural guarantee holds for arbitrary query values. It ensures that the reporting traversal does not repeat a prefix when each child list is duplicate-free.

theorem_title: The reporting frontier is exactly the set of positive-mass prefixes
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.Reporting.mem_frontier_iff : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq.{u_2 + 1} α] (I : Finset.{u_1} ι) (word : ι → List.{u_2} α)
  (weight : ι → Nat) (children : Nat → List.{u_2} α) (query : Nat → List.{u_2} α → Nat) (J k : Nat)
  (hlen :
    ∀ (i : ι),
      @Membership.mem.{u_1, u_1} ι (Finset.{u_1} ι)
          (@SetLike.instMembership.{u_1, u_1} (Finset.{u_1} ι) ι (@Finset.instSetLike.{u_1} ι)) I i →
        @Eq.{1} Nat (@List.length.{u_2} α (word i)) J)
  (hchildren :
    ∀ (i : ι)
      (hi :
        @Membership.mem.{u_1, u_1} ι (Finset.{u_1} ι)
          (@SetLike.instMembership.{u_1, u_1} (Finset.{u_1} ι) ι (@Finset.instSetLike.{u_1} ι)) I i)
      (j : Nat) (hj : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j J),
      @Membership.mem.{u_2, u_2} α (List.{u_2} α) (@List.instMembership.{u_2} α) (children j)
        (@GetElem.getElem.{u_2, 0, u_2} (List.{u_2} α) Nat α
          (fun (as : List.{u_2} α) (i : Nat) => @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i (@List.length.{u_2} α as))
          (@List.instGetElemNatLtLength.{u_2} α) (word i) j
          (@Eq.mpr.{0} (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j (@List.length.{u_2} α (word i))) (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j J)
            (@id.{0}
              (@Eq.{1} Prop (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j (@List.length.{u_2} α (word i))) (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j J))
              (@congrArg.{1, 1} Nat Prop (@List.length.{u_2} α (word i)) J
                (fun (_a : Nat) => @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j _a) (hlen i hi)))
            hj)))
  (hquery :
    ∀ (j : Nat),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat j J →
        ∀ (pre : List.{u_2} α),
          @Eq.{1} Nat (query j pre) (@ThreeSum.Reporting.mass.{u_1, u_2} ι α inst I word weight j pre))
  (hk : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat k J) (pre : List.{u_2} α),
  Iff
    (@Membership.mem.{u_2, u_2} (List.{u_2} α) (List.{u_2} (List.{u_2} α)) (@List.instMembership.{u_2} (List.{u_2} α))
      (@ThreeSum.Reporting.frontier.{u_2} α children query k) pre)
    (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0)))
      (@ThreeSum.Reporting.mass.{u_1, u_2} ι α inst I word weight k pre)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $I$ be a finite incidence set with words $w_i$ over an alphabet with decidable equality and natural weights $a_i$. Suppose every $w_i$ has length $J$, its symbol at position $j<J$ belongs to the supplied child list $C_j$, and every query through depth $J$ equals the exact prefix mass

$$M_k(P)=\sum_{i\in I:\,\operatorname{take}_k(w_i)=P}a_i.$$

Let $F_k$ be the frontier formed by repeatedly appending supplied children and filtering for positive query values. For $k\le J$ and every prefix $P$,

$$P\in F_k\iff M_k(P)>0.$$

This proves both soundness and completeness of positive-prefix reporting. Duplicate child entries are allowed in this membership theorem.

theorem_title: Local coordinates reconstruct any subset of a single block
natural_language_statement:
Let $J,L\in\mathbb N$, fix a block $i<J$, and let $Q\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$. Write $B_i(Q)=\{iL+a:a\in Q\}$. If a global set $T\subseteq\{0,\ldots,JL-1\}$ satisfies $T\subseteq B_i(Q)$, let $\operatorname{row}_i(T)$ collect its local coordinates in block $i$. Then

$$B_i\bigl(\operatorname{row}_i(T)\bigr)=T.$$

This inverse relation allows a child subset enumerated in the global address space to be interpreted as a local reporting row without losing any elements.

theorem_title: Appending a row updates one entry of the prefix map
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.ReportingHostMasks.prefixRows_append : ∀ {J L k : Nat} (pre : List.{0} (Finset.{0} (Fin L))) (hp : @Eq.{1} Nat (@List.length.{0} (Finset.{0} (Fin L)) pre) k)
  (hk : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat k J) (S : Finset.{0} (Fin L)),
  @Eq.{1} (Fin J → Finset.{0} (Fin L))
    (@ThreeSum.StoredReporting.prefixRows J L
      (@HAppend.hAppend.{0, 0, 0} (List.{0} (Finset.{0} (Fin L))) (List.{0} (Finset.{0} (Fin L)))
        (List.{0} (Finset.{0} (Fin L)))
        (@instHAppendOfAppend.{0} (List.{0} (Finset.{0} (Fin L))) (@List.instAppend.{0} (Finset.{0} (Fin L)))) pre
        (@List.cons.{0} (Finset.{0} (Fin L)) S (@List.nil.{0} (Finset.{0} (Fin L))))))
    (@Function.update.{1, 1} (Fin J) (fun (a : Fin J) => Finset.{0} (Fin L)) (instDecidableEqFin J)
      (@ThreeSum.StoredReporting.prefixRows J L pre) (@Fin.mk J k hk) S) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $J,L,k\in\mathbb N$ with $k<J$, let $P$ be a list of $k$ subsets of an $L$-element ground set, and let $S$ be another such subset. Define $R_P(i)$ to be the list entry $P_i$ when present and the empty set otherwise, for $i<J$. Then

$$R_{P\mathbin{+\!+}[S]}(i)=\begin{cases}S,&i=k,\\R_P(i),&i\ne k.\end{cases}$$

Thus extending a reporting prefix changes only its next row, giving the functional update required by the mask-transition identities.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.ReportingHostMasks.querySet_step : ∀ {J L k : Nat} (Q : Fin J → Finset.{0} (Fin L)) (hk : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat k J),
  @Eq.{1} (Finset.{0} (Fin (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) J L)))
    (@ThreeSum.BlockIndexedQuery.querySet J L
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) k
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
      Q)
    (@SDiff.sdiff.{0} (Finset.{0} (Fin (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) J L)))
      (@Finset.instSDiff.{0} (Fin (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) J L))
        (instDecidableEqFin (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) J L)))
      (@ThreeSum.BlockIndexedQuery.querySet J L k Q)
      (@ThreeSum.ReportingHostMasks.blockSet J L (@Fin.mk J k hk) (Q (@Fin.mk J k hk)))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $J,L\in\mathbb N$ and, for each block $i<J$, let $Q_i\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$. Encode a local set in block $i$ as $B_i(S)=\{iL+a:a\in S\}$. Let $R_k$ be the union of $B_i(Q_i)$ over the remaining blocks $k\le i<J$. For $k<J$,

$$R_{k+1}=R_k\setminus B_k(Q_k).$$

This identifies the exact set transition behind the reporting host's next-block query-mask update.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.ReportingHostPackedCatalog.upperBound_hit : ∀ {key : Nat → Nat} {n i : Nat} {S : List.{0} Int} (hi : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i n)
  (hunique :
    ∀ (a : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat a n →
        ∀ (b : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat b n → @Eq.{1} Nat (key a) (key b) → @Eq.{1} Nat a b)
  (hperm : @List.Perm.{0} Int S (ThreeSum.ReportingHostPackedCatalog.codes key n))
  (hs : @List.Pairwise.{0} Int (fun (x1 x2 : Int) => @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt x1 x2) S),
  have K :=
    ThreeSum.BinarySearch.upperBound
      (fun (j : Nat) => @List.getD.{0} Int S j (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0)))) n
      (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
          (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) (key i)
            (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) n

theorem_title: Every valid left-subset enumeration index selects an h-element set
natural_language_statement:
Let $L,h,i$ be natural numbers, and let $S_i$ be the subset obtained by decoding position $i$ in the enumeration of $L$-bit masks of weight $h$. If $i<\binom{L}{h}$, then
$$|S_i|=h.$$
Here the selected subset is a subset of $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$, and the index hypothesis ensures that the enumeration's default value is not used.

This validates the cardinality of the left component selected by the pair-enumeration host.

theorem_title: Number of enumerated left subsets
formal_statement:
@[simp]
theorem ThreeSum.ReportingHostPairEnumeration.lefts_length : ∀ (L h : Nat),
  @Eq.{1} Nat (@List.length.{0} (Finset.{0} (Fin L)) (ThreeSum.ReportingHostPairEnumeration.lefts L h)) (L.choose h) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
For natural numbers $L,h$, let $\operatorname{lefts}(L,h)$ be the ordered list obtained by decoding every width-$L$ subset mask of weight $h$. Then

$$
|\operatorname{lefts}(L,h)|=\binom{L}{h}.
$$

There is no assumption that $h\le L$; the binomial coefficient and enumeration are both zero when $h>L$. This is the outer-list size used in the direct enumeration of balanced row pairs.

theorem_title: The disjoint h-subset pair enumeration has an exact binomial length
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.ReportingHostPairEnumeration.pairs_length : ∀ (L h : Nat),
  @Eq.{1} Nat
    (@List.length.{0} (Prod.{0, 0} (Finset.{0} (Fin L)) (Finset.{0} (Fin L)))
      (ThreeSum.ReportingHostPairEnumeration.pairs L h))
    (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
      (L.choose
        (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) h))
      ((@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) h).choose
        h)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
For natural numbers $L,h$, enumerate all $h$-element subsets $S$ of $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$ and, for each $S$, enumerate all $h$-element subsets $R$ of its complement. Let $P(L,h)$ be the resulting list of ordered pairs $(S,R)$. Then
$$|P(L,h)|=\binom{L}{2h}\binom{2h}{h}.$$
The equality uses the usual convention that $\binom{L}{2h}=0$ when $2h>L$.

This gives the exact number of entries required for the host's list of balanced disjoint subset pairs.

theorem ThreeSum.ReportingHostPairEnumeration.rights_length : ∀ {L h : Nat} (S : Finset.{0} (Fin L)) (hS : @Eq.{1} Nat (@Finset.card.{0} (Fin L) S) h),

natural_language_statement:
Let $L,h\in\mathbb N$, and let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$ have cardinality $h$. The right-subset enumeration lists the $h$-element subsets of the complement of $S$. Its length is

$$
|\operatorname{rights}(S,h)|=\binom{L-h}{h}.
$$

The formula includes the case where the complement has fewer than $h$ elements, when the list is empty. It supplies the exact row length for enumerating disjoint balanced pairs.

formal_statement:

  (fun (m : Nat) =>

$$\lim_{m\to\infty}\frac{\lfloor\sqrt m\rfloor}{m}=0.$$

This limit controls the lower-order square-root rounding term in the construction's scale parameters.

theorem_title: Finite modulus loss from the selected prime-chain depth
natural_language_statement:
Let $R:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be any target-radix function. For $n\in\mathbb N$, put $m=\operatorname{inputBits}(n)$, $y=2^{\lfloor\sqrt m\rfloor+1}$, and $r=\operatorname{ilog}_{4y}(R(n)\mathbin{\mathrm{div}}4)$, where the integer logarithm is zero on argument zero. If a natural number $P$ satisfies $y^r\le P$, then

$$
R(n)\le32y\,4^r P.
$$

The multiplier $32y4^r$ is the construction's declared prime loss. There is no lower-bound assumption on the target $R(n)$.

This transfers the lower product bound for the actual selected prime chain into a finite comparison with the intended radix, including small input cases.

theorem_title: A guarded prefix traversal charges at most the threshold mass
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.SharedTraversalCosts.prefix_time_le : ∀ {time mass : Nat → Nat} {threshold initial work : Nat}
  (hzero :
    @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (time (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))))
      (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 30) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 30))))
  (hstep :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat
        (time
          (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) i
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1)))))
        (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
          (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (time i) initial)
          (@ite.{1} Nat
            (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat threshold
              (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
                (ThreeSum.SharedTraversalCosts.prefixMass mass i) (mass i)))
            (threshold.decLt
              (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
                (ThreeSum.SharedTraversalCosts.prefixMass mass i) (mass i)))
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0)))
            (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) (mass i) work))))
  (n : Nat),
  @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (time n)
    (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 30) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 30)))
        (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) n initial))
      (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat) threshold work)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $t,m:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be cumulative time and per-slot mass, and let $\theta,A,W\in\mathbb N$ be a threshold, fixed slot cost, and cost per unit mass. Write $P_i=\sum_{j<i}m(j)$. Suppose $t(0)\le30$ and

$$t(i+1)\le t(i)+A+\begin{cases}0,&\theta<P_i+m(i),\\m(i)W,&P_i+m(i)\le\theta.\end{cases}$$

Then, for every $n\in\mathbb N$,

$$t(n)\le30+nA+\theta W.$$

This bounds the expensive work admitted by the cumulative-mass guard without requiring any bound on a slot that crosses the threshold.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.SourceBandData.At.transfer : ∀ {μ ν f : Nat → Int} {base n g p m i : Nat} {shift : Int} (H : ThreeSum.SourceBandData.At μ f base n g p m shift i)
  (hm : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) m)
  (hhead :
    ∀ (q : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat q (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 6) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 6))) →
        @Eq.{1} Int
          (ν
            (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
              (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) base
                (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
                  (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 6) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 6))) i))
              q))
          (μ
            (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
              (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) base
                (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
                  (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 6) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 6))) i))
              q)))
  (hdata :
    ∀ (x : Nat),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (ThreeSum.SourceBandLayout.hist base n g m i) x →
        @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat x
            (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
              (ThreeSum.SourceBandLayout.flat base n g m i) (ThreeSum.SourceBandLayout.cap n g)) →
          @Eq.{1} Int (ν x) (μ x)),
  ThreeSum.SourceBandData.At ν f base n g p m shift i := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\mu,\nu$ be integer memories and $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ a source function. Fix natural parameters $b,n,g,p,m,i$ and an integer shift, with $m>0$. Suppose $\mu$ contains the band-$i$ representation: its six-cell header, reduced keys, histogram counts, bucket offsets, and physical source-position lists.

Let $H_i$ and $F_i$ be that band's histogram and flat-position bases. If the memories agree on the six header cells $b+6i,\ldots,b+6i+5$ and throughout $[H_i,F_i+\min(n,g))$, then

$$
\operatorname{BandAt}(\mu;f,b,n,g,p,m,\mathrm{shift},i)
\Longrightarrow
\operatorname{BandAt}(\nu;f,b,n,g,p,m,\mathrm{shift},i).
$$

This preservation rule keeps both histogram counts and exact original-position fibers available after unrelated memory changes.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.SourceBandPairData.Data.transfer : ∀ {μ ν fL fR : Nat → Int} {base NL NR g p m : Nat} {shift : Int}
  (H : ThreeSum.SourceBandPairData.Data μ fL fR base NL NR g p m shift)
  (hm : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) m)

  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\mu,\nu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ be memories and $f_L,f_R:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ source-value functions. Fix natural parameters $b,N_L,N_R,g,p,m$ with $m>0$, where $b$ is the layout base, $N_L,N_R$ are source lengths, $g$ is the band size, and $p,m$ are the residue moduli. Fix an integer shift $z$. Suppose $\mu$ satisfies the paired-band data contract: all left-band records are correct for $f_L$ with zero shift, all right-band records are correct for $f_R$ with shift $z$, and the shared zero array has zero in its $m+1$ cells. If
$$\nu(a)=\mu(a)\quad\text{for every }a\ge b+8,$$
then
$$\operatorname{Data}(\mu,f_L,f_R,b,N_L,N_R,g,p,m,z)
\Longrightarrow\operatorname{Data}(\nu,f_L,f_R,b,N_L,N_R,g,p,m,z).$$

This transfers the retained catalog data across computations that preserve its entire address region.

theorem_title: Preservation of stored source-band catalogs under a retained memory prefix
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.SourceBandPairData.Stored.of_kept : ∀ {μ ν fL fR : Nat → Int} {base NL NR g p m bound : Nat} {shift : Int}
  (H : ThreeSum.SourceBandPairData.Stored μ fL fR base NL NR g p m shift)
  (hm : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 0) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 0))) m)
  (K : Light.Kept μ ν bound) (hb : @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (ThreeSum.SourceBandPairData.next base NL NR g m) bound),
  ThreeSum.SourceBandPairData.Stored ν fL fR base NL NR g p m shift := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\mu,\nu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ be memories, and let $f_L,f_R$ describe source arrays of lengths $N_L,N_R$. Fix a base address, band width $g$, arithmetic modulus $p$, bucket modulus $m>0$, and right-side shift $s$. The stored pair consists of the eight-cell layout header, both band catalogs with their codes, histograms and position buckets, and the shared zero array of length $m+1$. Let $E$ be the layout's next free address.

If this pair is stored in $\mu$, $E\le B$, and the memories agree below $B$, then
$$
\operatorname{Stored}(\mu;f_L,f_R,\mathrm{base},N_L,N_R,g,p,m,s)
\Longrightarrow
\operatorname{Stored}(\nu;f_L,f_R,\mathrm{base},N_L,N_R,g,p,m,s).
$$
This transfers the complete retained source representation across later memory updates.

theorem_title: A stored bucket contains exactly the source indices with its key
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.Stored.mem_bucketList : ∀ {μ : Nat → Int} {key : Nat → Nat} {N M offsets flat r i : Nat}
  (H : ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.Stored μ key N M offsets flat)
  (hkey : ∀ (i : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i N → @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (key i) M)
  (hr : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat r M),
  Iff
    (@Membership.mem.{0, 0} Nat (List.{0} Nat) (@List.instMembership.{0} Nat)
      (ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.bucketList μ flat (ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.offset key N r)
        (ThreeSum.LightHistogram.count key r N))
      i)
    (And (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i N) (@Eq.{1} Nat (key i) r)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $N,M,o,f,r,i$ be natural numbers, let $\kappa:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ satisfy $\kappa(j)<M$ for $j<N$, and let $\mu$ store the stable bucket representation of these $N$ indices at offset base $o$ and flat-array base $f$. For a valid key $r<M$, define
$$D_r=\#\{j<N:\kappa(j)=r\},\qquad O_r=\sum_{s<r}D_s.$$
Let $L_r$ be the list read from the $D_r$ consecutive memory cells starting at $f+O_r$, interpreting their stored integers as natural indices. Then
$$i\in L_r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad i<N\ \land\ \kappa(i)=r.$$

This identifies physical bucket contents with their exact source-index semantics, including distinct indices whose input values coincide.

formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.position_bucket_iff : ∀ {key : Nat → Nat} {N i r : Nat} (hi : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i N),
  Iff
    (And (@LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.offset key N r) (ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.position key N i))
      (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.position key N i)
        (ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.offset key N
          (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) r
            (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1)))))))
    (@Eq.{1} Nat (key i) r) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $k:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and $N\in\mathbb N$. Put $C_r(t)=|\{a<t:k(a)=r\}|$, $O_r=\sum_{s<r}C_s(N)$, and $P(i)=O_{k(i)}+C_{k(i)}(i)$. For every $i<N$ and $r\in\mathbb N$,

$$
O_r\le P(i)<O_{r+1}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad k(i)=r.
$$

The equivalence identifies exactly which original indices occupy each contiguous bucket segment. It is valid without a global bound on the key values.

theorem_title: Counting-sort positions preserve distinct indices
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.position_injective : ∀ {key : Nat → Nat} {N i j : Nat} (hi : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i N) (hj : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j N)
  (he : @Eq.{1} Nat (ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.position key N i) (ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.position key N j)),
  @Eq.{1} Nat i j := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $k:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be a key function and $N\in\mathbb N$. Define $C_r(t)=|\{a<t:k(a)=r\}|$, $O_r=\sum_{s<r}C_s(N)$, and the counting-sort position $P(i)=O_{k(i)}+C_{k(i)}(i)$. For indices $i,j<N$,

$$
P(i)=P(j)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad i=j.
$$

No upper bound on the key values is required. Thus the retained bucket layout keeps distinct physical input indices separate even when their keys coincide.

Let $g>0$, let three original integer lists have lengths at most $n$, and let $A,B,C$ be their strictly increasing normalized lists. Suppose memory $\mu$ satisfies the normalized-data specification, including their representations, band lookup tables, owner records, and the three incidence arrays with returned count $r$. $$v_X+n\le b,\quad e_X+2+2n\le b\quad(X=A,B,C),$$

theorem_title: Membership in the explicit-leaf family
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.SparseBoxes.mem_explicitLeaves : ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder.{u_1} α] (q leaf : Finset.{u_1} α) (t : Nat),
  Iff
    (@Membership.mem.{u_1, u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α) (Finset.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α))
      (@SetLike.instMembership.{u_1, u_1} (Finset.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α)) (Finset.{u_1} α)
        (@Finset.instSetLike.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α)))
      (@ThreeSum.SparseBoxes.explicitLeaves.{u_1} α inst q t) leaf)
    (And
      (@LE.le.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α)
        (@Preorder.toLE.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α)
          (@PartialOrder.toPreorder.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α) (@Finset.instPartialOrder.{u_1} α)))
        leaf q)
      (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat
        (@Finset.card.{u_1} α
          (@SDiff.sdiff.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α)
            (@Finset.instSDiff.{u_1} α fun (a b : α) => @LinearOrder.toDecidableEq.{u_1} α inst a b) q leaf))
        t)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $q,\ell$ be finite subsets of a linearly ordered type and let $t\in\mathbb N$. Define the explicit-leaf family by taking $q\setminus m$ for every missing set $m\subseteq q$ of size less than $t$. Then

$$
\ell\in\operatorname{explicitLeaves}(q,t)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\ell\subseteq q\ \land\ |q\setminus\ell|<t.
$$

This characterizes precisely the leaves handled by direct accesses in the sparse-query decomposition, including the empty family at threshold zero.

theorem_title: Exact sparse-query decomposition into explicit leaves and boxes
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.SparseBoxes.sparse_query_identity : ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder.{u_1} α] (q : Finset.{u_1} α) (t : Nat) (weight : Finset.{u_1} α → Int),
  @Eq.{1} Int (∑ leaf ∈ @Finset.powerset.{u_1} α q, weight leaf)
    (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHAdd.{0} Int Int.instAdd)
      (∑ leaf ∈ @Finset.powerset.{u_1} α q with
        @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat
          (@Finset.card.{u_1} α
            (@SDiff.sdiff.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α)
              (@Finset.instSDiff.{u_1} α fun (a b : α) => @LinearOrder.toDecidableEq.{u_1} α inst a b) q leaf))
          t,
        weight leaf)
      (∑ u ∈ @Finset.powersetCard.{u_1} α t q,
        @ThreeSum.SparseBoxes.boxSum.{u_1} α inst
          (@SDiff.sdiff.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α)
            (@Finset.instSDiff.{u_1} α fun (a b : α) => @LinearOrder.toDecidableEq.{u_1} α inst a b) q u)
          (@ThreeSum.SparseBoxes.queryFree.{u_1} α inst q u) weight)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $q$ be a finite subset of a linearly ordered type, let $t\in\mathbb N$, and let $w$ assign an integer weight to each finite subset. For $u\subseteq q$, define $F(q,u)=\{x\in q\setminus u:\forall y\in u,\ x<y\}$. Let $B(A,F)$ denote the sum of $w(\ell)$ over $A\setminus F\subseteq\ell\subseteq A$. Then

$$
\sum_{\ell\subseteq q}w(\ell)
=\sum_{\substack{\ell\subseteq q\\|q\setminus\ell|<t}}w(\ell)
+\sum_{\substack{u\subseteq q\\|u|=t}}B(q\setminus u,F(q,u)).
$$

This exact identity separates the near-full subsets into explicit accesses and all remaining subsets into canonical box queries. It holds for signed weights and every threshold, including zero.

theorem_title: Adding two costs preserves their common power bound
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.StageBounds.PowerBound.add_same : ∀ {f g : Nat → Nat} {a : Real} (hf : ThreeSum.StageBounds.PowerBound f a) (hg : ThreeSum.StageBounds.PowerBound g a),
  ThreeSum.StageBounds.PowerBound
    (fun (n : Nat) => @HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) (f n) (g n)) a := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $f,g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and $a\in\mathbb R$. Suppose each function has power bound $a$: for every positive slack, each is eventually bounded by $n$ raised to $a$ plus that slack. Then their sum has the same power bound:

$$\forall\varepsilon>0,\quad f(n)+g(n)\le n^{a+\varepsilon}\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }n.$$

This closure property combines separate stage costs without increasing their common asymptotic exponent.

theorem_title: Forced-prefix counts from partial zeta transforms
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.Subset.forced_prefix_identity : ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq.{u_1 + 1} α] (f g : Finset.{u_1} α → Int)
  (prefix₁ prefix₂ suffix q : Finset.{u_1} α) (a b : Nat)
  (hf :
    ∀ (s : Finset.{u_1} α),
      @Ne.{1} Int (f s) (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0))) →
        @Eq.{1} Nat (@Finset.card.{u_1} α s) a)
  (hg :
    ∀ (v : Finset.{u_1} α),
      @Ne.{1} Int (g v) (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Int (nat_lit 0) (@instOfNat (nat_lit 0))) →
        @Eq.{1} Nat (@Finset.card.{u_1} α v) b)
  (hd₁ :
    @Disjoint.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α) (@Finset.instPartialOrder.{u_1} α) (@Finset.instOrderBot.{u_1} α) prefix₁ suffix)
  (hd₂ :
    @Disjoint.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α) (@Finset.instPartialOrder.{u_1} α) (@Finset.instOrderBot.{u_1} α) prefix₂ suffix)
  (hqs :
    @LE.le.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α)
      (@Preorder.toLE.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α)
        (@PartialOrder.toPreorder.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α) (@Finset.instPartialOrder.{u_1} α)))
      q suffix)
  (hq :
    @Eq.{1} Nat (@Finset.card.{u_1} α q)
      (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
        (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHSub.{0} Nat instSubNat) a (@Finset.card.{u_1} α prefix₁))
        (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHSub.{0} Nat instSubNat) b (@Finset.card.{u_1} α prefix₂)))),
  @Eq.{1} Int
    (@ThreeSum.Subset.mobius.{u_1} α
      (fun (t : Finset.{u_1} α) =>
        @HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHMul.{0} Int Int.instMul)
          (@ThreeSum.Subset.partialZeta.{u_1} α inst suffix f
            (@Union.union.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α) (@Finset.instUnion.{u_1} α inst) prefix₁ t))
          (@ThreeSum.Subset.partialZeta.{u_1} α inst suffix g
            (@Union.union.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α) (@Finset.instUnion.{u_1} α inst) prefix₂ t)))
      q)
    (∑ x ∈ @Finset.powerset.{u_1} α q,
      @HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Int Int Int (@instHMul.{0} Int Int.instMul)
        (f (@Union.union.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α) (@Finset.instUnion.{u_1} α inst) prefix₁ x))
        (g
          (@Union.union.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α) (@Finset.instUnion.{u_1} α inst) prefix₂
            (@SDiff.sdiff.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α) (@Finset.instSDiff.{u_1} α inst) q x)))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $f,g$ be integer-valued functions on finite subsets of a type with decidable equality, supported respectively on sets of cardinalities $a,b$. Let finite prefixes $P_1,P_2$ each be disjoint from a suffix set $S$, and let $Q\subseteq S$ satisfy $|Q|=(a-|P_1|)+(b-|P_2|)$, using truncated natural subtraction.

Define $Z_Sf(U)=\sum_{X\subseteq U\cap S}f((U\setminus S)\cup X)$ and $\mathcal MH(Q)=\sum_{T\subseteq Q}(-1)^{|Q|-|T|}H(T)$. Then
$$
\mathcal M\!\left(T\mapsto Z_Sf(P_1\cup T)Z_Sg(P_2\cup T)\right)(Q)
=\sum_{X\subseteq Q}f(P_1\cup X)g(P_2\cup(Q\setminus X)).
$$
This expresses the restricted reporting count through the partial zeta stages already available to the algorithm.

theorem_title: Möbius inversion on finite subsets
natural_language_statement:
Let $\alpha$ have decidable equality, let $f$ be an integer-valued function on finite subsets, and let $Q$ be a finite set. Define the zeta transform by $(\zeta f)(S)=\sum_{T\subseteq S}f(T)$. Then

$$\sum_{S\subseteq Q}(-1)^{|Q|-|S|}(\zeta f)(S)=f(Q).$$

Thus the signed subset transform inverts the ordinary zeta transform exactly. This identity supplies the algebraic recovery step for the subset-counting routines.

  (ht :

      (@Preorder.toLE.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α)
        (@PartialOrder.toPreorder.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α) (@Finset.instPartialOrder.{u_1} α)))
      t processed),
  @Eq.{1} Int
    (@ThreeSum.Subset.partialZeta.{u_1} α inst processed f
      (@Union.union.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α) (@Finset.instUnion.{u_1} α inst) s₀ t))
    (∑ x ∈ @Finset.powerset.{u_1} α t, f (@Union.union.{u_1} (Finset.{u_1} α) (@Finset.instUnion.{u_1} α inst) s₀ x)) := by

natural_language_statement:
Let $f$ be an integer-valued function on finite subsets of a type with decidable equality. For a processed set $P$, define

$$Z_Pf(U)=\sum_{X\subseteq U\cap P}f\bigl((U\setminus P)\cup X\bigr).$$

Let $S_0,T$ be finite sets with $S_0\cap P=\varnothing$ and $T\subseteq P$. Then

$$Z_Pf(S_0\cup T)=\sum_{X\subseteq T}f(S_0\cup X).$$

The unprocessed part $S_0$ is forced to remain present. This permits a forced-prefix query to be read from a single entry of a stored partial zeta stage.

theorem_title: Fixed-cardinality union convolution is disjoint convolution
natural_language_statement:
Let $\alpha$ have decidable equality and let $f,g$ be integer-valued functions on its finite subsets. Suppose $f(S)\ne0$ implies $|S|=a$ and $g(T)\ne0$ implies $|T|=b$, for fixed $a,b\in\mathbb N$. For a finite set $Q$ with $|Q|=a+b$,

$$\sum_{\substack{S,T\subseteq Q\\S\cup T=Q}}f(S)g(T)=\sum_{S\subseteq Q}f(S)g(Q\setminus S).$$

This converts exact-union convolution into the disjoint subset convolution needed by the fixed-cardinality counting construction, even when the coefficients are signed integers.

theorem_title: Fixed-weight bit-mask enumeration has no duplicates
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.SubsetAddress.enumerateLayer_nodup : ∀ (L k : Nat), @List.Nodup.{0} Nat (ThreeSum.SubsetAddress.enumerateLayer L k) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
For $L,k\in\mathbb N$, let $E_{L,k}$ be the recursively constructed list of $L$-bit masks having $k$ selected positions. The enumeration visits the lower half before the upper half and stops on empty layers. It has no repeated entries:

$$
\forall i,j<|E_{L,k}|,\qquad
E_{L,k}[i]=E_{L,k}[j]\Longrightarrow i=j.
$$

The assertion is uniform in $L$ and $k$: the zero-weight list contains only the zero mask, and layers with $k>L$ are empty.

This uniqueness property allows list positions to serve as unambiguous compact addresses for subsets of a fixed size.

          (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
        (L.choose k))

natural_language_statement:
Let $L,k\in\mathbb N$. Let $E(L,k)$ be the work recurrence for the direct enumeration of all $L$-position masks with exactly $k$ selected bits. It charges recursive invocations, emitted upper masks, and cells copied while appending lower lists. Then

$$E(L,k)\le(4L+1)\binom{L}{k}+1.$$

The statement also covers empty layers with $k>L$. It bounds direct fixed-cardinality enumeration by the number of outputs rather than by the size of the entire Boolean cube.

theorem_title: The rank within a fixed subset layer is injective
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.SubsetAddress.layerRank_injective : ∀ {L k m n : Nat} (hm : ThreeSum.SubsetAddress.IsMask L k m) (hn : ThreeSum.SubsetAddress.IsMask L k n)
  (he : @Eq.{1} Nat (ThreeSum.SubsetAddress.layerRank L k m) (ThreeSum.SubsetAddress.layerRank L k n)), @Eq.{1} Nat m n := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $L,k,m,n$ be natural numbers. Assume $m$ and $n$ encode subsets of $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$ of cardinality $k$; equivalently, both integers are less than $2^L$ and have exactly $k$ set bits. Let $\rho_{L,k}$ denote the recursive rank within this fixed-cardinality layer, with masks lacking the highest bit placed before masks containing it. Then
$$\rho_{L,k}(m)=\rho_{L,k}(n)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad m=n.$$

Thus a layer rank uniquely identifies its valid subset mask, as required for compact subset addressing.

natural_language_statement:
Let $L,k,m\in\mathbb N$. Suppose $m<2^L$ and the binary mask $m$ has exactly $k$ selected positions among its $L$ positions. Let $\rho_{L,k}(m)$ be the construction's zero-based layer rank, defined by recursion on the highest available bit. Then

$$\rho_{L,k}(m)<\binom{L}{k}.$$

This guarantees that compact addresses for masks of a fixed cardinality stay inside the allocated binomial-size layer.

theorem_title: Magnitude bound for every suffix zeta stage
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.SubsetStages.stageValue_abs_le : ∀ {L cut U : Nat} (f : Finset.{0} (Fin L) → Int)
  (hf :
    ∀ (S : Finset.{0} (Fin L)),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@Finset.card.{0} (Fin L) S) cut →
        @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup (f S))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt U))
  (j : Nat),
  @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat j L →
    ∀ (S : Finset.{0} (Fin L)),
      @LE.le.{0} Nat instLENat (@Finset.card.{0} (Fin L) S) cut →
        @LE.le.{0} Int Int.instLEInt
          (@abs.{0} Int instLatticeInt Int.instAddGroup (@ThreeSum.SubsetStages.stageValue L f j S))
          (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt
            (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
              (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
                (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid)))
                (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) j)
              U)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $L,c,U\in\mathbb N$ and let $f$ assign an integer to every subset of $\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$. Suppose $|f(S)|\le U$ for all $|S|\le c$. Let $P_j=\{L-j,\ldots,L-1\}$ for $j\le L$, and define $Z_jf(S)=\sum_{X\subseteq S\cap P_j}f((S\setminus P_j)\cup X)$. Then

$$
\forall j\le L\ \forall S\text{ with }|S|\le c,\qquad |Z_jf(S)|\le2^jU.
$$

This bounds every intermediate suffix-transform value from the original input bound, so intermediate magnitude bounds need not be additional assumptions in the stored-table specification.

theorem_title: The complete fast wanted host has polynomial resource needs
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.ThreeSumFastResources.poly_need : Light.PolyNeed ThreeSum.ThreeSumFastResources.need := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\operatorname{Need}(n,U)$ be the resource specification of the complete wanted-header loader and scan, where $n,U\in\mathbb N$ are input length and magnitude bound. Its fields bound word magnitudes, additional memory cells, and call depth; the latter includes the two outer call levels. There exist natural constants $s,k$ such that

$$\forall n,U,\quad\max\{\operatorname{Need}(n,U).\mathrm{word},\operatorname{Need}(n,U).\mathrm{cells},\operatorname{Need}(n,U).\mathrm{depth}\}\le2^s\bigl((n+1)(U+1)\bigr)^k.$$

This verifies the polynomial resource condition required when translating the fast solver to the benchmark word-RAM specification.

    (And (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i NL) (And (@LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j NR) (@Eq.{1} Nat (right j) (left i)))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $N_L,N_R,M,o,f,i,j$ be natural numbers and let $\ell,\rho:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be key functions satisfying $\ell(a)<M$ for $a<N_L$ and $\rho(b)<M$ for $b<N_R$. $$(i,j)\in P\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad i<N_L\ \land\ j<N_R\ \land\ \rho(j)=\ell(i).$$

This identifies the physical wanted-pair list with the exact equal-key join of the two original index ranges.

theorem_title: The stored bucket join emits no duplicate index pairs
natural_language_statement:
Let $N_L,N_R,M,o,f$ be natural numbers and let $\ell,\rho:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be left and right key functions, with $\ell(a)<M$ for $a<N_L$ and $\rho(b)<M$ for $b<N_R$. Form a list $P$ by visiting each $a<N_L$ and appending $(a,b)$ for every stored right index $b$ in the bucket of key $\ell(a)$. Then
$$P\text{ has no repeated ordered pair}.$$

The conclusion concerns physical source indices, so equal input values or repeated key values do not create duplicate reports of the same index pair.

theorem_title: Pairwise output stores realize a complete wanted-pair row
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.WantedPairs.row_segment : ∀ {μ ν : Nat → Int} {offsets flat NR M i dst previous : Nat} {left right : Nat → Nat}
  (H : ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.Stored μ right NR M offsets flat)
  (hr : ∀ (j : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j NR → @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (right j) M)
  (hi : @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat (left i) M)
  (hout :
    ∀ (t : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat t (ThreeSum.LightHistogram.count right (left i) NR) →
        And
          (@Eq.{1} Int
            (ν
              (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) dst
                (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
                  (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2)))
                  (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) previous t))))
            (@Nat.cast.{0} Int instNatCastInt i))
          (@Eq.{1} Int
            (ν
              (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
                (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) dst
                  (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
                    (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2)))
                    (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) previous t)))
                (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1)))))
            (μ
              (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat)
                (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) flat
                  (ThreeSum.SourceBuckets.offset right NR (left i)))
                t)))),
  Light.Seg ν
    (@HAdd.hAdd.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHAdd.{0} Nat instAddNat) dst
      (@HMul.hMul.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMul.{0} Nat instMulNat)
        (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 2) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 2))) previous))
    (ThreeSum.WantedPairs.cells (ThreeSum.WantedPairs.row μ offsets flat left i)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\ell,r:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be left and right keys, with $r(j)<M$ for $j<N_R$ and $\ell(i)<M$. Suppose memory $\mu$ stores the prescribed right-index buckets at offset-table base $o$ and flat-array base $f$. Write $O(v)=\sum_{u<v}|\{j<N_R:r(j)=u\}|$, let $J_i$ be the stored index list for key $\ell(i)$, and put $c=|J_i|$. For destination base $z$ and previous-pair count $p$, suppose memory $\nu$ satisfies

$$
\bigl(\nu(z+2(p+t)),\nu(z+2(p+t)+1)\bigr)
=\bigl(i,\mu(f+O(\ell(i))+t)\bigr)\quad(t<c).
$$

Then the segment of $2c$ cells starting at $z+2p$ is the flattened list $[(i,j):j\in J_i]$, in bucket order.

This connects the row-copy routine's cell-level output to the semantic list of matching index pairs.
