theorem_title: The position of a Boolean-tagged coordinate is explicit
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.WeightEnumeration.coordinates_idxOf : ∀ {L : Nat} (i : Prod.{0, 0} (Fin L) Bool),
  @Eq.{1} Nat
    (@List.idxOf.{0} (Prod.{0, 0} (Fin L) Bool)
      (@instBEqProd.{0, 0} (Fin L) Bool (@instBEqOfDecidableEq.{0} (Fin L) (instDecidableEqFin L))
        (@instBEqOfDecidableEq.{0} Bool instDecidableEqBool))
      i (ThreeSum.LocalHashMoments.coordinates L))
    (@ThreeSum.WeightEnumeration.coordinateIndex L i) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
For $L\in\mathbb N$, enumerate the coordinates in the order

$$(0,\mathrm{false}),(0,\mathrm{true}),(1,\mathrm{false}),(1,\mathrm{true}),\ldots.$$

For every $a<L$ and Boolean tag $b$, the zero-based first-occurrence index in this list is

$$\operatorname{index}(a,b)=2a+\begin{cases}1,&b=\mathrm{true},\\0,&b=\mathrm{false}.\end{cases}$$

This identifies the coordinate order used by the two coefficient families with the digit positions in the radix representation.

theorem_title: A decoded coordinate is the digit at its first occurrence
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.WeightEnumeration.decode_eq_digit : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq.{u_1 + 1} ι] [inst_1 : NatCast.{u_2} K] (p : Nat) (l : List.{u_1} ι)
  (k : Nat) (i : ι) (hi : @Membership.mem.{u_1, u_1} ι (List.{u_1} ι) (@List.instMembership.{u_1} ι) l i),
  @Eq.{u_2 + 1} K (@ThreeSum.WeightEnumeration.decode.{u_1, u_2} ι K inst inst_1 p l k i hi)
    (@Nat.cast.{u_2} K inst_1
      (@HMod.hMod.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHMod.{0} Nat Nat.instMod)
        (@HDiv.hDiv.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHDiv.{0} Nat Nat.instDiv) k
          (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
            (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) p
            (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHSub.{0} Nat instSubNat)
              (@HSub.hSub.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat (@instHSub.{0} Nat instSubNat) (@List.length.{u_1} ι l)
                (@OfNat.ofNat.{0} Nat (nat_lit 1) (instOfNatNat (nat_lit 1))))
              (@List.idxOf.{u_1} ι (@instBEqOfDecidableEq.{u_1} ι inst) i l))))
        p)) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\iota$ have decidable equality and let $K$ have a specified cast $c:\mathbb N\to K$. Let $l$ be a list of indices, $i\in l$, and let $t$ be the zero-based first-occurrence index of $i$ in $l$. For any natural radix $p$ and natural input $k$, the recursive decoder satisfies

$$D_{p,l}(k)(i)=c\!\left(\operatorname{mod}_{\mathbb N}\!\left(\operatorname{div}_{\mathbb N}(k,p^{|l|-1-t}),p\right)\right).$$

Natural division and remainder use their total conventions, so radix zero is included; no upper bound on $k$ is assumed. This formula connects dependent coordinate assignments to direct digit extraction even when labels repeat.

theorem_title: Ordered Cartesian enumeration equals radix decoding
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.WeightEnumeration.pi_eq_range : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} {K : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq.{u_1 + 1} ι] [inst_1 : NatCast.{u_2} K] (p : Nat)
  (l : List.{u_1} ι),
  @Eq.{max (u_1 + 1) (u_2 + 1)}
    (List.{max u_1 u_2} ((i : ι) → @Membership.mem.{u_1, u_1} ι (List.{u_1} ι) (@List.instMembership.{u_1} ι) l i → K))
    (@List.pi.{u_1, u_2} ι inst (fun (x : ι) => K) l fun (x : ι) =>
      @List.map.{0, u_2} Nat K (fun (n : Nat) => @Nat.cast.{u_2} K inst_1 n) (List.range p))
    (@List.map.{0, max u_1 u_2} Nat
      ((i : ι) → @Membership.mem.{u_1, u_1} ι (List.{u_1} ι) (@List.instMembership.{u_1} ι) l i → K)
      (@ThreeSum.WeightEnumeration.decode.{u_1, u_2} ι K inst inst_1 p l)
      (List.range
        (@HPow.hPow.{0, 0, 0} Nat Nat Nat
          (@instHPow.{0, 0} Nat Nat (@NPow.toPow.{0} Nat (@Monoid.toNPow.{0} Nat Nat.instMonoid))) p
          (@List.length.{u_1} ι l)))) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $\iota$ be an index type with decidable equality, and let $K$ carry a specified natural-number cast $c:\mathbb N\to K$. Let $p\in\mathbb N$ and let $l$ be a finite list of indices. Form the ordered Cartesian-product list $\Pi_l$ by choosing each coordinate from $[c(0),\ldots,c(p-1)]$, with the first list position varying most slowly. Let $D_{p,l}(k)$ be the recursive decoder that reads the most significant digit first; repeated labels use their first occurrence. Then

$$\Pi_l=\bigl[D_{p,l}(0),D_{p,l}(1),\ldots,D_{p,l}(p^{|l|}-1)\bigr].$$

This is equality of lists, including their order and repetitions. It identifies the original coefficient enumeration with concrete radix indices without assuming distinct labels or an injective cast.

theorem_title: The weighted modular score equals the final correction remainder
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum.WeightedScore.score_eq_remaining : ∀ (primes : Nat → Nat) (s q nA nB nC : Nat) (a b c : Nat → Int)
  (hprime : ∀ (i : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i s → Nat.Prime (primes i))
  (hinj :
    ∀ (i : Nat),
      @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat i s →
        ∀ (j : Nat), @LT.lt.{0} Nat instLTNat j s → @Eq.{1} Nat (primes i) (primes j) → @Eq.{1} Nat i j),
  @Eq.{1} Nat (ThreeSum.WeightedScore.score primes s q nA nB nC a b c)
    (ThreeSum.WeightedScore.remaining primes s q nA nB nC a b c s) := by
  sorry
natural_language_statement:
Let $a,b,c:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$ have specified lengths $n_A,n_B,n_C$, and let $p_0,\ldots,p_{s-1}$ be pairwise distinct natural primes. Let $N_m$ count index triples in these lengths for which $m\mid c_k-b_j-a_i$. Define $J(q,p)=q$ if $p\mid q$, and $J(q,p)=qp$ otherwise. The weighted score counts each triple divisible by $q$ with weight equal to the number of auxiliary primes that do not divide its difference. For any $q\in\mathbb N$,

$$
\operatorname{score}=sN_q-\sum_{j=0}^{s-1}N_{J(q,p_j)}
=\operatorname{remaining}(s).
$$

Subtraction is the natural-number subtraction of the defined correction accumulator. This matches the score specification with the array-ordered correction computation, including shared factors with $q$.
